impact_on_system: When multiple links or local and remote coexistent neighbors are configured for an LDP session, if the link parameters are inconsistent, the link cannot be added to the session. As a result, multiple links cannot be created as expected.
possible_causes: When LDP sessions are configured with multiple links or local-remote adjacencies, link parameters may be inconsistent.
procedure: 1. If ConfigType in the alarm information is Keepalive Hold Timer, check whether the keepalive-hold timer configurations in the session's interface or remote-peer views are consistent. If they are inconsistent, modify the keepalive-hold timer configurations in the interface or remote-peer views to make the configurations consistent. Then, go to Step 5. If they are the same, go to Step 6. 2. If ConfigType in the alarm information is Transport Address, check whether the transport-address configurations in the session's interface views are consistent. If they are inconsistent, modify the transport-address configurations in the interface views to make them consistent. Then, go to Step 5. If they are the same, go to Step 6. 3. If ConfigType in the alarm information is Label Advertisement Mode, check whether the advertisement configurations in the session's interface or remote-peer views are consistent.
parameters: VrfName::VRF name of LDP session exists. | PeerLsrId::LDP session ID. | LocalLsrId::Local LSR ID. | ConfigIfName::Configure the current interface name. | ConfigRmtPeerIp::Configure the IP address of the remote session. | ConfigType::Configuration inconsistent type. | EffectKa::KeepAlive value used by the LDP session. | EffectTa::LDP transport addresses used by the session. | EffectLam::Peer use label advertisement mode.

Cause 7: The VPLS PW is carried over a BGP over SLSP over GRE tunnel, and the signaling protocol status of the VPLS PW is up. Cause 8: The VPLS PW is carried over a TE over GRE tunnel, and the signaling protocol status of the VPLS PW is up. Cause 9: The VPLS PW is carried over a SR-POLICY tunnel, and the signaling protocol status of the VPLS PW is up. Cause 10: The VPLS PW is carried over a BGP over SR-POLICY tunnel, and the signaling protocol status of the VPLS PW is up. Cause 12: The VPLS PW is carried over a SR-MPLS TE over GRE tunnel, and the signaling protocol status of the VPLS PW is up. If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step 2. 2.Check and ensure that the IMA group attributes for the local and peer devices are correct. The IMA group attributes include the IMA version, IMA transmit frame length, and IMA group configuration mode. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 5. If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step 3. 3.Check on the NMS the IMA group status of the local and peer devices to determine whether the IMA group negotiation is successful. If the IMA group status of the local or peer device is not Operational, the negotiation fails. Deactivate and then activate the IMA group. Check whether the alarm is cleared.

description: The loop is detected on this interface. (Interface=[IfName], VlanId=[VlanId], Vsi=[vsi_name]) A loop was detected on an interface. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Cause 1: A loop was detected on the interface that has proactive loop detection enabled after it went Up. The interface was then blocked. The interface was blocked. Cause 2: A loop was detected on the interface that has proactive loop detection enabled after it went Up. A loop was detected on the interface.
possible_causes: Cause 1: A loop was detected on the interface that has proactive loop detection enabled after it went Up. The interface was then blocked. Cause 2: A loop was detected on the interface that has proactive loop detection enabled after it went Up.
procedure: Cause 1: A loop was detected on the interface that has proactive loop detection enabled after it went Up. The interface was then blocked. 1. Run the display loop-detect trigger trigger-down all command to check whether any interface is triggered to go Down. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 4. 2. Check whether a loop occurs on the interface. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 4. 3. After the loop is eliminated, run the reset loop-detect trigger trigger-down command to unblock the interface, and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 2: A loop was detected on the interface that has proactive loop detection enabled after it went Up. 1. Run the display loop-detect trigger loop all command to check whether loops are detected on an interface. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 3. 2. Check the cable connection of the interface and whether a loop occurs on the downstream Layer 2 network. If so, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End.
parameters: IfName::Name of the interface. | VlanId::Indicates a VLAN ID. The value is meaningless. Generally, the value is 0. | vsi_name::Indicates a VSI name. description: The TCP connection of RBS was torn down. (RBS name=[RbsName], Down reason=[RbsDownReason]) The TCP connection of the RBS was turn down.
impact_on_system: The RBS cannot perform data backup.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The RBS closed the TCP connection. Cause 2: The RBS's heartbeat timed out. Cause 3: The peer end tore down the TCP connection. Cause 4: Other unknown reasons caused the TCP connection to be torn down. Cause 5: The RBS flow control takes a long time.
procedure: Cause 1: The RBS closed the TCP connection. 1. Run the display this command in the RBS view to check whether the shutdown configuration exists. If yes, go to Step 6. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display remote-backup-service command on two devices that back up each other to check RBS information. The local IP address of the local device must be the same as the peer IP address of the backup device. The peer IP address of the local device must be the same as the local IP address of the backup device. The port numbers configured for the TCP connection on the two devices that back up each other must be the same. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Run the peer source port command to reconfigure TCP connection parameters for the RBS. 4. Run the ping command to check whether the peer device is reachable. 5. Collect the alarm, log, and configuration information and contact Huawei technical support. 6. End. Cause 2: The RBS's heartbeat timed out. The same as Cause 1. Cause 3: The peer end tore down the TCP connection. The same as Cause 1. Cause 4: Other unknown reasons caused the TCP connection to be torn down. The same as Cause 1. Cause 5: The RBS flow control takes a long time. The same as Cause 1.
parameters: RbsName::Name of the RBS | RbsDownReason::Reason that the TCP connection of the RBS was torn down

procedure: Cause 1: Interface physical link is down 1. Run the display interface brief [ <interface-type1> ]  [ main ] command to check whether the interface is shut down. If yes, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 3. 2. Run the undo shutdown command and enable the interface and check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 2: The DHCP server on the network cannot normally assign IP addresses. 1. Run the display dhcp server statistics error command in the diagnostic view to check statistics about invalid packets on the DHCP server. Then check whether error information about the DHCP server exists. If error information about the DHCP server exists, locate and rectify the fault based on the error type in the command output. If no error information about the DHCP server exists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support engineers. 3. End. Cause 3: The configuration of DHCP client is not correct 1. Check whether the DHCP client function is enabled. If yes, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. description: System rollback. (FileName=[SoftwareName], Version=[Version], Reason=[FailReason]) The system fails to start , and the software rolls back to the old version. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Cause 1: Rollback occurs on the system. The system software supports only the service features of the current version after the startup succeeds. Cause 2: The system starts from the backup area After the system software is started from the backup area, the user cannot add or delete files on the backup area, and cannot set the next startup package as a file on the backup area
possible_causes: Cause 1: Rollback occurs on the system. Cause 2: The system starts from the backup area
procedure: Cause 1: Rollback occurs on the system. 1. Run the dir command to check the file system. If the storage medium is unavailable, the storage medium is damaged. Go to step 2. If the storage medium is available, system software is faulty and cannot start the system. Go to step 3. 2. Check the storage medium saved in the system software. If the storage medium is an SD card or a USB disk, replace it and restart the upgrade. If the upgrade fails, go to step 3. If the storage medium is flash, record the device type and number, collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 3. Collect operation results, alarm information, and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 2: The system starts from the backup area 1. Run the display startup command in the user view to view information about the system software and configuration files started by the current device. The display shows that the storage path of the system software or configuration file used for this startup is the backup area, indicating that the system starts from the backup area. . 2. After starting from the standby area, the user cannot select the files in the standby area to set the next startup. Please format the root directory of the main area. After the main area is repaired, copy the system software to the main area directory and perform the upgrade. If the upgrade still fails, go to step 3 3. Collect operation results, alarm information, and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel.

description: Traffic fall alarm in the receive direction of an Ethernet interface. (hwPhysicalPortIfIndex=[hwPhysicalPortIfIndex],hwPhysicalPortName=[hwPhysicalPortName],hwBandwidthLast=[hwBandwidthLast] bits/sec,hwBandwidthCurrent=[hwBandwidthCurrent] bits/sec) Traffic fall alarm in the receive direction of an Ethernet interface.
impact_on_system: If the alarm exists, the traffic decreases sharply.
possible_causes: This alarm is reported when the following conditions are met: 1. The interface goes up. 2. The rate change of the current period ((Rate in the previous period - Rate in the current period)/Rate in the previous period) exceeds the specified threshold. (The rate in the current period is 5 minutes by default and configurable using the flow-change fall interval command. The threshold is 99% by default and configurable using the flow-change fall command.) 3. The initial bandwidth usage threshold is reached (20% by default; configurable using the flow-change fall start-check bandwidth-ratio command).
procedure: 1. Check whether the port status is down. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Check whether the alarm clearing time (5 minutes by default, which can be configured using the flow-change fall remain-time command) is exceeded. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Check whether the reset flow-change fall command is run in the system view to clear the sudden traffic decrease alarm on all interfaces.
parameters: hwPhysicalPortIfIndex::Index of physical port. | hwPhysicalPortName::Name of physical port. | hwBandwidthLast::Indicates the average rate in the previous interval, in bit/s. | hwBandwidthCurrent::Indicates the average rate in the current interval, in bit/s.

procedure: Cause 1: 1. Check the networking diagram and physical link connections to see whether a loop exists on the network. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 3. 2. Adjust the networking diagram and physical link connections to clear loops on the network. Wait for 1 minute and check whether the alarm is generated again. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 4.

procedure: Cause 1: 1. Run the display this command in the interface view to check whether the parameter settings of the peer interface are the same as those of the local interface. If they are consistent, go to Step 3. If they are inconsistent, go to Step 2. 2. Modify the configurations to ensure that the parameters of the two interfaces are consistent. description: APS reported an alarm about the mismatch of the working and protection paths. (PwApsId=[PwApsId], PWID=[PWID], PWTYPE=[PWTYPE], PWPeerIp=[PWPeerIp], PwIndex=[PwIndex]) Information about the working and protection paths in the APS packet sent from the remote end was inconsistent with that on the local end.

procedure: The troubleshooting procedure is as follows: 1. Run the display this command on the AC (sub-)interface of the CSG to view the PW state (primary or secondary) and on the AC (sub-)interface of the RSG to view the PW state (primary or backup) to check if the configurations on the two ends of each PW match. If the configurations match, go to Step 3. If the configurations do not match, go to Step 2. 2. Reconfigure the primary, secondary, and bypass PWs on the CSG and RSG and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3.

procedure: 1. Check whether the CC function is enabled for the MEG at the source and sink ends. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display interface command and check whether a physical interface bound to services is shut down.

(2). Run the reset saved-configuration command to clear the configuration file for next startup. (3). Run the startup saved-configuration command to update the configuration file for next startup. If the clearance fails, go to step 2.

If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2.On the NMS, check whether the laser on the corresponding LPU of the remote device is shut down. If the laser is shut down, switch on the laser and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3.On the NMS, check whether the transmit optical power of the remote device is correct. description: The board does not support this function. (SlotID=[SlotID], ReasonID=[ReasonID], ReasonDescription=[ReasonDescription]) The board does not support this function.
impact_on_system: Cause 1: The board does not support SRv6 SRH compression. For boards that do not support SRv6 SRH compression, traffic cannot be forwarded based on SRv6 SRH compression. Cause 2: The board does not support SRv6-TE FRR Trust Domain Verification. Traffic can be properly forwarded, but SRv6 TE FRR trusted-domain verification is not supported. Cause 3: The board in the current slot does not support the function of configuring the TCP MSS value in the outbound direction of the MGRE tunnel. Traffic forwarding is not affected. For boards that do not support the configuration, the MSS value of packets encapsulated in the MGRE tunnel cannot be adjusted. Cause 4: The board in the current slot does not support the function of configuring the TCP MSS value in the inbound direction of the MGRE tunnel. Traffic forwarding is not affected. For boards that do not support the configuration, the MSS value of packets encapsulated in the MGRE tunnel cannot be adjusted. Cause 5: The board in the current slot does not support the function of configuring the outbound TCP MSS value for the GRE tunnel. Traffic forwarding is not affected. For boards that do not support the configuration, the MSS value of packets encapsulated by the GRE tunnel cannot be adjusted. Cause 6: The board in the current slot does not support passive ND learning. Traffic forwarding is not affected. Passive ND learning does not take effect on boards that do not support it.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The board does not support SRv6 SRH compression. Cause 2: The board does not support SRv6-TE FRR Trust Domain Verification. Cause 3: The board in the current slot does not support the function of configuring the TCP MSS value in the outbound direction of the MGRE tunnel. Cause 4: The board in the current slot does not support the function of configuring the TCP MSS value in the inbound direction of the MGRE tunnel. Cause 5: The board in the current slot does not support the function of configuring the outbound TCP MSS value for the GRE tunnel. Cause 6: The board in the current slot does not support passive ND learning.
procedure: Cause 1: The board does not support SRv6 SRH compression. 1. Run the display version command in any view to check whether a board that does not support SRv6 SRH compression exists on the device. If so, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Replace the board that does not support SRv6 SRH compression with a board that supports SRv6 SRH compression. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 2: The board does not support SRv6-TE FRR Trust Domain Verification. 1. Run the display version command in any view to check whether a board that does not support SRv6 TE FRR trusted-domain verification exists on the device. If so, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Replace the board that does not support SRv6 TE FRR trusted-domain verification with a board that supports SRv6 TE FRR trusted-domain verification. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 3: The board in the current slot does not support the function of configuring the TCP MSS value in the outbound direction of the MGRE tunnel. 1. Run the display version command in any view to check whether a board that does not support the configuration of the TCP MSS value in the outbound direction of the MGRE tunnel exists on the device. If so, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Replace the board that does not support the configuration of the TCP MSS value in the outbound direction of the MGRE tunnel with a board that supports the configuration of the TCP MSS value in the outbound direction of the MGRE tunnel. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 4: The board in the current slot does not support the function of configuring the TCP MSS value in the inbound direction of the MGRE tunnel. 1. Run the display version command in any view to check whether there are boards that do not support the configuration of the TCP MSS value in the inbound direction of the MGRE tunnel. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Replace the board that does not support the specified configuration with a board that supports the configuration of the inbound TCP MSS value for the MGRE tunnel. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 5: The board in the current slot does not support the function of configuring the outbound TCP MSS value for the GRE tunnel. 1. Run the display version command in any view to check whether there is any board that does not support the configuration of the TCP MSS value in the outbound direction of the GRE tunnel. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Replace the board that does not support the specified configuration with a board that supports the configuration of the TCP MSS value in the outbound direction of the GRE tunnel. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 4. End. Cause 6: The board in the current slot does not support passive ND learning. 1. Run the display version command in any view to check whether a board that does not support passive ND learning exists on the device. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 3. 2. Replace the board that does not support passive ND learning with a board that supports passive ND learning. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 4. End.

description: The number of IPv6 prefixes in the VPN instance exceeded the maximum value. (VpnInstanceName=[VpnInstanceName], PrefixCount=[PrefixCount], MaxValue=[MaxValue]) The number of IPv6 route prefixes in a VPN instance exceeded the maximum number that is allowed.
impact_on_system: If more IPv6 routes are added, they will be discarded. As a result, traffic may be interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause1: A large number of IPv6 routes were added to the routing table. Cause2: The maximum number of IPv6 route prefixes in the VPN instance was reduced.
procedure: 1. Run the display ipv6 routing-table vpn-instance <vpn-instance-name> statistics command to check the total number of VPN route prefixes and the number of routes that each protocol has added to the IPv6 routing table. Run the display ipv6 routing-table limit command to check the total number of existing VPN route prefixes and the configured limit on the number of route prefixes. Then check whether the number of configured VPN route prefixes exceeds the maximum value. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Run the prefix limit <number> { alert-percent | simply-alert } command to reconfigure the maximum number of route prefixes or delete unnecessary VPN routes. Then, check whether the alarm persists. If yes, go to Step 3. If no, go to Step 4. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support.

description: Some HQoS functions on the port do not take effect. (ServiceType=[service-type],Slot=[slot-id],Interface=[interface-name],Reason=[reason-id],ReasonDescription=[reason-description]) HQoS did not take effect on the interface.
impact_on_system: Cause 1: Resources for the enhanced 8-CoS mode are not planned or the number of planned resources is insufficient. The 8-CoS port-queue CIR function does not take effect on the interface where the alarm is generated. Cause 3: The number of configured trunk interfaces whose scheduling trees are in merge mode exceeds the upper limit. No scheduling tree is created for the excess trunk interfaces, and traffic fails to be forwarded. Cause 4: The number of trunk interfaces that contain FlexE member interfaces exceeded the upper limit. The maximum number of trunk interfaces that contain FlexE member interfaces is 32. If more than 32 trunk interfaces contain FlexE member interfaces, traffic fails to be forwarded.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Resources for the enhanced 8-CoS mode are not planned or the number of planned resources is insufficient. Cause 3: The number of configured trunk interfaces whose scheduling trees are in merge mode exceeds the upper limit. Cause 4: The number of trunk interfaces that contain FlexE member interfaces exceeded the upper limit.
procedure: Cause 1: Resources for the enhanced 8-CoS mode are not planned or the number of planned resources is insufficient. 1. Run the display qos resource user-queue command to check whether the number of remaining resources displayed in the free field is 0 and whether there are interfaces that have not applied for resources in enhanced 8-CoS mode. If yes, change the number of CIRs configured for port queues on the current interface to be smaller than or equal to the specification supported by the board, or run the qos user-queue resource 8cos-enhance command to apply for resources for the enhanced 8-CoS mode for the interface, and then go to step 2. If no, go to step 3. 2. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to step 4. If no, go to step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 3: The number of configured trunk interfaces whose scheduling trees are in merge mode exceeds the upper limit. 1. Run the display current-configuration | section include qos schedule-tree merge-mode command to check whether the number of trunk interfaces whose scheduling trees are in merge mode exceeds the maximum value. If so, run the undo qos schedule-tree merge-mode outbound command to configure the scheduling trees of some trunk interfaces to work in distribute mode, or run the undo interface command to delete some trunk interfaces whose scheduling trees are in merge mode so that the number of trunk interfaces whose scheduling trees are in merge mode does not exceed the maximum value. Then, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 4: The number of trunk interfaces that contain FlexE member interfaces exceeded the upper limit. 1. Run the display current-configuration interface command in the system view to check whether the number of trunk interfaces that contain FlexE member interfaces in the slot where the alarm is generated exceeds 32. If yes, migrate services on some trunk interfaces that contain FlexE member interfaces to other devices and delete the corresponding trunk interfaces. Ensure that the number of trunk interfaces that contain FlexE member interfaces does not exceed 32. Then, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End.
parameters: service-type::Service type. | slot-id::Slot ID. | interface-name::Interface name | reason-id::ID of the alarm cause. | reason-description::Alarm cause description.

description: The number of routes received from the BGP peer exceeded the alarm threshold. (InstanceId=[InstanceId], Afi=[AddrFamilyAfi], Safi=[AddrFamilySafi], LocalIfName=[LocalIfName], PeerRemoteAddrType=[PeerIPAddrType], PeerRemoteAddr=[PeerIPAddr], MaxRouteNumber=[RouteLimitNum], AlarmThreshold=[RouteLimitThreshold]) The route-limit threshold command is run, and the number of routes received from a BGP unnumbered peer exceeds the alarm threshold.
impact_on_system: 1) If the alarm threshold is set to 100% and the alert-only parameter is not configured for a peer, the peer relationship is torn down and all routes received by the peer are deleted. 2) This command does not affect the neighbors that are configured with other parameters.
possible_causes: The number of routes received from the BGP unnumbered peer who configed with route-limit, exceeds the alarm threshold.
procedure: 1. Run the display bgp vpnv4 vpn-instance unnumbered peer verbose command to check whether the number of routes received from the peer exceeds the maximum number of routes configured for the peer multiplied by the alarm threshold (%). (1) If yes, go to Step 2. (2) If no, go to Step 9. 2. Check whether all the routes received from the peer are necessary. (1) If yes, go to Step 8. (2) If no, go to Step 3. 3. View user logs to check whether too many unnecessary routes are received because the local import policy, such as peer route-policy/ip-prefix/filter-policy, has been modified. (1) If yes, go to Step 4. (2) If no, go to Step 5. 4. Update the local import policy, such as peer route-policy/ip-prefix/filter-policy, to reject unnecessary routes. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 10. 5. Contact the maintenance personnel of the peer device to check whether all the routes advertised to the local end are necessary. (1) If yes, go to Step 6. (2) If no, go to Step 7. 6. Ask the maintenance personnel of the peer device to reduce the number of routes that can be advertised to the local end through route summarization and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 10. 7. Ask the maintenance personnel of the peer device to modify the import or export policy so that unnecessary routes are withdrawn and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 10. 8. Increase the maximum number of routes that can be accepted from the peer and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 10. 9. Please contact technical support. 10. End.

description: MEP enters LCK defect condition. (MdIndex=[MdIndex], MaIndex=[MaIndex], MdName=[MdName], MaName=[MaName], MepId=[MepId]) A MEP enterd the LCK faulty state.

procedure: 1. Check whether the mep mep-id <mep-id> lck enable level <level-value> command is run on a MEP in an inner MA. If this command is run, check whether the specified level is the same as the level of the MD to which the MEP generating the alarm belongs. If the levels match, go to 2. If the levels do not match, go to 3. 2. Run the undo mep mep-id <mep-id> lck enable command to disable the Ethernet lock (ETH-LCK) function on the MEP. 3. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 4. End.
parameters: MdIndex::Index of an MD | MaIndex::Index of an MA | MdName::Name of an MD | MaName::Name of an MA | MepId::MEP ID

If the fault persists, go to Step 5.

Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 4. End. 1. description: The result of two-way delay-measure exceeded the threshold. (MdIndex=[MdIndex], MaIndex=[MaIndex], RemoteMacAddress=[RemoteMacAddress], Timestamp=[Timestamp], DelayValue=[DelayValue], ThresholdValue=[ThresholdValue], DelayValueHigh=[DelayValueHigh], DelayValueLow=[DelayValueLow]) In the VLAN networking where two-way frame delay measurement was configured and the expected alarm threshold was set, if the network delay exceeded the set alarm threshold, an alarm was generated.
impact_on_system: Services will not be affected.
possible_causes: The device was enabled with two-way frame delay measurement and was configured with an alarm threshold, and the delay in bidirectional frame transmission exceeded the alarm threshold.

If there is no such a long delay, go to Step 3. 2. Troubleshoot the fault of a long delay. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel.

parameters: IfIndex::Interface index | hwIfMonitorOutputRatePercentage::Output traffic statistics. | hwIfMonitorOutputRateThreshold::Alarm threshold for outgoing traffic. | InterfaceName::Interface name.

If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3.Check whether the negotiation parameters at the local and peer ends are consistent, such as delay, the minimum number of activated links, and the number of link timeslots. description: The Xsec service is abnormal. (Slot=[slotId], Engine=[engineId], Reason=[reasonDetail], ReasonCode=[reasonID]) The Xsec service was abnormal. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Cause 1: The slot is abnormal. The Xsec service deployed on the board will be abnormal. Cause 2: The engine is abnormal. The Xsec service deployed on the board engine will be abnormal. Cause 3: Rebuild xsec sa by cli "reset xsec sa". The Xsec service will be interrupted for a period of time and then recover. Cause 4: The remote Xsec service is abnormal. The Xsec service will be abnormal.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The slot is abnormal. Cause 2: The engine is abnormal. Cause 3: Rebuild xsec sa by cli "reset xsec sa". Cause 4: The remote Xsec service is abnormal.
procedure: Cause 1: The slot is abnormal. 1. Run the display device command to check whether the status of the board in the slot specified by the hwXsecSlotID field is normal. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Run the display board-reset command to check the board restart time. If the alarm is generated during device restart, the alarm is caused by the board restart. Locate the fault based on the board restart cause. If the alarm is not generated during device restart, go to Step 4. 3. Run the power on or reset slot command to restore the board. After the board is restored, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 4. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 5. 4. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 5. End. Cause 2: The engine is abnormal. 1. Run the display board-reset command to check the engine fault cause and engine fault time. If the alarm is generated when the engine is faulty, the alarm is caused by the engine fault. Locate the fault based on the engine fault cause. If the alarm is not generated when the engine is faulty, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 3. End. Cause 3: Rebuild xsec sa by cli "reset xsec sa". The user runs the reset xsec sa command to re-establish services. This message is informational only, and no action is required. Cause 4: The remote Xsec service is abnormal. 1. Obtain the router ID of the peer end of the Xsec service based on the RemoteRouterId field in the alarm information. 2. On the peer end of the Xsec service that is connected to the local device, run the display current-configuration command to check whether there is an Xsec configuration with the router ID the same as the value of RemoteRouterId. If yes, the device is the one that is connected to the local device. Go to Step 3. If no, the device is not the peer device that is connected to the local device. Search for other devices. 3. On the faulty peer device, run the display alarm active command to rectify the fault based on the alarm information. 4. End.
parameters: slotId::Slot ID | engineId::Engine ID | reasonDetail::Reason list | reasonID::Reason code

Cause 2: The MPLS tunnel is congested on the service layer and the service layer is interrupted so that an AIS PDU is sent to notify the client layer.
procedure: 1. Run the display interface command to check whether any physical interface connected to the MPLS tunnel is shut down. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 4. 2. Run the undo shutdown command to enable the physical interface. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 3. 3. If all configurations are correct, the MPLS tunnel is congested. Then go to Step 4.

description: Users failed to login telnet server too frequently. (failed times=[hwUserInfoLoginFailedTimes], statistic period=[hwUserInfoStatisticPeriod] minutes) The number of login failures of telnet server during a specified period exceeded the threshold.

procedure: 1. By default, an alarm is generated if the number of login failures reaches 30 within 5 minutes and is cleared if the number of login failures falls below 20 within the same period. 2. Contact the administrator to obtain the correct Telnet user name and password and log in to the device again. After the login is successful, the alarm is cleared after a measurement period. 3. Run the display current-configuration configuration telnet include-default | include login-failed command to check the threshold of the number of Telnet server login failures during a specified period. Run the telnet server login-failed threshold-alarm command to set the alarm clearance threshold of the number of Telnet server login failures during a specified period (in minutes). After a measurement period, the alarm is cleared.

Locate the device where the conflicting IP address resides based on the upstream and downstream IP addresses of the conflicting IP address, and change the conflicting IP address. (The alarm will be cleared 24 hours later.) 4. End.

Cause 3: ND table used number trend predict over threshold 80%. If the current situation persists, users may fail to go online. Cause 4: ND prefix table used number trend predict over threshold 80%. Check the ARP resource usage and services. You can run the display arp all command to check ARP entry information on the device and run the display arp statistics slot <slot-id> command to check ARP entry statistics on a specified board. Cause 3: ND table used number trend predict over threshold 80%. Check the usage of ND entries and services. You can run the display ipv6 neighbors statistics slot <slot-id> command to check the usage of ND entries on a specified board. Cause 4: ND prefix table used number trend predict over threshold 80%. Check the usage of the ND prefix table and services. You can run the display ipv6-nd <slot-id> statistics command to check the usage of the ND prefix table on a specified board.

description: Static LSP went Down. (LspIndex=[LspIndex], InSegmentIndex=[InSegmentIndex], OutSegmentIndex=[OutSegmentIndex], OutIfIndex=[OutIfIndex], LspName=[LspName], LspStatus=[LspStatus], OutIfName=[OutIfName], InIfIndex=[InIfIndex], InIfName=[InIfName], ReasonIndex=[ReasonIndex], Reason=[Reason]) Static LSP went Down.
impact_on_system: If a service uses the corresponding static LSP to take traffic, traffic will be interrupted. If no service uses the corresponding static LSP, there is no impact.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Others Cause 2: MPLS disabled on an interface Cause 3: Route change Cause 4: Inbound interface Down Cause 5: Outbound interface Down Cause 6: Static LSP configuration update
procedure: Cause 1: Others 1. Run the display mpls interface command. If the trap is generated on the ingress of static LSPs, you need to check the information about only the outbound interface; if the trap is generated on the egress of static LSPs, you need to check the information about only the inbound interface; if the trap is generated on the transit of static LSPs, you need to check the information about the outbound interface and inbound interface. You need to check whether the corresponding interface is displayed in the command output, whether the Status field of the interface is Up. If the interface is not Up, check and correct the interface configuration. Then go to Step 2. If the interface information is not displayed, MPLS is disabled on the interface. Enable MPLS on the interface and go to Step 2. 2.Run the display ip routing-table <ip-address> command on the ingress to check whether a valid route to the next-hop IP address exists. If such a route exists, go to Step 3. If such a route does not exist, check and correct the route configuration to ensure the next-hop IP address is reachable. Then go to Step 4. 3.Run the display mpls lsp command on the ingress to check whether dynamic LSPs with the same prefix as the static LSP are configured. If such an LSP exists, block it and go to Step 4. If such an LSP does not exist, go to Step 5. 4.Check whether this trap message is cleared. If the trap message is cleared, go to Step 6. If the trap message persists, go to Step 5. 5.Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 6.End. Cause 2: MPLS disabled on an interface The same as Cause 1. Cause 3: Route change The same as Cause 1. Cause 4: Inbound interface Down The same as Cause 1. Cause 5: Outbound interface Down The same as Cause 1. Cause 6: Static LSP configuration update The same as Cause 1.
parameters: LspIndex::Indicates the index of the LSP. | InSegmentIndex::Indicates the inSegment index of a static LSP. | OutSegmentIndex::Indicates the outbound interface index of a static LSP. | OutIfIndex::Indicates the outbound interface index of a static LSP. | LspName::Indicates the name of a static LSP. | LspStatus::Indicates the status of a static LSP. | OutIfName::Indicates the outbound interface name of a static LSP. | InIfIndex::Indicates the inbound interface index of a static LSP. | InIfName::Indicates the inbound interface name a static LSP. | ReasonIndex::Indicates the reason that the static LSP down. | Reason::Alarm cause.

Run the display interface <interface-type interface-num> command based on the obtained interface name. View the value of the current state field. If the value of the current state field is Up, go to Step 2. If the value of the current state field is not Up, go to Step 6. 2. Run the display cfm mep [ md <md-name> [ ma <ma-name> [ mep-id <mep-id> ] ] ] command to check the value of CCM Send. Check whether the RMEP is enabled to send CCMs. If the value of the CCM Send field is enabled, go to Step 4. If the value of the CCM Send field is disabled, go to Step 3. 3. Perform the following operations: a. Run the cfm md <md-name> command to enter the MD view. b. Run the ma <ma-name> command to enter the MA view. c. Run the mep ccm-send enable command to enable the RMEP to send CCMs. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 4. 4. Run the display cfm remote-mep [ md <md-name> ma <ma-name> mep-id <mep-id> ] command to check the value of CCM Receive. If the value of the CCM Receive field is enabled, go to Step 8. If the value of the CCM Receive field is disabled, go to Step 5. 5. Perform the following operations: a. Run the cfm md <md-name> command to enter the MD view. b. Run the ma <ma-name> command to enter the MA view. c. Run the remote-mep ccm-receive enable command to enable the MEP to receive CCMs. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 8. 6. Run the display this command in the interface view to check whether the interfaces at both ends are shut down. If the interfaces at both ends are sub-interfaces, check whether VLAN IDs are configured for the interfaces. If the interface is shut down, run the undo shutdown command to enable the interface. If the interfaces are sub-interfaces, run the vlan-type dot1q command to configure correct VLAN IDs on the sub-interfaces, and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 7. If the interface is not shut down, go to step 7. 7. Check whether the physical connection is normal (for example, whether the Ethernet cable or optical module is loose or disconnected). If the physical link is abnormal, reconnect the physical link, and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 8. If the physical link works properly, go to Step 8. 8. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: MdName::MD Name | MaName::MA Name | MepId::MEP ID | RmepId::RMEP ID | MdIndex::MD Index | MaIndex::MA Index

description: The local device detected that the instance ID was mismatched with that of a neighboring device. (SysInstance=[hwisisSysInstance], InterfaceId=[ifIndex], InterfaceName=[ifName], AdjacencySysID=[hwIsisAdjSysID], AdjacencySysInstance=[hwIsisAdjSysInstance]) This alarm is reported when the IS-IS process IDs are inconsistent.
impact_on_system: The process ID of the local device is different from that of the neighbor, and the two IS-IS processes may incorrectly interwork, causing a possible routing loop.
possible_causes: The local device detected that the instance ID was mismatched with that of a neighboring device.
procedure: 1. Locate the neighbor whose IS-IS process ID is different from the local IS-IS process ID based on the alarm information. 2. Check whether the process ID inconsistency between the local device and the neighbor meets network plan requirements. If no, re-plan the neighbor relationships and IS-IS process IDs on the network and ensure that the IS-IS process IDs of the local device and its neighbor are the same. If yes, run the undo instance-id consistency detect enable command to disable IS-IS process ID consistency check. 3. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If no, collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. If yes, no further action is required.
parameters: hwisisSysInstance::ID of an IS-IS process. | ifIndex::Interface index. | ifName::Interface name. | hwIsisAdjSysID::Neighbor system ID. | hwIsisAdjSysInstance::Neighbor process ID.

description: The status of the PWE3 VC turned DOWN. (VcId=[VcId], VcType=[VcType], PeerAddress=[PeerAddress], InterfaceIndex=[InterfaceIndex], VcInboundLabel=[VcInboundLabel], VcOutboundLabel=[VcOutboundLabel], SecondaryPw=[SecondaryPw], HWL2VpnStateChangeReason=[HWL2VpnStateChangeReason], SysUpTime=[SysUpTime], InterfaceName=[InterfaceName], SwitchVcId=[SwitchVcId], TunnelPolicyName=[TunnelPolicyName]) Indicates that a VC of the PWE3 goes Down.
impact_on_system: The PWE3 service is interrupted and traffic is blocked.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Invalid reason type. Cause 3: Local VC Deleted. Cause 4: LDP Session Down. Cause 6: Same LDP mapping was received with different label and MTU. Cause 8: LDP mapping was received with mismatching interface parameters. Cause 12: New LDP mapping message was received but remote VC or local VC is Down. Cause 13: LDP Withdrawn Received. Cause 14: LDP release message was received. Cause 19: Interface Down. Cause 20: Encapsulation changed. Cause 24: Tunnel was Down. Cause 31: LDP Notification Not-Forwarding. Cause 32: PW was recreated. Cause 41: Local PSN Fault. Cause 43: BFD for pw status changed to Down. Cause 47: Manual set was enabled. Cause 60: MTU Unmatched. Cause 94: AC or PW token exceed.
procedure: Cause 1: Invalid reason type. 1. Check whether the alarm alarm-name hwPWVcDown initial-startup enable command has been run. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 4. 2. Check whether the service is newly created. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 4. 3. Complete the service configuration according to the product manual. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 3: Local VC Deleted. 1. Confirm that whether the VPWS connection is need to be deleted. If so, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Recreate the VPWS connection. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 4: LDP Session Down. 1. Run the display mpls ldp session command to check the status of the LDP session between the local and remote devices. If such an LDP session does not exist, or the LDP session is not in the operational state, restore the status of the LDP session and check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 3. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End. Cause 6: Same LDP mapping was received with different label and MTU. 1. Run the reset pw command to reset local PW. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 3. End. Cause 8: LDP mapping was received with mismatching interface parameters. 1. Run the display mpls l2vc interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command to check whether the MTU is same of local PW and remote PW. If the interface is ATM or TDM, check whether the parameters of the interfaces is same. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Make sure the MTU and parameters of the ATM or TDM interfaces is coincident. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 12: New LDP mapping message was received but remote VC or local VC is Down. 1. Run the display mpls l2vc command to check whether the MTUs of the local and remote PWs are the same. If the interface is an ATM or TDM interface, check whether the interface parameters are consistent. If yes, go to Step 3. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Adjust the MTUs to be the same and change the parameter setttings of the local and remote ATM or TDM interfaces to be the same. Then, check whether the fault is rectified. If the fault is rectified, go to Step 4. If the fault persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 13: LDP Withdrawn Received. 1. Check whether the VPWS connection needs to be deleted manually. If not, run the mpls l2vc command to restore the connection. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 3. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 3. End. Cause 14: LDP release message was received. 1. Run the display mpls l2vc command to check whether the control word values of the local and remote PWs are the same. If the interface is an ATM or TDM interface, check whether the local and remote interface parameter settings are consistent. If yes, go to Step 3. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Adjust the control word values to ensure that the control words at both ends of the PW are consistent. In addition, change the parameter settings of the local and remote ATM or TDM interfaces to be consistent. Then, check whether the fault is rectified. If the fault is rectified, go to Step 4. If the fault persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 19: Interface Down. 1. Run the display mpls l2vc interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command to check the status of the AC interface. If the AC state is Down, go to Step 2. If the AC state is Up, go to Step 3. 2. Run the display interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command to view the physical and link status of the interface. If the status of the interface is Down, restore the physical and link status to Up. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 20: Encapsulation changed. 1. Run the display mpls l2vc command to check whether the local and remote PW encapsulation types are the same. If they are the same, go to Step 2. If they are different, change them to be the same and go to Step 3. 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 3. End. Cause 24: Tunnel was Down. 1. Run the display mpls l2vc command to check whether the tunnel ID exists. If the tunnel ID exists, go to Step 3. If the tunnel ID does not exist, go to Step 4. 2. Check whether the public network interface is Down. If it is Down, bring it Up and then run the display tunnel-info all command to check the tunnel status. After the tunnel goes Up, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 31: LDP Notification Not-Forwarding. 1. Run the display mpls l2vc interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command to check the status of the remote AC interface. If the AC state is Down, go to Step 2. If the AC state is Up, go to Step 3. 2. Run the display interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command to view the physical and link status of the remote interface. If the status of the interface is Down, restore the physical and link status to Up. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display mpls l2vc vc-id command to check the VC tunnel/token info field in the command output. If VC tunnel/token info is displayed as 0 tunnels/tokens, it indicates that no tunnel is selected by a PW. Run the display mpls l2vc interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command to check the tunnel policy name field in the command output. If tunnel policy name is displayed as "--", it indicates that an LDP LSP is used as the tunnel for a PW or no tunnel policy is configured. An MPLS TE tunnel can be used for a PW only after a tunnel policy is configured. If tunnel policy name is not displayed as "--", it indicates that a tunnel policy is adopted. In this case, you can run the display this command in the tunnel policy view to view the tunnel policy configuration. Modify the configuration on the outbound interface on a public network and restore the tunnel connected to the peer. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 32: PW was recreated. 1. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 3. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 3. End. Cause 41: Local PSN Fault. 1. Run the display tunnel-info all command to check information about the tunnel connected to the peer. Modify the configuration on the outbound interface on a public network and restore the tunnel connected to the peer. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 3. End. Cause 43: BFD for pw status changed to Down. 1. Perform the troubleshooting operations described in hwBfdSessDown to rectify the fault. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 3. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 3. End. Cause 47: Manual set was enabled. 1. Run the display this command on the AC interface to check whether the manual-set pw-ac-fault configuration exists. If the configuration exists, go to Step 2. If the configuration does not exist, go to Step 3. 2. Run the undo manual-set pw-ac-fault command and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 3. If the alarm persists, go to Step 4. 3. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 60: MTU Unmatched. 1. Run the display mpls l2vc interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command to check whether the local VC MTU is the same as remote VC MTU. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Check the MTU of the local AC interface and the MTU of the remote AC interface. If two MTUs are not the same, modify them to be the same. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display mpls l2vc interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command to check the local control word is the same as the remote control word. Note that they are the same only when both are either in the enable state or in the disable state. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 94: AC or PW token exceed. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel.
parameters: VcId::VC ID. | VcType::VC type. | PeerAddress::IP address of a peer. | InterfaceIndex::AC interface index. | VcInboundLabel::Incoming label of a VC. | VcOutboundLabel::Outgoing label of a VC. | SecondaryPw::Flag indicating whether the PW is a secondary PW: 1: secondary PW. 2: non-secondary PW. | HWL2VpnStateChangeReason::Cause of the VC status change. | SysUpTime::System startup time. | InterfaceName::AC interface name. | SwitchVcId::Switch VC ID. | TunnelPolicyName::Name of a tunnel policy.

description: OSPFv3 routes advertised by another device were deleted, and the possibly faulty device did not support OSPFv3 flush LSA source trace. Log in to the possibly faulty device. If it is flushing LSAs, reset or isolate it. If the possibly faulty node is not flushing LSAs, check other possibly faulty nodes. impact_on_system: Network flapping may occur, affecting traffic forwarding. In the alarm, the value of FlushLsaNum may be 0. The interval at which the alarm is cleared and the interval at which the value of FlushLsaNum on the faulty node is cleared are both 3600s. There may be a short period (5 minutes at most) during which the value of FlushLsaNum on the faulty node is cleared but the alarm still persists. This is a normal situation.
possible_causes: OSPFv3 routes advertised by another device were deleted, and the possibly faulty device did not support OSPFv3 flush LSA source trace.
procedure: 1. Log in to the suspected faulty device and run the display ospfv3 routing command to check whether routes are deleted. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End.

description:
The ptsf alarm of the ptp port occurs. (hwPtpPortIfIndex=[hwPtpPortIfIndex], hwPtpPortName=[hwPtpPortName], hwPtpPortPtsfReason=[hwPtpPortPtsfReason]) The PTSF alarm is generated on a PTP port in the following situations:
1. PTSF-Sync packet loss: PTP Sync packets sent by the master clock were lost.
2. PTSF-Unavailable: The PTP time signal received by the slave clock was unavailable, exceeding the tolerance threshold of the slave clock.
3. PTSF-Unavailable: The accumulated drift of the PTP time received by the slave clock was too large, exceeding the terminal's tolerance threshold.
4. PTSF-Unavailable: The PTP time received by the slave clock changed sharply and greatly, exceeding the terminal's tolerance threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The PTP time cannot be locked.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Sync packet loss. Cause 2: The PDV is too large or the clock jitter of the master is too large. Cause 3: The accumulated drift of the PTP time is too large. Cause 4: The PTP time changed sharply and greatly.
procedure: Cause 1: Sync packet loss. 1. Run the display this include-default command in the interface view of the time source device to check whether the packet sending rate decreases. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Run the ptp sync-interval <sync-interval-value> command in the interface view of the time source device to increase the packet sending rate. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 2: The PDV is too large or the clock jitter of the master is too large. 1. Run the display this command in the interface view to check whether the ptp asymmetry-correction command is run to correct the asymmetry delay. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Run the undo ptp asymmetry-correction command and check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 3: The accumulated drift of the PTP time is too large. 1. Check whether the upstream link of the faulty port that reports the PTSF alarm has been configured or changed. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Restore the configuration or link change and check whether the PTSF alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 4. End. Cause 4: The PTP time changed sharply and greatly. 1. Check whether the upstream link of the faulty port that reports the PTSF alarm has been configured or changed. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Restore the configuration or link change and check whether the PTSF alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 4. End.
parameters: hwPtpPortIfIndex::Index of the interface where the clock source is located. | hwPtpPortName::Name of the interface where the clock source is located. | hwPtpPortPtsfReason::Causes of PTSF: 1: LOSS_SYNC. Sync packets are lost. 2: UNUSABLE. The PDV is too large or the clock jitter of the master is too large. 3: UNUSABLE_SLOW. The accumulated drift of the PTP time received by the slave device is too large. 4: UNUSABLE_FAST. The PTP time received by the slave device changes sharply and greatly.

procedure: 1. Run the display ospf brief command to check whether the number of ASE LSAs generated when OSPF imports routes exceeds the upper alarm threshold. The Current status field in the display ospf brief command output shows the overload status. Normal indicates that the number is less than the lower alarm threshold. Approach limit indicates that the number reaches 90% of the upper alarm threshold. Exceed limit indicates that the number reaches or exceeds the maximum number. If the threshold is exceeded, this message is informational only, and no action is required. If the threshold is not exceeded yet, go to Step 2. 2. Perform the following operations as required: If a change in the maximum number of ASE LSAs generated when OSPF imports routes is allowed, run the import-route limit <limit-number> [ threshold-alarm upper-limit <upper-limit-value> lower-limit <lower-limit-value> ] command to change the maximum number. If a change in the maximum number of ASE LSAs generated when OSPF imports routes is not allowed, go to Step 3. 3. Contact technical support personnel.
parameters: hwOspfv2ProcessIdIndex::Indicates the OSPF process ID. | hwOspfv2Threshold::Indicates the upper alarm threshold for the number of ASE LSAs generated when an OSPF process imports external routes.

description: PCEP session state change. (PcepEntityIndex=[EntityIndex], PcepPeerAddrType=[AddrType], PcepPeerAddr=[PeerAddr], PcepSessInitiator=[SessionInitiator], PcepSessState=[SessionState], PcepSessStateLastChange=[StateChangeTime], Reason=[Reason]) The PCEP session status changed.
impact_on_system: Establishment of new services based on the PCEP session and maintenance of existing services are affected.
possible_causes: Cause 1: PCEP session in a low state Cause 2: Hold timer expired Cause 3: Malformed message received Cause 4: Maximum unknown requests received Cause 5: Maximum unknown messages received Cause 6: CLI Reset Cause 7: Source address configuration change Cause 8: Protocol error message received Cause 9: Protocol close message received Cause 10: Socket message received Cause 11: Open message received Cause 12: Mandatory objects missing Cause 13: Multiple close connections received Cause 14: PCEP configuration delete Cause 16: Numerous packets were stacked on the PCC and failed to be sent Cause 17: Stateful PCE resource limit exceeded Cause 18: StartTLS negotiation failed Cause 19: TLS negotiation failed
procedure: Cause 1: PCEP session in a low state 1. Run the display current-configuration command to check whether the source IP address configured on the PCE server is consistent with the IP address of the candidate server configured on the PCE client. - If yes, go to step 2. - If no, run the source-address command on the PCE server or the connect-server command on the forwarder to modify the configuration, so that the source IP address configured on the PCE server is consistent with the IP address of the candidate server configured on the PCC client. Then, check whether the fault is resolved. If the fault persists, proceed with the subsequent operations. 2. Run the display current-configuration command to check whether the keychain configuration on the PCE server is consistent with that on the PCE client, such as the authentication algorithm and Key-id. If the configuration is consistent, it is recommended that the key-string command be run to set a password to ensure that the keychain configuration is consistent at both ends. Then, check whether the fault is resolved. If the fault persists, proceed with the subsequent operations. 3. Run the display ip routing-table command on the forwarder to check whether the forwarder has received the routing from the server. - If yes, go to step 4. - If no, check whether the IS-IS configuration is consistent at both ends. Such configuration include the system ID, IS-IS level, and regional address. If the IS-IS configuration is inconsistent, modify the configuration by referring to section IS-IS Configuration, ensuring that the forwarder can receive the routing from the server. Then, check whether the fault is resolved. If the fault persists, go to step 4. 4. Check whether the physical connection between the PCE server and PCE client is normal. - If yes, go to step 5. - If no, disconnect and then reconnect the forwarder and controller, or replace the physical connection between the forwarder and controller for the link to be normal. description: The prefix-sid conflict is detected. (SrProtocol=[hwSrProtocol], SrProcessId=[hwSrProcessId], SrPrefixSid=[hwSrPrefixSid], SrPrefixAddress=[hwSrPrefixAddress], SrPrefixAddressMask=[hwSrPrefixAddressMask], SrConflictType=[hwSrConflictType], SrConflictState=[hwSrConflictState]) The prefix or SID conflict was detected.
impact_on_system: Conflicting routes are not used in SR. If a prefix conflict occurs, the system selects a single prefix and ignores the same prefixes advertised by the other devices. If a SID conflict occurs, the system selects a single SID and ignores the same SIDs advertised by the other devices.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The configuration is incorrect. Cause 2: The prefix on a LoopBack interface is the same as the address of a LoopBack interface on another device. Cause 3: The SID configured on a LoopBack interface is the same as the SID on another router. Cause 4: This device is an OSPF ABR, and the LoopBack interfaces of other devices in different areas are configured with the same SID.
procedure: 1. If an OSPF prefix SID conflict occurs, run the display ospf routing command to check the routing entry corresponding to the conflicting prefix. If the value of the Type field is Direct, the local device is the conflicting prefix advertisement source. Otherwise, the conflicting prefix advertisement source is the device identified by the AdverRouter field. Run the ospf prefix-sid { absolute <sid-value> | index <index-value> } [ node-disable ] command on the advertisement source to modify the SID configuration. 2. If an IS-IS prefix SID conflict occurs, run the isis prefix-sid { absolute <sid-value> | index <index-value> } [ node-disable ] command on the advertisement source to modify the SID configuration. 3. In the case of an IS-IS SR/IS-IS SR prefix SID conflict, it is an inter-protocol or inter-process conflict. In this case, run the display segment-routing conflict-db segr { { prefix [ <dest-ip> <mask> ] } | { sid [ <sid> ] } } command to view details about the conflict and run the ospf prefix-sid { absolute <sid-value> | index <index-value> } [ node-disable ] or isis prefix-sid { absolute <sid-value> | index <index-value> } [ node-disable ] command on the advertisement source to modify the SID configuration. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support.
parameters: hwSrProtocol::Segment Routing protocol that raised the alarm. 1. OSPF: A conflict within the same process in the OSPF protocol, and the prefix-sid in the conflict state displays OSPF. 2. ISIS: A conflict within the same process in the ISIS protocol, and the prefix-sid in the conflict state displays ISIS. 3. OSPF-SR: A conflict between the OSPF protocol and other protocols, the OSPF protocol is not preferred, or the OSPF protocol conflicts between processes, an OSPF process is not preferred, then the hwSrProtocol of the prefix-sid in the conflict state displays OSPF-SR. 4. ISIS-SR: A conflict between the ISIS protocol and other protocols, the ISIS protocol is not preferred, or the ISIS protocol conflicts between processes, an ISIS process is not preferred, then the hwSrProtocol of the prefix-sid in the conflict state displays ISIS-SR. 5. IGP-SR: A conflict between the label of IGP-SR and BGP-SR, the label of IGP-SR is not preferred, then the hwSrProtocol of the prefix-sid in the conflict state displays IGP-SR. | hwSrProcessId::Process ID | hwSrPrefixSid::Prefix Sid | hwSrPrefixAddress::The Prefix Address configured in the Loopback Interface. | hwSrPrefixAddressMask::Prefix Ip Address Mask. | hwSrConflictType::Conflict type can be Prefix Sid conflict or Prefix conflict. 1. SidConflict 2. PrefixConflict | hwSrConflictState::Current conflict state.

If car-type in the alarm is PROFILE_BROADCAST_SUPPRESSION_CAR, run the broadcast-suppression cir command in the QoS profile view to change the CIR so that the CAR value is smaller than the rate limit capability of the NP. If car-type in the alarm is PROFILE_UNKNOWN_UNICAST_SUPPRESSION_CAR, run the unknown-unicast-suppression cir command in the QoS profile view to change the CIR so that the CAR value is smaller than the rate limit capability of the NP. If car-type in the alarm is PROFILE_MULTICAST_SUPPRESSION_CAR, run the multicast-suppression cir command in the QoS profile view to change the CIR so that the CAR value is smaller than the rate limit capability of the NP. If car-type in the alarm is PROFILE_BU_SUPPRESSION_CAR, run the bu-suppression cir command in the QoS profile view to change the CIR so that the CAR value is smaller than the rate limit capability of the NP. If car-type in the alarm is PROFILE_BUM_SUPPRESSION_CAR, run the bum-suppression cir command in the QoS profile view to change the CIR so that the CAR value is smaller than the rate limit capability of the NP. If car-type in the alarm is ACL_CAR, run the car command in the traffic behavior view to change the CIR or PIR so that the CAR value is smaller than the rate limit capability of the NP. If car-type in the alarm is ACL_BROADCAST_SUPPRESSION_CAR, run the broadcast-suppression cir command in the traffic behavior view to change the CIR so that the CAR value is smaller than the rate limit capability of the NP. If car-type in the alarm is ACL_MULTICAST_SUPPRESSION_CAR, run the multicast-suppression cir command in the traffic behavior view to change the CIR so that the CAR value is smaller than the rate limit capability of the NP. If car-type in the alarm is ACL_UNKNOWN_UNICAST_SUPPRESSION_CAR, run the unknown-unicast-suppression cir command in the traffic behavior view to change the CIR so that the CAR value is smaller than the rate limit capability of the NP. After the configuration is modified, check whether the alarm is cleared.

description: The hot-standby LSP of the tunnel changes to Down. (SessionTunnelId=[SessionTunnelId], TunnelInstIndex=[TunnelInstIndex], IngressLsrId=[IngressLsrId], EgressLsrId=[EgressLsrId], mplsTunnelIfName=[mplsTunnelIfName], hwMplsTunnelDownReason=[hwMplsTunnelDownReason], hwMplsTunnelDownLSRId=[hwMplsTunnelDownLSRId], hwMplsTunnelDownIfAddrType=[hwMplsTunnelDownIfAddrType], hwMplsTunnelDownIfAddr=[hwMplsTunnelDownIfAddr], SignalledTunnelName=[SignalledTunnelName]) The hot-standby LSP of the tunnel changes to Down.
impact_on_system: If traffic is not forwarded along the hot-standby LSP of the tunnel, traffic forwarding will not be affected. If traffic is forwarded along the primary LSP of the tunnel and other LSP of the tunnel is in up state, traffic will be switched to the other LSP. If not, traffic forwarding will be interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The interface went Down. Cause 2: The configuration of the tunnel was deleted. Cause 3: The link was faulty. Cause 4: The hot-standby LSP had nodes through which the primary LSP passed. Cause 5: RSVP-TE LSP resources were preempted. Cause 6: Transmission of an RSVP message timed out. Cause 7: RSVP Hello mechanism detected a downstream node failure. Cause 8: The bypass tunnel in use was Down or unbound from the primary tunnel. Cause 9: CSPF failed to calculate a path. Cause 10: The tunnel was manually shut down.
procedure: Cause 1: The interface went Down. 1. Run the display mpls te tunnel-interface <tunnel-name> command on the ingress (the node where the alarm is generated) to check the tunnel configuration. Check the Tunnel State Desc field to determine whether the tunnel is down. Run the display mpls te tunnel-interface last-error command to check the error message. If the following error information is displayed: If "Cspf failed to calculate a path for Tunnel." is displayed, CSPF has been enabled on the ingress, but CSPF path calculation fails. Go to Step 2. If the message "Trigger RSVP failed." is displayed, go to Step 2. If "One LSP is deleted at smooth period." is displayed, go to Step 6. If "One LSP is deleted at Tunnel aging period" is displayed, go to Step 6. If other errors occur, go to Step 6. If no error message is displayed, go to Step 2. 2. Run the ping command on the egress to check whether the destination IP address of the tunnel can be pinged successfully. If the ping fails, rectify the route fault so that the ingress can ping the destination address of the tunnel. Then, check whether the MPLS_LSPM_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.121.2.1.48 hwMplsTunnelHotstandbyUp alarm is generated. If yes, go to Step 7. If no, go to Step 3. If the ping succeeds, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display this command in the MPLS view on the ingress to check whether the mpls te cspf command is run. That is, check whether CSPF is enabled. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 5. 4. Run the display mpls te cspf destination command on the ingress to check whether a path satisfying the specified constraints exists. If such a path is available, the path information is displayed and CSPF path calculation succeeds. If such a path is unavailable, no path information is displayed and CSPF path calculation fails. If the path computation is successful, run the display current-configuration interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command on the ingress to check tunnel configurations. Determine the working tunnel, protection tunnel, and protection interface. Check whether the mpls te auto-frr command is run in the MPLS view. If the command is run, automatic protection is configured. In this case, you can determine which tunnel is the primary tunnel according to the configuration of the tunnel. If the mpls te auto-frr command is not run, check the mpls te fast-reroute, mpls te record-route, and mpls te bypass-tunnel command configurations to determine the primary and backup tunnels. After determining the primary and backup tunnels, perform the following checks: Check whether the explicit-path command is run to determine whether an explicit path is configured for the tunnel. Check whether the mpls te affinity property command is run to determine whether the affinity attribute is configured for the tunnel. Check whether the mpls te bandwidth command is run to determine whether the bandwidth is configured for the tunnel. Run the display mpls te cspf destination command with constraints specified based on tunnel configurations. The parameters include priority setup-priority, bandwidth, explicit-path path-name, affinity, and hop-limit hop-limit-number. Then check whether a path that satisfies the constraints exists. If such a path is available, the path information is displayed and CSPF path calculation succeeds. If such a path is unavailable, no path information is displayed and CSPF path calculation fails. a. If explicit path calculation fails, check the explicit path and tunnel interface configurations to determine the primary and backup paths. Check whether each interface along the explicit path is up and whether MPLS and MPLS TE are enabled. If explicit path calculation succeeds, check whether the affinity attribute and bandwidth are successfully calculated and whether they are the same as those of the explicit path. You can run the display mpls te cspf destination <ip-address> bandwidth ct0 <ct0-bandwidth> explicit-path <path-name> command. b. If affinities fail to be used to compute a path, run the mpls te affinity property command in the tunnel interface view to modify affinities and run the mpls te link administrative group command in the view of each interface along the path to modify the administrative group attribute. c. If bandwidth-based path computation fails, run the display mpls te link-administration bandwidth-allocation interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command to check whether the bandwidth of the outbound interfaces along the tunnel is sufficient. If bandwidth resources are sufficient, a higher-priority tunnel may preempt bandwidth resources of an existing tunnel. Run the mpls te bandwidth max-reservable-bandwidth and mpls te bandwidth command to increase bandwidth values. d. If path calculation based on other constraints fails, go to Step 6. Then, check whether the MPLS_LSPM_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.121.2.1.48 hwMplsTunnelHotstandbyUp alarm is generated. If yes, go to Step 7. If no, go to Step 5. If path calculation fails, go to Step 5. 5. Run the display explicit-path command to check the interfaces along the tunnel and run the display this command in the interface view to check whether MPLS, MPLS TE, and RSVP-TE are enabled on the interfaces to the destination address. If the functions are not enabled, run the mpls, mpls te, and mpls rsvp-te commands in the interface view. If the interface is not in the Up state, restart the interface. That is, run the shutdown command and then the undo shutdown command in the interface view, or run the restart command in the interface view. Then, check whether the MPLS_LSPM_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.121.2.1.48 hwMplsTunnelHotstandbyUp alarm is generated. If yes, go to Step 7. If no, go to Step 6. 6. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 7. End. Cause 2: The configuration of the tunnel was deleted. The same as Cause 1. Cause 3: The link was faulty. The same as Cause 1. Cause 4: The hot-standby LSP had nodes through which the primary LSP passed. The same as Cause 1. Cause 5: RSVP-TE LSP resources were preempted. The same as Cause 1. Cause 6: Transmission of an RSVP message timed out. The same as Cause 1. Cause 7: RSVP Hello mechanism detected a downstream node failure. The same as Cause 1. Cause 8: The bypass tunnel in use was Down or unbound from the primary tunnel. The same as Cause 1. Cause 9: CSPF failed to calculate a path. The same as Cause 1. Cause 10: The tunnel was manually shut down. The same as Cause 1.
parameters: SessionTunnelId::Indicates the ID of the tunnel. | TunnelInstIndex::Indicates the InstIndex of the tunnel. | IngressLsrId::Indicates the LSR ID of the ingress on the tunnel. | EgressLsrId::Indicates the LSR ID of the egress on the tunnel. | mplsTunnelIfName::Indicates the name of a tunnel. | hwMplsTunnelDownReason::Indicates the reason why a tunnel goes Down. | hwMplsTunnelDownLSRId::Indicates the LSR ID of the error node on a tunnel. | hwMplsTunnelDownIfAddrType::Indicates the IP address type of the error interface on a tunnel. | hwMplsTunnelDownIfAddr::Indicates the IP address of the error interface on a tunnel. | SignalledTunnelName::Tunnel alias.
