description: A conflict between the network slice source prefix of the local device and the IPv6 prefix of another device is detected. (Ospfv3Process=[hwOspfv3ProcessId], RouterId=[hwOspfv3CommonRouterId], PrefixAddress=[hwOspfv3Ipv6Prefix], PrefixAddressMask=[hwOspfv3Ipv6PrefixMask], ConflictRouterId=[hwOspfv3ConflictRouterId]) A conflict between a network slice source prefix of the local device and an IPv6 prefix of another device was detected.

If the local configuration is incorrect, run the ipv6-prefix block-length command on the local device to modify the source prefix of the network slice. 3. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, no further action is required. If the alarm persists, go to Step 4.

description: Neighbor in the BGP update peer-group have not entered a stable state for a long time. (BGP instance=[InstanceName], Afi=[AddrFamilyAfi], Safi=[AddrFamilySafi], VPN instance=[VpnInstance], BgpPeerAddr=[PeerAddress], Description=[Description]) The peers in the BGP update peer-group do not enter the stable state for a long time.
impact_on_system: Traffic is incorrectly forwarded.

description: The software package is damaged.(PhysicalName=[PhysicalName],PackageName=[PackageName]) The software package was damaged. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Cause 1: The storage medium is faulty, causing a damage to the software package. On a device with multiple main control boards, if the software package on a single main control board is damaged, system running is not affected. If the software packages on all the main control boards are damaged, boards may fail to start when they are inserted or restarted. Cause 2: The storage medium is faulty, causing a damage to the software package. The device may be abnormal during running or restart.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The storage medium is faulty, causing a damage to the software package. Cause 2: The storage medium is faulty, causing a damage to the software package.
procedure: Cause 1: The storage medium is faulty, causing a damage to the software package. 1. Determine whether the software package of the master or slave main control board is damaged based on PhysicalName and PhysicalIndex in the alarm. If the software package of the master main control board is damaged, go to Step 3. If the software package of the slave main control board is damaged, go to Step 2. 2. Run the reset slot <slot-id> command to reset the slave main control board. After the slave main control board is reset, the damaged software package is automatically repaired. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 4. 3. Run the slave switchover command to perform an active/standby switchover. The original master main control board synchronizes the software package from the new master main control board to repair the damaged software package. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 2: The storage medium is faulty, causing a damage to the software package. 1. Run the reboot command to restart the device. After the device is restarted, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm and log information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End.

description: ARP detect abnormal. (IfName=[IfName], IpAddr=[IpAddr], MacAddr=[MacAddr], VLAN=[VlanId], CEVLAN=[CeVlanId], OutIfName=[OutIfName]) ARP probe was abnormal.
impact_on_system: Cause 1: ARP entries are aged due to timeout, and the query result shows that IS-IS neighbor entries are matched. After 60 seconds, IS-IS neighbor entries are queried again. If the entries are not deleted, the alarm is reported. If this alarm is generated, the IS-IS route is still reachable when the ARP entry ages unexpectedly. If the conflict is not cleared in a timely manner, faults such as service forwarding failures may occur. Cause 2: IS-IS pushes neighbor information, but ARP entries do not exist. The neighbor information is used to trigger a probe. After the probe is complete, no entry is generated (IS-IS flapping scenario). If this alarm is generated, the status of the IS-IS entry is inconsistent with that of the ARP entry. The IS-IS neighbor information exists, but the ARP entry cannot be probed. As a result, IS-IS flapping may occur. If the conflict is not cleared in a timely manner, faults such as service forwarding failures may occur.
possible_causes: Cause 1: ARP entries are aged due to timeout, and the query result shows that IS-IS neighbor entries are matched. After 60 seconds, IS-IS neighbor entries are queried again. If the entries are not deleted, the alarm is reported. Cause 2: IS-IS pushes neighbor information, but ARP entries do not exist. The neighbor information is used to trigger a probe. After the probe is complete, no entry is generated (IS-IS flapping scenario).
procedure: Cause 1: ARP entries are aged due to timeout, and the query result shows that IS-IS neighbor entries are matched. After 60 seconds, IS-IS neighbor entries are queried again. If the entries are not deleted, the alarm is reported. Collect alarm and configuration information, determine the reason why the ARP entry ages, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 2: IS-IS pushes neighbor information, but ARP entries do not exist. The neighbor information is used to trigger a probe. After the probe is complete, no entry is generated (IS-IS flapping scenario). Collect alarm information, check IS-IS neighbor information, and contact technical support personnel.

description: The status of the non-virtual neighbor has changed. (RouterId=[RouterId], NbrIfIndex=[NbrIfIndex], NbrIfInstId=[NbrIfInstId], NbrRtrId=[NbrRtrId], NbrState=[NbrState], IfName=[IfName], Reason=[NbrStateChangeReason], SubReason=[SubReason]) The OSPFv3 neighbor status changes. The possible causes are that the status of the interface on the neighbor router changes and the contents of Hello packets change.
impact_on_system: This trap is sent when the status of the neighbor on the non-virtual link changes. This trap indicates that the status of the neighbor changes. If the neighbor status changes from a lower state to a higher state, no action is required. If the neighbor status changes from a higher state to a lower state, services may be interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Adjacency holdTimer expired Cause 2: Physical interface change Cause 3: Protocol reason Cause 4: BFD session state change Cause 5: Configuration change Cause 7: Peer router reason
procedure: Cause 1: Adjacency holdTimer expired 1. Run the display ipv6 interface and display ospfv3 peer commands to check the Up/Down status of the interface connected to the neighbor. If the physical interface is Down, check the link and ensure that the link is Up, and then go to Step 2. If the physical interface is Up, go to Step 2. 2. Check whether packets are correctly forwarded and ping the IP address of the peer interface. If the ping operation fails, go to step 5. If the ping operation succeeds, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display ipv6 interface command on the neighbor to check whether the interface of the OSPFv3 neighbor is Up. If the interface is Down, go to Step 5. If the interface is Up, go to Step 4. 4. Run the display ospfv3 interface command to check whether the configurations on both ends are correct. If the configurations are correct, go to step 6. If the configuration is incorrect, go to Step 5. 5. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 6. End. Cause 2: Physical interface change 1. Run the display ipv6 interface command to check whether the physical status of the interface on which the OSPFv3 neighbor relationship is established is normal. If the physical status of the interface is Down, check the optical power of the interface and whether the transmission device is normal. Restore the physical status of the interface to clear the alarm. If the physical status of the interface is *down, the interface has been shut down manually. Run the undo shutdown command on the interface to clear the alarm. If the physical status of the interface is Up, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display ipv6 interface command to check the protocol status of the interface that establishes the OSPFv3 neighbor relationship. If the current protocol status is Down, check whether an IPv6 address is configured and whether the IPv6 address is correct. If yes, clear the alarm by checking the IPv6 address. If the protocol status is Up, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 3: Protocol reason 1. Run the display this command in the interface view and OSPFv3 view of the local and remote devices to check whether the same protocol is enabled on the devices at both ends of the link. If so, go to Step 2. If not, configure the same protocol on the interfaces at both ends of the link where the neighbor relationship needs to be established. 2. Run the display ospfv3 peer command to check OSPF neighbor information. If no neighbor information is displayed, the local device cannot receive Hello packets from the peer device or the received Hello packets are discarded. Go to step 3. If Init is displayed, the local device can receive Hello packets from the peer device, but the peer device cannot receive Hello packets from the local device. Run the ping command to check whether the link to the peer device is normal. Generally, this problem occurs because the forwarding plane is faulty. As a result, packets are discarded. If the alarm cannot be cleared by rectifying the forwarding fault, go to step 4. If 2-way is displayed, ospfv3 dr-priority 0 has been configured on the OSPFv3 interface. Run the ospfv3 dr-priority command to set the DR priority of the interface to a value greater than 0 to clear the alarm. If Exstart is displayed, the device keeps performing DD negotiation and cannot complete DD synchronization. Go to step 3. If Loading is displayed, the local device considers the received LSAs invalid, discards them, and keeps requesting for LSAs. You can run the reset ospfv3 process-id command on both ends of the link where the OSPFv3 neighbor relationship needs to be established to clear the alarm. Resetting an OSPFv3 connection (using the reset ospfv3 process-id command) interrupts the OSPFv3 neighbor relationship between devices. Exercise caution when resetting OSPFv3 connections. 3. Run the display this command in the interface view and OSPFv3 process view to check whether the authentication configurations on both ends of the link are the same. If so, go to Step 4. If not, configure the same authentication mode on both ends of the link. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 4: BFD session state change 1. Run the ping command to check whether the link to the peer device is normal. If the peer device cannot be pinged, check the transmission devices, links, and interfaces, and adjust the hardware to restore services. If the ping operation succeeds, go to step 4. 2. Run the ping command in the interface view to check whether the link configuration is correct. If the configurations are correct, go to Step 3. If the configuration is incorrect, modify the configuration. 3. Run the display ospfv3 peer command to check whether the neighbor relationship is Up. If the neighbor relationship is Up, go to Step 4. If the neighbor relationship is Down, rectify the fault. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 5: Configuration change 1. Run the display this command in the OSPFv3 process view to check whether the area configurations on both ends of the neighbor are consistent. If they are different, change them to be the same. If they are consistent, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display ospfv3 interface command to check whether the ospfv3 network-type values of the interfaces at both ends of the link are the same. If they are different, change them to be the same. If they are consistent, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 7: Peer router reason 1. Check whether the peer device is provided by another vendor. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Contact the vendor to check the running status of the peer device. 3. Check whether the peer device or OSPFv3 process is restarted. If the peer device or OSPFv3 process has been restarted, locate the fault based on the alarm and log information on the peer device. If the peer device or OSPFv3 process is not restarted, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 5. End.
parameters: RouterId::Router ID | NbrIfIndex::Indicates the IP address of the neighbor. | NbrIfInstId::Indicates the interface index. | NbrRtrId::It identifies the router ID of a neighbor. | NbrState::This parameter indicates the peer state. For the neighbors between DR Others on a broadcast or NBMA network, if the neighbor state is 2-Way, this trap is a service recovery trap; if the neighbor state is Down, Attempt, or Init, this trap is an alarm trap. For the neighbors on a P2P or P2MP network and the neighbors between non-DR Others on a broadcast or NBMA network, if the neighbor state is Full, this trap is a service recovery trap; if the neighbor state is any other state, this trap is an alarm trap. 1: Down 2: Attempt 3: Init 4: 2-Way 5: ExStart 6: Exchange 7: Loading 8: Full | IfName::Indicates the interface name. | NbrStateChangeReason::Indicates the reason why the neighbor status changes. | SubReason::Indicates the detailed reason.

description:

impact_on_system: The network stability may be adversely affected.
possible_causes: The number of NSSA LSAs generated when an OSPF process imported external routes reached or exceeded the maximum number allowed.
procedure: 1. Run the display ospf brief command to check whether the number of NSSA LSAs generated when OSPF imports routes reaches or exceeds the maximum number allowed. The Current status field in the display ospf brief command output shows the overload status. Normal indicates that the number is less than the lower alarm threshold. Approach limit indicates that the number reaches 90% of the upper alarm threshold. Exceed limit indicates that the number reaches or exceeds the maximum number. If the maximum number is exceeded, this message is informational only, and no action is required. If the maximum number is not exceeded yet, go to Step 2. 2. Perform the following operations as required: If a change in the maximum number of NSSA LSAs generated when OSPF imports routes is allowed, run the import-route limit <limit-number> [ threshold-alarm upper-limit <upper-limit-value> lower-limit <lower-limit-value> ] command to change the maximum number. If a change in the maximum number of NSSA LSAs generated when OSPF imports routes is not allowed, go to Step 3. 3. Contact technical support personnel.
parameters: hwOspfv2ProcessIdIndex::Indicates the OSPF process ID. | hwOspfv2AreaId::Indicates the ID of an OSPF area. | hwOspfv2MaxLimit::Indicates the maximum value for the number of NSSA LSAs generated when an OSPF process imports external routes.

If the IPv6 address of the peer interface is different from that of the local interface, go to 3. If information about the peer device is not obtained, go to 4. 2.According to network planning and service deployment, modify the IPv6 address of the local interface and check whether the alarm is cleared. No: Go to 5. 3.According to network planning and service deployment, check whether the IPv6 address of the local interface can be modified.

impact_on_system: When a device imports too many IS-IS routes (reaching the maximum number allowed), it may encounter LSDB overload and heavy flooding workload, potentially causing unexpected restarts and making it unable to advertise new imported routes. This issue can also affect connected devices with limited memory if they receive more routes than they can handle.
possible_causes: The number of imported routes reached the maximum number of routes that can be advertised in the process.
procedure: 1. Run the display this command in the IS-IS view to check whether the maximum number of imported routes that can be advertised by an IS-IS process is too small. If so, run the import-route limit command to adjust the maximum number of imported routes that can be advertised by an IS-IS process, and then go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display isis lsdb local verbose command to check advertised imported routes. Check whether there are unnecessary routes. If so, delete unnecessary routes directly or using the undo import-route command. Then, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 4. 3. Check whether the alarm is cleared.
parameters: hwisisSysInstance::ID of an IS-IS process. | hwIsisAddressFamily::IS-IS address family. | hwisisSysLevelIndex::IS-IS Level. | hwisisImportRouteAdvMax::Maximum number of imported routes that can be advertised by an IS-IS process. | hwIsisImportRouteAdvNumber::Number of imported routes advertised by an IS-IS process.

After the upload is complete, if the trust certificate is about to expire, run the trusted-ca load command to replace the certificate as follows: Command for loading an ASN1 trusted-CA file for an SSL policy: trusted-ca load asn1-ca filename Command for loading a PEM trusted-CA file for an SSL policy: trusted-ca load pem-ca filename Command for loading a PFX trusted-CA file for an SSL policy: trusted-ca load pfx-ca filename auth-code cipher password 3. If the identity certificate is about to expire, run the certificate load command to replace the certificate as follows. Command for loading a PEM certificate for an SSL policy: certificate load pem-cert filename key-pair dsa key-file filename auth-code cipher password Command for loading a PFX certificate for an SSL policy: certificate load pfx-cert filename key-pair rsa key-file filename auth-code cipher password Command for loading a PEM certificate chain for an SSL policy: certificate load pem-chain filename key-pair rsa key-file filename auth-code cipher password

description: The mac address learned by the board is beyond the threshold of the global mac limit rule. (EntPhysicalIndex=[hwEntPhysicalIndex], PhysicalName=[hwPhyscialName], RuleName=[rule_name], LearnNumber=[learn_number], LimitNumber=[limit_number]) The number of MAC addresses learned by the board reached the limit set in the global rule. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: 1. If the action to be taken after the MAC address limit is reached is discard, for example, if the mac-limit rule-name aaa maximum 10 rate 10 action discard command is run to limit the number of learned MAC addresses to 10, packets with excess MAC addresses are discarded. 2. If the action to be taken after the MAC address limit is reached is forward, for example, if the mac-limit rule-name aaa maximum 10 rate 10 action forward command is run to limit the number of learned MAC addresses to 10, packets with excess MAC addresses are forwarded.
possible_causes: A global MAC address limit was configured and enabled, and the number of learned dynamic MAC addresses reached the limit.
procedure: 1. This alarm is informational only. To clear the alarm, go to Step 2. 2. Run either of the following commands: (1) To delete unnecessary MAC address entries, run the undo mac-address command in the system view. (2) To reconfigure the maximum number of MAC addresses that can be learned, run the mac-limit rule-name maximum command in the system view. After the configuration is complete, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End.
parameters: hwEntPhysicalIndex::Indicates the index of a physical entity. | hwPhyscialName::Name of a physical entity. | rule_name::Name of the global MAC limit rule. | learn_number::Number of learned MAC addresses. | limit_number::Maximum number.

Replace the board whose hardware active/standby role is abnormal and check whether the alarm is generated again.

(hwPhysicalPortIfIndex=[hwPhysicalPortIfIndex],SlotID=[hwPhysicalPortInSlot],CardID=[hwPhysicalPortInCard],PortID=[hwPhysicalPortInPort],InterfaceName=[hwPhysicalPortName]) B2 Sf counter in the multiplex section alarm. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: A service switchover or interruption will occur.
possible_causes: Cause 0: The optical fiber was broken. Cause 1: The optical loss was beyond the normal range. Cause 2: The remote device failed to send the optical signal. Cause 3: The cross-connect board of the remote device failed, was not installed, or was not installed properly. Cause 4: The clock board of the remote device failed.
procedure: 1.Check whether any optical fiber is connected to the optical interface. If no optical fiber is used, shut down the laser of the optical interface and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 2.Check whether the optical fiber is broken. If the optical fiber is broken, replace the optical fiber and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 3.Check whether the receive optical power of the local device is less than the minimum value. If the receive optical power is less than the minimum value, clean the optical fiber connector and the optical interface on the interface board. Check that the flange and the optical attenuator are properly connected and the optical attenuator value is in the normal range. Then check whether the alarm is cleared.
parameters: hwPhysicalPortIfIndex::Index of physical port. | hwPhysicalPortInSlot::Slot ID. | hwPhysicalPortInCard::Card ID. | hwPhysicalPortInPort::Port ID. | hwPhysicalPortName::Name of physical port.

description: An IS-IS IP address conflict between the local device and another device was detected. (SysInstance=[hwisisSysInstance], Level=[hwisisSysLevelIndex], ConflictType=[hwIsisConflictType], ConflictIP=[hwIsisConflictIpAddr], ConflictSystemID1=[hwIsisConflictSystemID], ConflictSystemID2=[hwIsisConflictSystemID2]) The local interface IP address used to establish the IS-IS IPv4 neighbor relationship conflicts with the IP address of the outbound interface of another device.
impact_on_system: If the IP addresses of interfaces on some devices are the same, routes are incorrectly calculated or route flapping occurs, affecting services.
possible_causes: The IP address of a device on the IS-IS network is the same as the IP address of the local interface used to establish the neighbor relationship.
procedure: 1. Determine the conflicting IS-IS process, process level, conflict type, conflicting IP address, and conflicting device based on the alarm information. 2. Run the undo ip address command to delete the IS-IS IP address of the conflicting device. 3. Re-plan the IP addresses in the IS-IS process on the device to ensure that they are unique on the network. 4. Run the ip address command to configure a new IP address and check whether the alarm is cleared. If no, collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. If yes, no further action is required.
parameters: hwisisSysInstance::ID of an IS-IS process. | hwisisSysLevelIndex::IS-IS Level. | hwIsisConflictType::Conflicting type. | hwIsisConflictIpAddr::Conflicting IP address. | hwIsisConflictSystemID::Conflicting local system ID. | hwIsisConflictSystemID2::Conflicting system ID.

description: Patch operation failed. (SlotIndex=[SlotIndex], PatchIndex=[PatchIndex], PackageName=[PackageName], PackageVersion=[PackageVersion], FailReason=[FailReason], PhysicalName=[PhysicalName]) The patch package fails to be installed. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Services will not be affected.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Failed to read the configuration information of the patch package. Cause 2: The cause value was not used. Cause 3: The memory space of the memory was not enough. Cause 4: The patch conflicted with the previous one. Cause 5: The patch package version was incorrect. Cause 8: Failed to synchronize the patch package file because of insufficient disk space. Cause 9: The patch configuration is inconsistent. Cause 10: The source file in the patch is abnormal. Cause 11: The patch package does not support the current main control board.
procedure: Cause 1: Failed to read the configuration information of the patch package. 1. Reinstall the patch package. After the installation is complete, run the display patch-information command to check the status of the patch package. If the patch package is in the run state, the patch package is successfully installed. The fault is rectified. If the patch package is not in the run state, go to Step 2. 2. Collect logs and contact technical support personnel. Cause 2: The cause value was not used. Collect logs and contact technical support personnel. Cause 3: The memory space of the memory was not enough. 1. Run the dir command to check whether the remaining space is sufficient. If yes, go to step 3. If no, go to step 2. 2. Clear the space and reinstall the patch package. After the patch package is installed, run the display patch-information command to check whether the patch package is in the run state. If the patch package is in the run state, the patch package is successfully installed. If yes, go to step 4. If no, go to step 3. 3. Collect logs and contact technical support. 4. End. Cause 4: The patch conflicted with the previous one. 1. Uninstall the current patch and reinstall the patch package. After the patch package is installed, run the display patch-information command to check whether the patch package is in the run state. If the patch package is in the run state, the patch package is successfully installed. If yes, go to step 4. If no, go to step 2. 2. Restart the device and install the patch package. After the patch package is installed, run the display patch-information command to check whether the patch package is in the run state. If the patch package is in the run state, the patch package is successfully installed. If yes, go to step 4. If no, go to step 3. 3. Collect logs and contact technical support. 4. End. Cause 5: The patch package version was incorrect. 1. Run the display startup command to query the version of the system software package. 2. Replace the patch with a patch that matches the system software package version. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to step 4. If no, go to step 3. 3. Collect alarm and log information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 8: Failed to synchronize the patch package file because of insufficient disk space. 1. Run the dir command to check the free disk space of the board in the slot indicated in the alarm information. If the remaining space is less than the size of the patch file to be loaded, run the delete /unreserved command to delete unnecessary files and clear the environment to ensure sufficient space. Then, go to step 2. If the remaining disk space is greater than the size of the patch file to be loaded, go to step 3. 2. Load the patch again and restart the board in the corresponding slot. 3. Collect alarm and log information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 9: The patch configuration is inconsistent. There are three ways to clear the alarm: 1. After the trap is reported, the active/standby switchover is performed twice. Half an hour after the board is registered, the trap is cleared through the aging mechanism. If the trap cannot be cleared, go to step 4. 2. After the alarm is reported, restart a single board. After the board is registered for half an hour, the alarm on the corresponding board is cleared through the aging mechanism. If the alarm persists, go to step 4. 3. After the alarm is reported, restart the device. If the alarm is cleared, go to step 4. 4. Collect logs and contact technical support. Cause 10: The source file in the patch is abnormal. Collect trap, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 11: The patch package does not support the current main control board. 1. Reload the correct patch package and check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 6. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Perform two active/standby switchovers. After the main control boards are registered for half an hour, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared through the aging mechanism, go to Step 6. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Restart the main control boards. After the main control boards are registered for half an hour, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared through the aging mechanism, go to Step 6. If not, go to Step 4. 4. Restart the device and check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 6. If not, go to Step 5. 5. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support engineers. 6. End. 1. Reload the correct patch package and check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Restart the board. After the board is registered for half an hour, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared through the aging mechanism, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Restart the device and check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support engineers. 5. End.
parameters: SlotIndex::Indicates the index of the board where the patch file is located. | PatchIndex::Indicates the index of a patch file. | PackageName::Name of the patch file. | PackageVersion::Version of the patch file. | FailReason::Indicates the failure cause of the patch installation. | PhysicalName::Indicates the name of the entity where the patch file is located. When the value of SlotIndex is 128, PhysicalName is the system device, indicating that the device reports an alarm.

description: The state of clock source is abnormal. (hwClockSrcCfgChassisIndex=[hwClockSrcCfgChassisIndex], hwClockSrcCfgSourceTypeIndex=[hwClockSrcCfgSourceTypeIndex], hwClockSrcCfgSourceIndex=[hwClockSrcCfgSourceIndex], hwClockChassisId=[hwClockChassisId], hwClockCurSourceName=[hwClockCurSourceName], hwClockSrcCfgSourceState=[hwClockSrcCfgSourceState], hwClockSrcFailedReason=[hwClockSrcFailedReason]) The clock source status was abnormal. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The clock source cannot be used as the synchronization source of the NE.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Clock synchronization is not supported. Cause 2: The link layer is faulty. Cause 3: The slave end of the electrical interface can synchronize the clock only when the negotiation status of the electrical interface is master. Cause 4: The clock signal is abnormal. Cause 5: The large frequency offset is abnormal. Cause 6: The small frequency offset is abnormal.
procedure: 1. Check the cause of the source exception. If clock synchronization is not supported, go to Step 2. If the link layer is faulty, go to Step 3. If the slave port can synchronize clock signals only when the negotiation status of the electrical port is master, go to Step 10. If the clock signal is abnormal, go to Step 11. If the large frequency deviation is abnormal, go to Step 14. If the small frequency deviation is abnormal, go to Step 14. 2. Use the optical module that supports clock synchronization to restore the clock and go to Step 15. 3. View the name of the clock source to determine the type of the clock source. If the clock source is a line clock source, go to Step 4. If the clock source is an external clock source, go to Step 5. If the clock source is a PTP clock source, go to Step 14.
parameters: hwClockSrcCfgChassisIndex::Index of the chassis where the non-PTP clock source is located. In the case of a single chassis, the value is always 1. The chassis index of a PTP source is invalid. | hwClockSrcCfgSourceTypeIndex::Index of the clock source type. The values are as follows: bits(1) ptp(2) interface(3) cesacr(4) | hwClockSrcCfgSourceIndex::Index of the clock source. | hwClockChassisId::Chassis ID. | hwClockCurSourceName::Name of the current clock source. | hwClockSrcCfgSourceState::Status of the current clock source. The values are as follows: initial(0): initial state. normal(1): normal state. abnormal(2): abnormal state. wtr(3): wait-to-restore state. holdoff(4): holdoff state. | hwClockSrcFailedReason::Cause of the loss of a clock source: If multiple causes exist, the main cause is reported based on the priority. normal(0): The frequency source is normal. clockSyncNonsupport(1): Clock synchronization is not supported. linkLayerFault(2): The link layer is faulty. electricalportNegoMaster(3): The slave port can synchronize clock signals only when the negotiation status of the electrical port is master. clockSignalAbnormal(4): The clock signal is abnormal. largeFreqDeviation(5): The large frequency deviation is abnormal. smallFreqDeviation(6): The small frequency deviation is abnormal.

description: The CPU usage exceeded the pre-set overload threshold. (TrapSeverity=[TrapSeverity], ProbableCause=[ProbableCause], EventType=[EventType], PhysicalIndex=[PhysicalIndex], PhysicalName=[PhysicalName], RelativeResource=[RelativeResource], UsageType=[UsageType], SubIndex=[SubIndex], CpuUsage=[CpuUsage], Unit=[Unit], CpuUsageThreshold=[CpuUsageThreshold]) CPU usage is continuously sampled. This alarm is generated when the average CPU usage sampled in a sampling period is greater than the overload threshold. The default sampling period is 8 minutes. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Services are not affected in a short period. However, if the CPU usage is too high for a long period, services may not be processed in a timely manner. As a result, the system performance, such as the time taken to respond to the user interface, neighbor status, or route convergence performance, will be affected.
possible_causes: The CPU usage exceeded the pre-set overload threshold.
procedure: 1. Run the display cpu-usage and display cpu-usage configuration commands to check the current CPU usage and CPU usage threshold. 2. Delete unnecessary services and configurations to reduce the CPU usage as required. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End.
parameters: TrapSeverity::Indicates the alarm severity. | ProbableCause::Indicates the alarm cause. | EventType::Indicates the alarm type. | PhysicalIndex::Physical index. | PhysicalName::Entity name. | RelativeResource::Indicates the name of the related resource. | UsageType::Indicates the overload type. | SubIndex::Entity sub-index. | CpuUsage::Indicates the CPU usage. | Unit::Unit. | CpuUsageThreshold::Indicates the CPU threshold.

description: An IS-IS system ID conflict occurred. The system ID may have been automatically restored, but the conflicting configuration may still exist. (SysInstance=[hwisisSysInstance], Level=[hwisisSysLevelIndex], ConflictSystemID=[hwIsisConflictSystemID], LocalHostName=[hwIsisHostName], RemoteHostName=[hwIsisAdjSysName]) This alarm is generated when an IS-IS system ID conflict occurs.

possible_causes: The same IS-IS system ID is configured on multiple non-directly connected devices in the network.
procedure: 1. Run the undo network-entity command to delete the IS-IS system ID of the local device. 2. Re-plan the IS-IS system ID of the local device to ensure that it is unique on the network. 3. Run the network-entity command to configure a new IS-IS system ID. 4. Run the display isis system-id conflict command to check whether an IS-IS system ID conflict exists. If the conflict persists, go to Step 1 or collect log and configuration information and contact technical support personnel. If the conflict no longer exists, the alarm is cleared, and no further action is required.

description: The status of the SVC VC turned DOWN. (InterfaceIndex=[InterfaceIndex], InterfaceIndex=[InterfaceIndex2], SvcId=[SvcId], SVcType=[SVcType], PeerAddress=[PeerAddress], SvcInboundLabel=[SvcInboundLabel], SvcOutboundLabel=[SvcOutboundLabel], HWL2VpnStateChangeReason=[HWL2VpnStateChangeReason], InterfaceName=[InterfaceName], TunnelPolicyName=[TunnelPolicyName]) An SVC PW went Down.
impact_on_system: The static PW service is interrupted and traffic is blocked.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Invalid reason type. Cause 3: VC was deleted. Cause 19: Interface was Down. Cause 24: Tunnel was Down. Cause 32: PW was recreated. Cause 41: Local PSN Fault. Cause 94: AC or PW of SVC service token exceed.
procedure: Cause 1: Invalid reason type. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 3: VC was deleted. 1. Check whether the VPWS connection needs to be deleted. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Re-establish the VPWS connection and check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 19: Interface was Down. 1. Run the display mpls static-l2vc interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command to check the AC state. If the AC interface is down, go to Step 2. If the AC interface is up, go to Step 3. 2. Run the display interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command to check the physical status and link status of the AC interface. If the interface is down, restore the physical and link status of the interface to up, and then check whether the fault is rectified. If the fault is rectified, go to Step 4. If the fault persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 24: Tunnel was Down. 1. Run the display mpls static-l2vc command to check whether the tunnel ID exists. If yes, go to Step 3. If no, go to Step 4. 2. Check whether the public network-side interface is down. After the public network-side interface goes up, run the display tunnel-info all command to check whether the tunnel goes up. Then, check whether the fault is rectified. If the fault is rectified, go to Step 4. If the fault persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 32: PW was recreated. 1. Check whether the fault is rectified. If the fault is rectified, go to Step 3. If the fault persists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End. Cause 41: Local PSN Fault. 1. Run the display tunnel-info all command to check information about the tunnel to the peer end. Adjust the configuration of the outbound interface on the public network to restore the tunnel to the peer end. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If the fault is rectified, go to Step 3. If the fault persists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End. Cause 94: AC or PW of SVC service token exceed. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel.
parameters: InterfaceIndex::AC interface index. | InterfaceIndex2::AC interface index. | SvcId::SVC PW ID. | SVcType::SVC type. | PeerAddress::Peer address. | SvcInboundLabel::Incoming label of an SVC PW. | SvcOutboundLabel::Outgoing label of an SVC PW. | HWL2VpnStateChangeReason::Cause of the VC status change. | InterfaceName::AC interface name. | TunnelPolicyName::Name of the referenced tunnel policy.

description: The BGP FSM moves from a higher numbered state to a lower numbered state. (BgpPeerRemoteAddr=[PeerIpv4Ipv6Addr], InstanceId=[InstanceId], BgpPeerLastError=[PeerLastError], BgpPeerState=[PeerState], LocalIfName=[LocalIfName], Reason=[Reason], Description=[Description]) The BGP state machine changes from the Openconfirm or Established state to a lower state.
impact_on_system: The BGP peer relationship is interrupted, routes become unreachable, and BGP forwarding services are interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause 1: BGP configuration lead peer down Cause 2: BGP receive notification Cause 3: BGP receive error packet Cause 4: BGP hold timer expire Cause 5: BGP remote peer not reachable Cause 6: BGP direct connect-interface down Cause 7: BGP route exceed the maximum number allowed Cause 9: The system memory is overloaded
procedure: Cause 1: BGP configuration lead peer down 1. Check whether the peer relationship is interrupted due to incorrect configurations. If yes, go to step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Delete the configuration that causes the peer relationship to go Down. 3. Check whether the BGP connection is reset. If the BGP connection is not reset, go to Step 4. If the BGP connection is reset, wait for a while and check whether the connection is restored. If the connection is not restored, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information and contact technical support. Cause 2: BGP receive notification 1. Run the display bgp vpnv4 vpn-instance unnumbered peer interface log-info command to check the Notification message sent when the BGP peer relationship is interrupted. If the error code in the Notification message is 4, the BGP hold timer expires and no Keepalive message is received. In this case, go to Step 3. If the error code in the Notification message is 5, the BGP FSM is faulty. In this case, go to Step 7. If the error code in the Notification message is 6, the BGP connection is torn down manually. In this case, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display bgp vpnv4 vpn-instance unnumbered peer interface log-info command to check whether the Notification message is sent by the device that generates the alarm. If yes, go to Step 3. If no, go to Step 4. 3. Run the ping command to check whether the IP address of the BGP peer can be pinged. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 5. 4. Check whether the CPU usage is too high. If yes, go to Step 7. If no, go to Step 5. 5. Run the display acl command to check whether the device is configured with an ACL that denies TCP port 179. If yes, delete the ACL that denies TCP port 179. If no, go to Step 6. 6. Contact maintenance engineers of the peer device and check whether BGP has been reset on the peer device, the peer device has been enabled using the peer enable command in other address families on the local device, or BGP connection parameters have been set. If any of these operations has been performed, wait for a while and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 7. 7. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 3: BGP receive error packet 1. Run the display bgp vpnv4 vpn-instance unnumbered peer interface log-info command to check the Notification message sent when the BGP peer relationship is interrupted. If the error code in the Notification message is 1, BGP received messages with incorrect headers. In this case, go to Step 2. If the error code in the Notification message is 2, BGP received incorrect Open messages. In this case, go to Step 2. If the error code in the Notification message is 3, BGP received incorrect Update messages. In this case, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 4: BGP hold timer expire 1. Run the ping command to check whether the IP address of the BGP peer can be pinged. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Check whether the CPU usage is too high. The command varies according to the device. If yes, go to Step 5. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display acl command to check whether an ACL is configured to disable TCP port 179. If yes, delete the ACL that denies TCP port 179. If no, go to Step 4. 4. Contact the maintenance personnel of the peer device to check whether BGP is reset on the peer device, whether the peer enable command is used to enable the peer in another address family on the local device, or whether BGP connection parameters are set. If any of the preceding operations is performed, wait for a while and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 5. 5. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 5: BGP remote peer not reachable 1. Run the ping command to check whether the IP address of the BGP peer can be pinged. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Check whether the CPU usage is too high. The command varies according to the device. If yes, go to Step 5. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display acl command to check whether an ACL is configured to disable TCP port 179. If yes, delete the ACL that denies TCP port 179. If no, go to Step 4. 4. Contact the maintenance personnel of the peer device to check whether BGP is reset on the peer device, whether the peer enable command is used to enable the peer in another address family on the local device, or whether BGP connection parameters are set. If any of the preceding operations is performed, wait for a while and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 5. 5. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 6: BGP direct connect-interface down 1. Check whether the shutdown command is executed on the interface. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information and contact technical support. Cause 7: BGP route exceed the maximum number allowed 1. Check whether the peer route-limit command is configured and whether the number of routes exceeds the upper limit. If yes, go to step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Check whether the peer route-limit command is necessary. If it is necessary, reduce the number of routes to ensure that the number of routes is smaller than the upper limit of the peer route-limit command. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information and contact technical support. Cause 9: The system memory is overloaded 1. If the memory usage exceeds the threshold, all BGP peers are disconnected. Ten minutes after all BGP peers are disconnected, the BGP process automatically restarts. After the restart, check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to step 3. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End.
parameters: PeerIpv4Ipv6Addr::IP address of a peer. This alarm reports only IPv6 addresses. | InstanceId::Instance ID. | PeerLastError::Error code returned when the peer was disconnected last time. The value of this parameter is displayed in the format of [ErrorCode][ErrorSubCode], where [ErrorCode] indicates an error code and [ErrorSubCode] indicates an error subcode. For example, 35,3 indicates an error code, and 5 indicates an error subcode. For details about error codes, see "BGP Packet Format" in BGP Principles. The value 0 indicates that no error occurs. | PeerState::Status of the BGP peer. | LocalIfName::Name of the local interface. | Reason::Cause of the peer disconnection. Configuration lead peer down: The peer is disconnected due to the configuration. Receive notification: A Notification message is received. Receive error packet: An error packet is received. Hold timer expire: The Hold timer expires. Remote peer not reachable: The remote peer is unreachable. Direct connect-interface down: The directly connected interface is Down. Route limit: The number of routes reaches the upper limit. System memory overloaded: The system memory is overloaded. | Description::Description of a neighbor.

description: The number of TWAMP responder session is out of device capability. The number of TWAMP sessions on the session-responder exceeded the device capability.
impact_on_system: Cause 1: The board was reset or became faulty or the board was removed in the case of normal TWAMP session status, causing the number of TWAMP sessions on the session-responder to exceed the device capability. The excess TWAMP sessions on the session-responder cannot work properly. Cause 2: This alarm is generated when the number of TWAMP responder sessions configured on the device exceeds the device capability. The excess TWAMP sessions on the session-responder cannot work properly. Cause 3: This alarm is generated when a link-bundle TWAMP responder session has excessive trunk member interfaces. The excess TWAMP sessions on the session-responder cannot work properly. Cause 4: This alarm is generated when a standard TWAMP reflector attempts to respond to a test session that exceeds the device capability. The standard TWAMP reflector session that exceeds the system capability cannot work properly.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The board was reset or became faulty or the board was removed in the case of normal TWAMP session status, causing the number of TWAMP sessions on the session-responder to exceed the device capability. Cause 2: This alarm is generated when the number of TWAMP responder sessions configured on the device exceeds the device capability. Cause 3: This alarm is generated when a link-bundle TWAMP responder session has excessive trunk member interfaces. Cause 4: This alarm is generated when a standard TWAMP reflector attempts to respond to a test session that exceeds the device capability.
procedure: 1. Delete some TWAMP sessions on the Session-Reflector, delete some trunk member interfaces of a link-bundle session, stop some standard TWAMP sessions, or insert a new board to increase the device capability. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, the TWAMP session status on the Session-Reflector is normal. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect trap, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.

description: The specified path MTU of an SR Policy was greater than the detected minimum path MTU. (hwSrPolicyEndpoint=[SrPolicyEndpoint], hwSrPolicyColor=[SrPolicyColor], hwSrListId=[SegmetListId], hwSpecifiedPathMTU=[SpecifiedPathMTU], hwDetectedMinMTU=[DetectedMinMTU], hwReplyNodeAddress=[ReplyNodeAddress]) The path MTU of the SR Policy is too large.
impact_on_system: If the MTU value is not adjusted, the path may be disconnected, causing packet loss.
possible_causes: The specified path MTU of an SR Policy was greater than the detected minimum path MTU.
procedure: 1. Run the display alarm active command to query the specified MTU and the minimum MTU detected in the alarm. 2. Run the path-mtu command in the Segment Routing IPv6 view or SR Policy view or configure the MTU of the segment list in the candidate path view to adjust the MTU of the SR Policy to be less than the minimum MTU in the alarm. 3. Check the MTU of each hop on the candidate path of the SR Policy and ensure that the MTU of each hop is no less than the specified MTU in the alarm. 4. Disable path MTU detection in the SR Policy view. 5. Disable path MTU detection globally.
parameters: SrPolicyEndpoint::Endpoint of an SR Policy. | SrPolicyColor::Color of an SR Policy. | SegmetListId::SR Policy candidate path segment list ID. | SpecifiedPathMTU::Specified MTU value. | DetectedMinMTU::Minimum path MTU that is detected. | ReplyNodeAddress::Reply node address.

description: The bridge loses the position of root bridge. (ProcessID=[ProcessID], InstanceID=[InstanceID], ProInstRootType=[ProInstRootType]) A device lost its root bridge role.
impact_on_system: Services may be interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The bridge ID of new equipment is not optimal. Cause 2: Modify thr priority or domain configuration of the device in the original network.
procedure: Cause 1: The bridge ID of new equipment is not optimal. 1. Check whether the new physical link is the required one. If the physical link is required, go to Step 2. If the physical link is not required, go to Step 3. 2. Run the display stp command on the new device to check whether the bridge ID is optimal on the entire network. If the bridge ID is optimal, go to Step 3. If the bridge ID is not optimal, go to Step 5. 3. Check whether the bridge ID of the new device should be the optimal one on the entire network. If the ID should be the optimal one on the entire network, no action is required. If the ID should not be the optimal one on the entire network, go to Step 4. 4. Correct the configuration according to the network topology, and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 5. 5. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 2: Modify thr priority or domain configuration of the device in the original network. 1. Run the display stp command to check whether the priority or region configuration of the instance is changed normally. If yes, no action is required. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Correct the configuration according to the network topology, and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: ProcessID::MSTP process ID | InstanceID::Instance ID | ProInstRootType::Root bridge role type

If no, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End.
parameters: AddressFamily::Address family. | SubdomainID::BIER sub-domain. | ConflictEndBIERSID::Conflicting End.BIER SID. | NextHopAddr::Next hop address.

description:
The LSP sequence number has reached or exceeded the upper threshold value. (SysInstance=[isisSysInstance], SysLevel=[isisSysLevelIndex], LspId=[isisPduLspId], ThresholdValue=0x[thresholdVal]) The LSP sequence number exceeds the specified upper threshold.
After the sequence number of an IS-IS LSP exceeds a specified upper threshold, this alarm is generated. After the sequence number of an IS-IS LSP falls below a specified upper threshold, this alarm is cleared.
impact_on_system: If the LSP sequence number exceeds the upper threshold of 0xFFFFFFFF for more than three times, the IS-IS instance system enters the sleep mode and stops sending or receiving IS-IS packets.
possible_causes: Cause 1: An attacker simulated a locally generated LSP, set its sequence number to a value that is greater than the upper alarm threshold, and sent the LSP to the local device. Cause 2: Another device on the network had the same IS-IS System ID as the local one.
procedure: 1. Run the display isis lsdb command to check the sequence number of the LSP generated by the local device. If the sequence number increases normally, this log message is informational only, and no action is required. If the sequence number increases too fast, go to step 2. 2. Run the timer lsp-refresh command in the IS-IS view to increase the value of the LSP refresh timer, and then run the display isis lsdb command to view the sequence number of the LSP generated by the local device. If the sequence number increases normally, go to step 5. If the sequence number still increases too fast, go to step 3. 3. Check whether there is a device whose system ID conflicts with the local system ID in the domain.
parameters: isisSysInstance::Indicates the IS-IS process ID. | isisSysLevelIndex::Indicates the IS-IS level. | isisPduLspId::Indicates the LSP ID. | thresholdVal::The upper threshold value of LSP sequence Number

impact_on_system: Cause 1: A patch package running on a board was damaged. If the patch package is damaged, the LPU or SFU may fail to start. Cause 2: A patch package running on a board was damaged. An exception may occur when the device is running or restarted.

procedure: Cause 1: A patch package running on a board was damaged. 1. Run the display device command to check whether the patch package on the slave main control board is damaged. If so, run the reset slot <slot-id> command to restart the board to automatically fix the patch package. If not, go to step 2. 2. Run the display device command to check whether only the patch package on the master MPU is damaged. If so, run the slave switchover command in the system view to perform a master/slave main control board switchover if conditions permit and services are not affected. If not, go to step 3. 3. If the active/standby switchover cannot be performed or the patch packages on all boards are damaged, the alarm persists until you run the patch load <file-name>all run command to load the patch package of the next version to clear the alarm. If the alarm persists, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information and contact technical support. Cause 2: A patch package running on a board was damaged. 1. Run patch load <file-name> all run to load the patch package of the next version to clear the alarm. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.

description: Static CR-LSP went Down. (LspIndex=[LspIndex], InSegmentIndex=[InSegmentIndex], OutSegmentIndex=[OutSegmentIndex], OutIfIndex=[OutIfIndex], LspName=[LspName], LspStatus=[LspStatus], OutIfName=[OutIfName], InIfIndex=[InIfIndex], InIfName=[InIfName], DownReason=[DownReason]) The trap message was sent when the bandwidth of the tunnel changed.
impact_on_system: If there is some service using the tunnel, the service is interrupted. If there is a backup path is used to protect the tunnel, the flow of the service is changed to the backup path. If there is not any service using the tunnel, there is no impact.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Others Cause 3: MPLS disabled on an interface Cause 4: MPLS TE disabled on an interface Cause 5: Route change Cause 6: Tunnel binding associated with the CR-LSP deleted Cause 8: Inbound interface Down Cause 9: Outbound interface Down Cause 10: Tunnel associated with the static CR-LSP has been shut down Cause 11: Static CR-LSP configuration update Cause 12: The bound ring is invalid
procedure: Cause 1: Others 1. Run the display mpls interface command. If the alarm is generated on the ingress of static CR-LSPs, you need to check the information about only the outbound interface; if the alarm is generated on the egress of static CR-LSPs, you need to check the information about only the inbound interface; if the alarm is generated on the transit of static LSPs, you need to check the information about the outbound interface and inbound interface. You need to check whether the corresponding interface is displayed in the command output, whether the Status field of the interface is Up, and whether the TE Attr field is En. If the interface status is not Up, check the interface. If the MPLS or MPLS TE is not enabled, configure this function. If the alarm is generated on the ingress, egress, or a transit node, go to Step 2. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 5. If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display current-configuration interface tunnel <interface-number> command on the ingress to check whether the corresponding tunnel is correctly configured. If the tunnel configuration is correct, go to Step 3. If the tunnel is not consistent with the destination address of the static CR-LSP, you need to enter the corresponding tunnel view and run the destination command to modify the destination address of the tunnel. If the signaling mode is not cr-static, run the mpls te signal-protocol cr-static command to modify the signaling mode of the tunnel. After modifying the configuration of the tunnel, run the commit command to commit the modification. 3. If the static CR-LSP is configured with the bandwidth attribute, run the display current-configuration interface interface-number command to check the maximal bandwidth and the maximal reservable bandwidth on the outbound interface. If neither preceding operations can locate the fault, go to Step 4. If the available bandwidth of the outbound interface is smaller than the bandwidth required by the static CR-LSP, you need to enter the corresponding interface view and run the mpls te bandwidth max-reservable-bandwidth command to increase the bandwidth of the outbound interface. After modifying the configuration of the tunnel, run the commit command to commit the modification. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 5. If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 3: MPLS disabled on an interface The same as Cause 1. Cause 4: MPLS TE disabled on an interface The same as Cause 1. Cause 5: Route change The same as Cause 1. Cause 6: Tunnel binding associated with the CR-LSP deleted The same as Cause 1. Cause 8: Inbound interface Down The same as Cause 1. Cause 9: Outbound interface Down The same as Cause 1. Cause 10: Tunnel associated with the static CR-LSP has been shut down The same as Cause 1. Cause 11: Static CR-LSP configuration update The same as Cause 1. Cause 12: The bound ring is invalid The same as Cause 1.
parameters: LspIndex::Indicates the index of the LSP. | InSegmentIndex::Indicates the inSegment index of a static CR-LSP. | OutSegmentIndex::Indicates the outSegment index of a static CR-LSP. | OutIfIndex::Indicates the outbound interface index of a static CR-LSP. | LspName::Indicates the name of a static CR-LSP. | LspStatus::Indicates the status of a static CR-LSP. | OutIfName::Indicates the outbound interface name of a static CR-LSP. | InIfIndex::Indicates the inbound interface index of a static CR-LSP. | InIfName::Indicates the inbound interface name a static CR-LSP. | DownReason::Indicates the reason that the static CR-LSP down.

In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: A service switchover or interruption will occur.
possible_causes: Cause 0: The optical fiber was disconnected. Cause 1: The optical loss was beyond the normal range. Cause 2: The remote device failed to send the optical signal. Cause 3: The cross-connect board of the remote device failed, was not installed, or was not installed properly. Cause 4: The clock board of the remote device failed.
procedure: 1.Check whether any optical fiber is connected to the optical interface. If no optical fiber is used, shut down the laser of the optical interface and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 2.Check whether the optical fiber is broken. If the optical fiber is broken, replace the optical fiber and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 3.Check whether the receive optical power of the local device is less than the minimum value. If the receive optical power is less than the minimum value, clean the optical fiber connector and the optical interface on the interface board. Check that the flange and the optical attenuator are properly connected and the optical attenuator value is in the normal range. Then check whether the alarm is cleared.
parameters: hwPhysicalPortIfIndex::Index of the physical port. | hwPhysicalPortInSlot::Slot ID. | hwPhysicalPortInCard::Card ID. | hwPhysicalPortInPort::Port ID. | hwPhysicalPortName::Name of physical port.

description: The OSPF prefix-sid conflict is detected. (ProcessId=[hwProcessId], PrefixSid=[hwPrefixSid], PrefixAddress=[hwPrefixAddress], PrefixAddressMask=[hwPrefixAddressMask], Algorithm=[hwAlgorithm], ConflictType=[hwConflictType]) An OSPF prefix SID conflict was detected.
impact_on_system: The conflicting route is not used by the SR. If a prefix conflict occurs, the system selects only one prefix and ignores the same prefix advertised by other devices. If a SID conflict occurs, the system selects only one SID and ignores the same SIDs advertised by other devices.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The configuration is incorrect. Cause 2: The SID of the flexible algorithm configured on a LoopBack interface is the same as that configured on another device. Cause 3: This device is an OSPF ABR, and the LoopBack interfaces of other devices in different areas are configured with the same SID for the same flexible algorithm.
procedure: 1. If an OSPF prefix SID conflict occurs, run the display ospf routing command to check the routing entry corresponding to the conflicting prefix. If the value of the Type field is Direct, the local device is the conflicting prefix advertisement source. Otherwise, the conflicting prefix advertisement source is the device identified by the AdverRouter field. You need to run the ospf prefix-sid command on the advertisement source device to modify the SID configuration. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support engineers.
parameters: hwProcessId::Process ID | hwPrefixSid::Prefix SID | hwPrefixAddress::Prefix address | hwPrefixAddressMask::Prefix mask | hwAlgorithm::Flexible algorithm (128-255) | hwConflictType::1. SID conflict 2. Prefix conflict

description: All the configured authentication or accounting servers in the RADIUS server group are down. (GroupName=[GroupName],ServerType=[ServerType]) Communication with all authentication or accounting servers in the RADIUS server group is interrupted. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The server is unreachable, and users fail to go online.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The route between the device and the configed RADIUS server was unreachable or the RADIUS server did not respond to the request of the device within the timeout period Cause 2: Delete servers in the RADIUS server group. After the servers are deleted, the communication of all the authentication or accounting servers is interrupted, and an alarm is triggered. After the servers are deleted, no authentication or accounting server exists in the RADIUS server group, and an alarm is triggered.
procedure: Cause 1: The route between the device and the configed RADIUS server was unreachable or the RADIUS server did not respond to the request of the device within the timeout period 1. Run the ping command to check whether the RADIUS server is reachable. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display interface command to check whether the interface is Up. If so, go to Step 3. If not, check the physical link connection and ensure that the physical link connection is normal. 3. Run the display current-configuration command to check whether the RADIUS server configuration on the device is correct. If so, go to Step 4. If not, modify the configuration of the RADIUS server according to the Configuration Guide. 4. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 2: Delete servers in the RADIUS server group. After the servers are deleted, the communication of all the authentication or accounting servers is interrupted, and an alarm is triggered. After the servers are deleted, no authentication or accounting server exists in the RADIUS server group, and an alarm is triggered. For details, see the recovery suggestion for cause 1. Configure a normal RADIUS server in the RADIUS server group.
parameters: GroupName::RADIUS server group name. | ServerType::RADIUS server type.

If the discard rate field is not 0, congestion occurs on a member interface. Go to step 3. If no member interface is congested or you cannot confirm the congestion, go to step 4. 3. Perform any of the following operations based on service requirements:

description: The clock-class of input time source is below threshold. The input of the time source deteriorated. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The clock level of the current synchronization source deteriorated.
possible_causes: Cause1: If the device uses the fragmented packets on a PTP input interface to obtain the time reference source, the clock class of the current PTP reference source is lower than a specified SSM threshold, and the value of stepsRemoved is 0 for the PTP reference source. Cause 5: RSVP-TE LSP resources were preempted. Cause 6: Transmission of an RSVP message timed out. Cause 7: RSVP Hello mechanism detected a downstream node failure. Cause 8: The bypass tunnel in use was Down or unbound from the primary tunnel. Cause 9: CSPF failed to calculate a path. Cause 10: The tunnel was manually shut down.
procedure: Cause 1: Others Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 2: A static LSP went Down. 1. Check whether the configurations for the current tunnel interface, RSVP, an IGP, link connectivity, and bandwidth for links along the tunnel are correct. If a configuration is incorrect, correct the configuration and commit the new configuration. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 5. If not go to Step 4. If all configurations are correct and the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display mpls te tunnel-interface last-error command to check error information, and deal with the problem according to the error information. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display mpls lsp statistics command to check whether the number of LSPs exceeds the upper limit. If the number of LSPs exceeds the upper limit, delete unwanted LSPs and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 5. If the alarm persists, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 3: A static CR-LSP went Down. The same as Cause 2. Cause 4: The outbound interface of an RSVP-TE LSP's ingress went Down. 1. Check the configuration and status of the current tunnel interface. If the outbound interface is incorrectly configured, reconfigure it correctly. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 3.End. Cause 5: RSVP-TE LSP resources were preempted. 1. Change the setup and holding priorities on the tunnel interface.Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 3.End. Cause 6: Transmission of an RSVP message timed out. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 7: RSVP Hello mechanism detected a downstream node failure. 1. Check configurations and statues of all downstream nodes of the ingress. Correct the configuration if there is an error. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 3.End. Cause 8: The bypass tunnel in use was Down or unbound from the primary tunnel. 1. Run the display mpls te tunnel-interface command to check the status of the bypass tunnel. If a problem occurs, solve it and Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display mpls te tunnel verbose command to check the binding between the primary and bypass tunnel. If a problem occurs, solve it. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 4.End. Cause 9: CSPF failed to calculate a path. 1. CSPF is enabled on the ingress but CSPF fails to calculate a path for the tunnel. Check whether configurations for explicit paths are correct, whether MPLS TE has been enabled for the IGP, and whether routing configurations are correct. If a configuration is incorrect, correct the configuration and commit the new configuration. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 3. If not go to Step 2. If all configurations are correct and the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 3. End. Cause 10: The tunnel was manually shut down. 1. Run the undo shutdown command in the tunnel interface view.Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 3.End.
parameters: SessionTunnelId::Indicates the ID of the tunnel. | TunnelInstIndex::Indicates the InstIndex of the tunnel. | IngressLsrId::Indicates the LSR ID of the ingress on the tunnel. | EgressLsrId::Indicates the LSR ID of the egress on the tunnel. | mplsTunnelIfName::Indicates the name of a tunnel. | hwMplsTunnelDownReason::Indicates the reason why a tunnel goes Down. | hwMplsTunnelDownLSRId::Indicates the LSR ID of the error node on a tunnel. | hwMplsTunnelDownIfAddrType::Indicates the IP address type of the error interface on a tunnel. | hwMplsTunnelDownIfAddr::Indicates the IP address of the error interface on a tunnel. | SignalledTunnelName::Tunnel alias.

description: The state of interface changed from unsuppress to suppress. (InterfaceName=[InterfaceName], SuppressState=[SuppressState]) After the physical status flapping suppression function is enabled, the interface enters the suppression state from the non-suppression state.

procedure: 1. This alarm indicates that the physical interface is unstable because the optical fiber of the physical interface is intermittently disconnected. As a result, the interface frequently alternates between up and down states. If the physical link is abnormal, check the physical link status (including whether the network cable and optical module are loose or disconnected). Reconnect the physical link and check whether the alarm is cleared. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel.
parameters: InterfaceName::Interface name | SuppressState::Interface suppression status: 0: The interface is not suppressed. 1: The interface is suppressed.

Run the display mac-address-usage command to check whether the MAC address usage alarm threshold configured on the board is smaller than or equal to the actual MAC address usage on the board. If the configured alarm threshold is smaller than or equal to the actual MAC address usage, go to Step 3. procedure: 1. Increase the soft pipe bandwidth or reduce the number of services deployed on the soft pipe, and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 3. description: The payload no-matching alarm in the higher order path. Cause 3: The remote device failed to send the optical signal. Cause 4: The cross-connect board of the remote device failed, was not installed, or was not installed properly. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 2. Check whether the optical fiber is broken. If the optical fiber is broken, replace the optical fiber and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 3. Check whether the receive optical power of the local device is less than the minimum value. If the receive optical power is less than the minimum value, clean the optical fiber connector and the optical interface on the interface board. Check that the flange and the optical attenuator are properly connected and the optical attenuator value is in the normal range. Then check whether the alarm is cleared.
parameters: hwPhysicalPortIfIndex::Index of physical port. | hwPhysicalPortInSlot::Slot ID. | hwPhysicalPortInCard::Card ID. | hwPhysicalPortInPort::Port ID. | hwSDHHpPerfCurrentHpIndex::High-order path ID. | hwPhysicalPortName::Name of physical port.

description: The root bridge role flapped. (ProcessID=[ProcessID], InstanceID=[InstanceID]) The root bridge role flapped for a non-root bridge device.

If the root bridge information in multiple copies of BPDU packets is inconsistent, the root bridge flaps and the MSTP network reconverges. When the count of root flaps up to 10 in 5 minutes, the alarm will be triggered.
procedure: 1. Check MSTP logs to determine whether alarms indicating frequent intermittent Down events are reported on the ports or port priorities are frequently changed. If yes, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 3. 2. Deploy the network topology correctly and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, no action is required. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Check MSTP logs to determine the source of BPDUs on the ports and identify the flapping source.
parameters: ProcessID::Process ID | InstanceID::Instance ID

description: A device anti-theft lock alarm was generated. (Reason=[ReasonDesc]) The anti-theft function of the device is locked. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The device anti-theft function is not authorized for a long time, and the grace period has expired. The device configuration control policy is as follows: The current configuration cannot be modified, the configuration file for next startup cannot be specified, and the current configuration file cannot be modified. The device cannot be replaced with a version that does not support anti-theft through a command or through a console port. The version cannot be changed by running commands.
possible_causes: The anti-theft grace period has expired and the device enters the anti-theft lock state.
procedure: 1. Use the NMS to authorize the device anti-theft function online. Alternatively, export a temporary authorization file from the NMS anti-theft page, upload the file to the device, and run the anti-theft install authorization file <filename> command on the device to perform temporary authorization. After the authorization, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 3. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 3. End.
parameters: ReasonDesc::Alarm cause.
