description: The board temperature was abnormal. (EntityPhysicalIndex=[EntityPhysicalIndex],EntPhysicalIndex=[EntPhysicalIndex],EntPhysicalName=[EntityPhysicalName],EntityThresholdType=[EntThresholdType],EntityThresholdWarning=[EntityThresholdWarning],EntityThresholdCurrent=[EntThresholdCurrent],EntityTrapFaultID=143617,Reason=The board temperature was too high.) The board or subcard temperature alarm. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Services will not be affected, but a speedy solution is required.
possible_causes: The board temperature was too high.
procedure: 1. Check if there are idle slots without filler panels on the device. If there are idle slots without filler panels, install filler panels to cover these slots. 2. Check if the filter screen of the fan module is clogged. If the filter screen is clogged, clean the filter screen. 3. Check the ambient temperature. If the ambient temperature is too high, reduce the temperature to a normal level. 4. Check if the fan module is faulty. If there is a fault on the fan module, rectify the fault first. 5. If the ambient temperature is normal but the alarm is still reported, the possible cause is that the module temperature is too high. In this case, collect the information about alarms, logs, and configurations, and then contact technical support personnel.
parameters: EntityPhysicalIndex::Indicates the index of the physical entity. | EntPhysicalIndex::Indicates the index of the physical entity. | EntityTrapFaultID::To describe the fault id of trap. | Reason::Indicates the description of the cause of the trap. | EntityPhysicalName::Indicates the name of the physical entity, such as "SFU | LPU | MPU slot <slotID>". The entity name varies according to the board type, such as the SFU, LPU, and MPU. | EntThresholdType::Indicates the alarm type. The following values: 1: High temperature. 2: Low temperature. | EntityThresholdWarning::Indicates the alarm threshold. | EntThresholdCurrent::The current value that been measured.

description: The number of AS-external LSAs generated when an OSPFv3 process imports external routes exceeds the maximum number. (hwOspfv3ProcessId=[hwOspfv3ProcessId], hwOspfv3MaxLimit=[hwOspfv3MaxLimit]) The number of ASE LSAs generated when an OSPFv3 process imported external routes reached or exceeded the maximum number allowed.
impact_on_system: The network stability may be adversely affected.
possible_causes: The number of ASE LSAs generated when an OSPFv3 process imported external routes reached or exceeded the maximum number allowed.
procedure: 1. Run the display ospfv3 command to check whether the number of ASE LSAs generated when an OSPFv3 process imported external routes reaches or exceeds the maximum number allowed. If the number reaches or exceeds the maximum number allowed, this trap message is informational only and no action is required. If the number has not reached or exceeded the maximum number allowed, go to Step 2. Check the overload status based on the value of the Current status field in the display ospfv3 command output. Normal: The number of LSAs generated when an OSPFv3 process imports external routes is less than or equal to the lower alarm threshold (in percentage) multiplied by the maximum number allowed. Approach limit: The number of LSAs generated when an OSPFv3 process imports external routes is approaching (reaching or exceeding 90% of) the upper alarm threshold. Exceed limit: The number of LSAs generated when an OSPFv3 process imports external routes has reached or exceeded the maximum number allowed. 2. Perform the following operations as required: If a change in the limit on the number of ASE LSAs is allowed, run the import-route limit <limit-number> [ threshold-alarm upper-limit <upper-limit-value> lower-limit <lower-limit-value> ] command to change the limit. If a change in the limit on the number of ASE LSAs is not allowed, go to Step 3.
parameters: hwOspfv3ProcessId::OSPFv3 process ID | hwOspfv3MaxLimit::Limit on the maximum number of ASE LSAs

If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 2.Check whether the optical fiber is broken. If the optical fiber is broken, replace the optical fiber and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 3.Check whether the receive optical power of the local device is less than the minimum value. If the receive optical power is less than the minimum value, clean the optical fiber connector and the optical interface on the interface board. Check that the flange and the optical attenuator are properly connected and the optical attenuator value is in the normal range. Then check whether the alarm is cleared.

description: The number of DCN serial interfaces has reached the maximum value. (Number=[Number]) The number of DCN serial interfaces reached the upper limit. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The system will not be affected.
possible_causes: When the number of DCN serial interfaces reached the upper limit, a corresponding alarm was generated.

Delete unnecessary DCN interfaces and adjust the number of DCN serial interfaces to be within the normal range. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to step 4. If no, go to step 3. 3. description: Current lock status of clock frequency synchronization failed. (hwPtpFreqLockStatus=[hwPtpFreqLockStatus]) The frequency was out of lock. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The clock frequency fails to be locked.
possible_causes: Cause 1: During frequency synchronization based on synchronous Ethernet, the reference frequency source has an excessive frequency deviation. Cause 2: During frequency synchronization based on IEEE 1588v2, timestamps are incorrect. Cause 3: The DSP internal frequency control word exceeds +/-10 ppm. Cause 4: The board hardware is faulty.
procedure: 1. Run the display clock source command to check whether the clock synchronization source is a PTP source. Specifically, check whether the value of the current system trace source is PTP. If yes, the fault is caused by Cause 1. Go to Step 2. If not, the fault is caused by Cause 2. Go to Step 3. 2. Run the display current-configuration command to check whether PTP-related configurations are changed. If so, reconfigure PTP attributes on the local end. For details, see 1588v2 Configuration in the Configuration Guide. If not, go to Step 4. 3. Run the display clock config command to check whether the clock source configurations are correct.
parameters: hwPtpFreqLockStatus::Clock frequency locking status. The values are as follows: unlock(0). lock(1).

description: Configuration backup failed in the system. (reason=[cause]) The system configuration fails to be backed up.
impact_on_system: Cause 0: Backup failed due to no enough disk space. Data cannot be synchronized between the active and standby boards. Data is inconsistent between these two boards. Cause 1: Checkpoint backup failed. Data cannot be synchronized between the active and standby boards, and the rollback point files on the active and standby boards are inconsistent. Cause 2: Configuration file backup failed due to disk damage.Please save the configuration. File backup is not supported. As a result, configuration files, rollback point files, or other files may be lost or become inconsistent.
possible_causes: Cause 0: Backup failed due to no enough disk space. Cause 1: Checkpoint backup failed. Cause 2: Configuration file backup failed due to disk damage.Please save the configuration.
procedure: Cause 0: Backup failed due to no enough disk space. 1. Run the delete command to delete unnecessary files from the home directory on the slave main control board to release space on the slave main control board. Then, run the reset slot <slotId> command to reset the slave main control board to trigger configuration backup. If yes, go to Step 3. If the operation fails, go to step 2. 2. Collect log and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End Cause 1: Checkpoint backup failed. 1. Run the delete command to delete unnecessary files from the home directory on the slave main control board to release space on the slave main control board. Then, run the reset slot <slotId> command to reset the slave main control board to trigger configuration backup. If yes, go to Step 3. If the operation fails, go to step 2. 2. Collect log and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End Cause 2: Configuration file backup failed due to disk damage.Please save the configuration. 1. Run the slave switchover command to perform an active/standby switchover and replace the main control board with the faulty disk. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to step 3. If no, go to step 2. 2. Collect log and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End.
parameters: cause::Failure Cause

description: An OSPF IP address conflict between the local device and another device was detected. (ProcessId=[hwOspfv2ProcessIdIndex], Area=[hwOspfv2AreaId], ConflictType=[hwOspfv2ConflictType], Conflict IP=[hwOspfv2ConflictIp], Conflict Router=[hwOspfv2ConflictRouterId], Conflict Router2=[hwOspfv2ConflictRouterId2]) The interface address used by the local device to establish an OSPF IPv4 neighbor relationship conflicts with the interface address sent by another device. If the source IP address of a Hello packet received from a directly connected interface is the same as the IP address of the local interface, an IP address conflict alarm with hwOspfv2ConflictType being Direct is generated. If two router LSAs exist in the LSDB and the carried link information (link data of P2P links and transit links and link IDs of stub links) has the same IP address, an IP address conflict alarm with hwOspfv2ConflictType being Intra-Area is triggered.
impact_on_system: If the IP addresses of interfaces on some devices are the same, routes are incorrectly calculated or route flapping occurs, affecting services.
possible_causes: The IP address of a device on the OSPF network is the same as the IP address of the local interface used to establish a neighbor relationship.
procedure: 1. Determine the conflicting OSPF process, router ID, conflict type, conflicting IP address, and conflicting device based on the alarm information. 2. Run the undo ip address command to delete the OSPF IP address of the conflicting device. 3. Replan the IP address of the OSPF process on the device to ensure that the IP address is unique on the network. 4. Run the ip address command to configure a new IP address and check whether the alarm is cleared. If no, collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. If yes, no further action is required.
parameters: hwOspfv2ProcessIdIndex::OSPF process ID. | hwOspfv2AreaId::ID of an OSPF area. | hwOspfv2ConflictType::Conflict type. Currently, the following types are supported: Direct Intra-Area | hwOspfv2ConflictIp::Conflicting IP address. | hwOspfv2ConflictRouterId::Conflicting router ID. | hwOspfv2ConflictRouterId2::Second conflicting router ID.

description: The CRC error is rising. (hwIfMonitorIndex=[hwIfMonitorIndex],hwIfMonitorCrcErrorStatistics=[hwIfMonitorCrcErrorStatistics],hwIfMonitorCrcErrorThreshold=[hwIfMonitorCrcErrorThreshold],hwIfMonitorCrcErrorInterval=[hwIfMonitorCrcErrorInterval],hwIfMonitorName=[hwIfMonitorName]) The CRC error is rising. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Some service data on the interface where the alarm was generated will be lost.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Transmission distances of optical modules on two directly connected devices were inconsistent with actual transmission distances. As a result, the input optical power of the devices was either too high or too low, causing error codes or packets over the link. Cause 2: The connector or extension component (such as a flange or concentrator) on the direct cable or link was not connected securely, causing error codes or packets over the link. Cause 3: The direct optical fiber or cable was not connected securely with devices on both ends, causing error codes or packets over the link. Cause 4: The direct optical module or power module was not connected securely with devices on both ends, causing error codes or packets over the link. Cause 5: The transmission network was faulty, causing routers to receive error codes or packets. Cause 6: The connector or extension component (such as a flange or concentrator) on the direct cable or link aged, causing error codes or packets over the link. Cause 7: The configurations of interconnected physical layer devices were inconsistent, causing error codes or packets over the link.
procedure: 1.Check that the optical fiber is connected properly. Run the display this interface command in the interface view to check the interface status. If the interface is Up, go to Step 2. If the interface is Down, go to End. 2.Check the optical receive power in the display this interface command output. If the optical receive power is within the allowed range, go to Step 3. If the optical receive power is not in the allowed range, go to End. 3.Check the link protocol, clock mode and scramble of the local device in the display this interface command output. Then check whether they are consistent with those of the peer device.
parameters: hwIfMonitorIndex::Index of physical port. | hwIfMonitorCrcErrorStatistics::CRC error statistics value. | hwIfMonitorCrcErrorThreshold::CRC error alarm threshold. | hwIfMonitorCrcErrorInterval::Indicates the CRC configuration interval, in seconds. | hwIfMonitorName::Name of physical port.

description: Failed to restore system configurations.(Result=[Result]) System configurations failed to be restored.
impact_on_system: The configuration database fails to be restored. As a result, the configuration information of the existing services is lost.
possible_causes: Cause 0: The configuration database file was lost or damaged.
procedure: Cause 0: The configuration database file was lost or damaged. 1. Run the display configuration recover-result command to check the commands that fail to be restored. Check whether the commands in the configuration file are in correct format or executed in a correct view. If not, go to step 2. If so, go to step 5. 2. Re-configure the commands that fail to be restored. If the alarm persists, go to step 4. If the alarm is not generated, go to step 5. 3. Run the display startup command to check whether the current startup version is as expected. If not, run the check system-software XX.cc command to check whether the basic software package (XX.cc) of the expected startup version is normal. If the XX.cc package is abnormal, delete it, upload a correct basic software package, and complete the upgrade in the operation time window. If the XX.cc package is normal, perform the upgrade in the operation time window. If the upgrade fails, go to step 4. If the upgrade is successful, go to step 2. 4. Collect log and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 5. End.
parameters: Result::Configuration restoration result.

description: ISIS adjacency state change. (SysInstance=[IsisSysInstance], SysLevel=[IsisSysLevelIndex], CircIndex=[IsisCircIndex], CircIfIndex=[IsisCircIfIndex], LspId=[IsisPduLspId], AdjState=[IsisAdjState], IfIndex=[IfIndex], IfName=[IfName], Reason=[HwIsisAdjChgReason], SubReason=[HwIsisAdjChgSubReason]) The IS-IS adjacency state changed.
impact_on_system: IS-IS may re-calculate routes, which causes route flapping and interrupts the IS-IS service.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The adjacency HoldTimer expired Cause 2: The physical interface went Down Cause 3: Protocol reason Cause 4: BFD detected that the neighbor went Down Cause 5: Configurations changed Cause 6: Peer router reason
procedure: Cause 1: The adjacency HoldTimer expired 1. Run the ping command to check whether the link to the peer device is normal. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 4. 2. Run the display current-configuration configuration isis command to check whether the IS-IS configuration of the peer device is correct. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 5. 3. Run the display cpu-usage command to check whether the CPU usage is too high. If so, go to Step 6. If not, go to Step 7. 4. Check the link configuration and go to Step 7. 5. Modify the configuration according to the IS-IS protocol and check whether the neighbor status is Up. If so, go to Step 8. If not, go to Step 7. 6. Run the display current-configuration command to check device configurations, delete unnecessary configurations, and check whether the neighbor status is Up. If so, go to Step 8. If not, go to Step 7. 7. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 8. End. Cause 2: The physical interface went Down 1. Run the display isis interface command to check whether the interface status is Down. If so, go to step 2. If not, go to step 3. 2. Modify the configuration and check whether the interface status changes to Up. If yes, go to Step 4. If not, go to step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 3: Protocol reason 1. Run the display current-configuration command to check whether the local configuration is correct. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Modify the local configuration and check whether the neighbor status changes to Up. If so, go to Step 6. If not, go to Step 5. 3. Run the display cpu-usage command to check whether the CPU usage is too high. If so, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 5. 4. Delete unnecessary configurations and check whether the neighbor relationship is Up. If so, go to Step 6. If not, go to Step 5. 5. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 6. End. Cause 4: BFD detected that the neighbor went Down 1. Run the ping command to check whether the link to the peer device is in the normal state. If yes, go to Step 3. If not, go to step 2. 2. Check the link configuration. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 5: Configurations changed 1. Check whether a modified configuration affects the neighbor relationship establishment. If so, go to step 2. If not, go to step 4. 2. Check whether the configuration modification is expected. If so, go to step 5. If not, go to step 3. 3. Restore the configurations, and then check whether the neighbor is Up. If so, go to step 5. If not, go to step 4. 4. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 6: Peer router reason 1. Check whether the configuration on the remote device is correct. If so, go to step 2. If not, go to step 3. 2. Rectify the fault on the peer device and check whether the neighbor relationship is Up. If yes, go to Step 4. If not, go to step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End.
parameters: IsisSysInstance::Indicates the IS-IS process ID. | IsisSysLevelIndex::IS-IS neighbor type. 1: Level-1 2: Level-2 3: Level-1-2 | IsisCircIndex::Sequence number of an IS-IS internal interface, starting from 1. | IsisCircIfIndex::Interface index in an IS-IS process. The value is equal to IfIndex. | IsisPduLspId::Specifies the LSP ID. | IsisAdjState::Indicates the status of a neighbor. 1:Down 2:Init 3:Up 4:Fail | IfIndex::Global interface index of the device. | IfName::Indicates the interface name. | HwIsisAdjChgReason::Reason for the status change of the IS-IS adjacency. When the Reason parameter is The alarm was cleared, the trap indicates that an alarm has been cleared. The other values of the Reason parameter indicate that an alarm has been generated. | HwIsisAdjChgSubReason::Indicates the detailed reason why the neighbor status changes. 1: Adjacency state go to Up 2: Delete adjacency 3: Delete interface 4: Interface silent 5: Received invalid hello packet 6: Hello packet authentication failed 7: SystemID in hello conflict with local or different with adj 8: Maximum area number mismatch with local 9: Area Mismatch 10: Adjacency HoldTimer Expired 11: Interface state go to down

description: Mac-hopping exist. (VlanId=[VlanId], Vsi=[vsi_name], BDId=[BD_ID], the port list of Mac-hopping = [PortName1], [PortName2], [PortName3], [PortName4], the peer list of Mac-hopping = [PeerList], DetectMac = [DetectMac], trustport = [TrustPortName], trustpeer = [TrustPeerInfo]) MAC address flapping occurred. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: 1. A loop occurs on the Layer 2 network, a broadcast storm occurs on the loop, the Layer 3 device connected to the Layer 2 loop is affected by the broadcast storm, and a large number of broadcast packets are continuously sent to impact the CPU of the Layer 3 device. As a result, the control plane of the board is overloaded, affecting the processing of other protocol packets and normal running of the board. 2. After MAC address flapping is enabled, some interfaces are blocked.
possible_causes: MAC address transition frequently occurred in the broadcast domain. A Layer 2 loop may exist.
procedure: 1. Check the configuration of the interface where MAC address flapping occurs and check whether the loop is caused by incorrect configuration. (You can run the display loop-detect eth-loop hop-info command to view the detailed flapping interface list.) 2. If configurations are correct, check whether the interface where the MAC address flapping occurs is properly connected and whether the loop is caused by incorrect connection. 3. Run the loop-detect eth-loop command to enable MAC flapping detection and block the corresponding interface. 4. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support.
parameters: VlanId::VLAN ID of the broadcast domain. | vsi_name::Name of a VSI. | BD_ID::BD ID. | PortName1::Interface on which MAC address flapping occurred. | PortName2::Interface on which MAC address flapping occurred. | PortName3::Interface on which MAC address flapping occurred. | PortName4::Interface on which MAC address flapping occurred. | PeerList::Information about the peer with MAC address flapping. | DetectMac::Detected MAC address. | TrustPortName::Trusted port | TrustPeerInfo::Trusted peer

description: The trace identifier unstable in the higher order path alarm. (hwPhysicalPortIfIndex=[hwPhysicalPortIfIndex],SlotID=[hwPhysicalPortInSlot],CardID=[hwPhysicalPortInCard],PortID=[hwPhysicalPortInPort],HpID=[hwSDHHpPerfCurrentHpIndex],InterfaceName=[hwPhysicalPortName]) The trace identifier unstable in the higher order path alarm.
impact_on_system: A service switchover or interruption will occur.
possible_causes: Cause 0: The optical fiber was broken. Cause 1: The optical loss was beyond the normal range. Cause 2: The remote device failed to send the optical signal. Cause 3: The cross-connect board of the remote device failed, was not installed, or was not installed properly. Cause 4: The clock board of the remote device failed.
procedure: 1.Check whether any optical fiber is connected to the optical interface. If no optical fiber is used, shut down the laser of the optical interface and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 2.Check whether the optical fiber is broken. If the optical fiber is broken, replace the optical fiber and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 3.Check whether the receive optical power of the local device is less than the minimum value. If the receive optical power is less than the minimum value, clean the optical fiber connector and the optical interface on the interface board. Check that the flange and the optical attenuator are properly connected and the optical attenuator value is in the normal range. Then check whether the alarm is cleared.
parameters: hwPhysicalPortIfIndex::Index of physical port. | hwPhysicalPortInSlot::Slot ID. | hwPhysicalPortInCard::Card ID. | hwPhysicalPortInPort::Port ID. | hwSDHHpPerfCurrentHpIndex::High-order path ID. | hwPhysicalPortName::Name of physical port.

Run the display this command in the interface view to check whether the local or remote interface is shut down. If either interface is shut down, run the undo shutdown command to enable the interface, and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step 2. If no interface is shut down, go to Step 2. 2. Check whether the physical link of the interface works improperly. If the physical link works improperly, you need to correctly connect the physical link and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step 3. If the physical link works properly, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display interface eth-trunk command in the system view to check whether a local or remote interface is removed from an Eth-Trunk. If the interface is incorrectly removed from the Eth-Trunk, run the eth-trunk command in the member interface view or the trunkport command in the Eth-Trunk interface view to re-add the interface to the Eth-Trunk, and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step 4. If the interface is correctly removed from the Eth-Trunk, go to Step 4. 4. Collect the alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 2: The remote system MAC address in the received LACPDU was the same as the local system MAC address. 1. Check whether the interface is a loopback interface. If the interface is a loopback interface, go to Step 2. If the interface is not a loopback interface, go to step 3. 2. Clear the loopback configuration and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to step 3. 3. Collect the alarm, log, and configuration information and contact Huawei technical support. 4. End.

description: The primary LSP of the tunnel changes to Down. (SessionTunnelId=[SessionTunnelId], TunnelInstIndex=[TunnelInstIndex], IngressLsrId=[IngressLsrId], EgressLsrId=[EgressLsrId], mplsTunnelIfName=[mplsTunnelIfName], hwMplsTunnelDownReason=[hwMplsTunnelDownReason], hwMplsTunnelDownLSRId=[hwMplsTunnelDownLSRId], hwMplsTunnelDownIfAddrType=[hwMplsTunnelDownIfAddrType], hwMplsTunnelDownIfAddr=[hwMplsTunnelDownIfAddr], SignalledTunnelName=[SignalledTunnelName]) The primary LSP of the tunnel changes to Down.
impact_on_system: If traffic is not forwarded along the primary LSP of the tunnel, traffic forwarding will not be affected. If traffic is forwarded along the primary LSP of the tunnel and a backup LSP is configured, traffic will be switched to the backup LSP. If not, traffic forwarding will be interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Others Cause 2: A static LSP went Down. Cause 3: A static CR-LSP went Down. Cause 4: The outbound interface of an RSVP-TE LSP's ingress went Down. Cause 5: RSVP-TE LSP resources were preempted. Cause 6: Transmission of an RSVP message timed out. Cause 7: RSVP Hello mechanism detected a downstream node failure. Cause 8: The bypass tunnel in use was Down or unbound from the primary tunnel. Cause 9: CSPF failed to calculate a path. Cause 10: The tunnel was manually shut down.
procedure: Cause 1: Others 1. Run the display mpls te tunnel-interface <tunnel-name> command on the ingress (that is, the node that generates the trap) to check the configurations of the tunnel. View the Tunnel State Desc field to check whether the tunnel is in the Down state Then, run the display mpls te tunnel-interface last-error command to view the prompt. In the case of the following error prompts, do as required: If the error prompt is "Cspf failed to calculate a path for Tunnel." (indicating that the ingress is enabled with CSPF, but the CSPF path calculation fails), go to Step 2. If the error prompt is "Trigger Rsvp failed", go to Step 2. If the error prompt is "One LSP is deleted at smooth period", go to Step 6. If the error prompt is "One LSP is deleted at Tunnel aging period", go to Step 6. For other types of errors, go to Step 6. If there is no error prompt, go to Step 2. 2. Run the ping command on the ingress to check whether the destination IP address of the tunnel can be pinged. If the ping fails, rectify the route fault to ensure that the destination IP address of the tunnel can be pinged, and then check whether the alarm MPLS_LSPM_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.121.2.1.46 hwMplsTunnelPrimaryUp is generated. If so, go to Step 7. If not, go to Step 3. If the ping is successful, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display this command in the MPLS view of the ingress to check whether the mpls te cspf command is configured, that is, to check whether the CSPF is enabled. If so, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 5. 4. Run the display mpls te cspf destination command on the ingress to check whether a path that meets the constraints is available. If so, the path of the TE tunnel is displayed, indicating that CSPF calculation is successful. If not, null is displayed, indicating that CSPF calculation fails. If the path is successfully calculated, run the display current-configuration interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command on the ingress to check the tunnel configurations, including the primary tunnel, protection tunnel, and the protection interface. Check whether the mpls te auto-frr command is configured in the MPLS view. If so, it indicates that Auto FRR is enabled. In this case, you can check the primary tunnel. If not, check whether the mpls te fast-reroute, mpls te record-route, and mpls te bypass-tunnel are configured to identify the primary and backup tunnels. After the primary and backup tunnels are checked, you can check the explicit-path command to verify whether the explicit path is configured; check the mpls te affinity property command to verify whether the affinity property is configured; check the mpls te bandwidth command to verify whether the bandwidth is configured. Run the display mpls te cspf destination command and configure the parameters of constraints one by one, including the priority (priority setup-priority), bandwidth (bandwidth), explicit path (explicit-path path-name), affinity property (affinity properties), and hop limit (hop-limit hop-limit-number), and you can check whether the path that meets the constraints is available. If so, the path of the TE tunnel is displayed, indicating that CSPF calculation is successful. If not, null is displayed, indicating that CSPF calculation fails. a. If the explicit path fails to be calculated, check whether the interfaces along the explicit path are in the Up state and are enabled with MPLS and MPLS TE. If the explicit path is successfully calculated, check whether path calculation according to the affinity property and bandwidth is consistent with the explicit path by running the display mpls te cspf destination <ip-address> bandwidth ct0 <ct0-bandwidth> explicit-path <path-name> command. b. If CSPF path calculation fails after affinity property is configured, run the mpls te affinity property command in the tunnel view to modify the affinity property of the tunnel, or run the mpls te link administrative group on the interfaces along the tunnel to modify the administrative group property of the link. c. If CSPF path calculation fails after bandwidth is configured, run the display mpls te link-administration bandwidth-allocation interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command to check whether the bandwidth of each outbound interface along the tunnel is enough. If the bandwidth is enough, it is possible that the tunnel with a higher priority preempts the bandwidth of the current tunnel. Then run the mpls te bandwidth max-reservable-bandwidth and mpls te bandwidth commands in the interface view to increase the bandwidth. d. If CSPF path calculation fails because of other constraints, go to Step 6. Then, check whether the alarm MPLS_LSPM_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.121.2.1.46 hwMplsTunnelPrimaryUp is generated. If so, go to Stpe 7. If not, go to Step 5. If CSPF path calculation fails, go to Step 5. 5. Run the display explicit-path command to check the interfaces along the tunnel. Then, run the display this command in the interface view of each interface of the tunnel to check whether the interface is enabled with MPLS, MPLS TE, and RSVP-TE. If MPLS, MPLS TE, or RSVP-TE is not enabled, run the mpls, mpls te or mpls rsvp-te commands in the view of the interface. If any interface along the tunnel is not in Up state, restart the interface. impact_on_system: If trigger-lsp or trigger-section is configured during the configuration of the CRC error packet rate on a physical interface, the alarm is generated, triggering an LSP or section switching. If trigger-lsp or trigger-section is not configured, services may be interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Transmission distances of optical modules on two directly connected devices were inconsistent with actual transmission distances. As a result, the input optical power of the devices was either too high or too low, causing error codes or packets over the link. Cause 2: The connector or extension component (such as a flange or concentrator) on the direct cable or link was not connected securely, causing error codes or packets over the link. Cause 3: The direct optical fiber or cable was not connected securely with devices on both ends, causing error codes or packets over the link. Cause 4: The direct optical module or power module was not connected securely with devices on both ends, causing error codes or packets over the link. Cause 5: The transmission network was faulty, causing routers to receive error codes or packets. Cause 6: The connector or extension component (such as a flange or concentrator) on the direct cable or link aged, causing error codes or packets over the link. Cause 7: The configurations (CRC mode, scramble mode of interfaces, and clock mode of WAN interfaces) of interconnected physical layer devices were inconsistent, causing error codes or packets over the link.
procedure: 1.Check that the optical fiber is connected properly. Run the display this interface command in the interface view to check the interface status. If the interface is Up, go to Step 2. If the interface is Down, go to Step 5. 2.Check the optical receive power in the display this interface command output. If the optical receive power is within the allowed range, go to Step 3. If the optical receive power is not in the allowed range, go to Step 6. 3.Check the link protocol, clock mode and scramble of the local device in the display this interface command output. Then check whether they are consistent with those of the peer device.

description: TWAMP does not support service alarm clearing on the bound interface. (SessionId=[SessionId])
impact_on_system: Services are not affected.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The TWAMP reflector configuration was removed. Cause 2: The interface used the supported VLL services.

description: Number of lost ATM PW disorder packets on the network side over the threshold in a certain period. (IfIndex=[IfIndex], VcId=[VcId], VcType=[VcType], PeerAddress=[PeerAddress], InterfaceName=[InterfaceName]) Number of lost ATM PW disorder packets on the network side over the threshold in a certain period.
impact_on_system: Lines on the public network are faulty and services may be affected.
possible_causes: The public network detected out-of-order packets.
procedure: 1.Check the links on the public network side. a.Check whether the physical module (such as optical module and optical cable) is faulty. If yes, change the fault optical modules or optical cables. Check whether the alarm is cleared.  - If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 3. - If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step b. If not, go to step b. b.Run the command display this in the interface view to check whether the configurations (VC ID/VC type/Peer IP address which should be its peer interface ip address) on both end interface are the same. If yes, go to step 2. If not, change them to be the same. And check whether the alarm is cleared.  - If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 3. - If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step 2.
parameters: IfIndex::Interface Index. | VcId::VcId . | VcType::VcType. | PeerAddress::Peer Address. | InterfaceName::Interface Name.

description: The FCS-SD error is rising. (hwPhysicalPortIfIndex=[hwPhysicalPortIfIndex],hwPhysicalPortName=[hwPhysicalPortName]) The FCS-SD error is rising. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: These errors cause packet loss, affecting services.
possible_causes: The FlexE physical interface receives fcs-sd data.
procedure: 1. Check whether optical fibers are properly connected. (If you hear a click when inserting an optical fiber, it indicates that the optical fiber is properly connected.) Then, run the display this interface command to check whether the interface is up. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 4. 2. Run the display this interface command in the interface view to check whether the receive optical power of the optical module is within the normal range. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Replace the optical module and check whether the alarm is cleared.
parameters: hwPhysicalPortIfIndex::Index of physical port. | hwPhysicalPortName::Name of physical port.

description: The configured client IDs did not match. (hwPortIfIndex=[hwPortIfIndex],hwPortName=[hwPortName]) The configured client IDs did not match.
impact_on_system: The FlexE interface does not go up.
possible_causes: The configured client IDs did not match.
procedure: 1. Check whether there is a FlexE interface with the same client-id configuration at both ends. If not, check whether the alarm is cleared after configuring the same client-id parameter. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 6. If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step 2. 2. Check if the connected FlexE interface is configured with bandwidth. If not, check whether the alarm is cleared after configuring bandwidth for the connected FlexE interface. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 6.
parameters: hwPortIfIndex::Index of port. | hwPortName::Name of port.

description: The alarm that the hardware do not support PTP time synchronization is resumed. (hwPtpChassisId=[hwPtpChassisId], hwPtpPortIfIndex=[hwPtpPortIfIndex], hwPtpPortName=[hwPtpPortName]) In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: There is no impact on the system.
possible_causes: In current link mode, the hardware, such as boards and optical modules,  support PTP time synchronization.
parameters: hwPtpChassisId::Chassis ID. | hwPtpPortIfIndex::Interface index. | hwPtpPortName::Interface name.

description: Inconsistency between application configuration data and master main board configuration data. The data in the service process database is inconsistent with that in the central database. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: If the data in the service process database is inconsistent with that in the central database, the host behavior may be inconsistent with the operator's expectation. As a result, related services cannot be executed.
possible_causes: This alarm was automatically generated because the data in the service process database was detected inconsistent with that in the central database after data consistency verification was enabled.
procedure: 1. Run the display ha process running-state or display system process running-state command in the diagnostic view to display all process IDs. 2. Run the display cmf-info recovery verify-appdata process <all process IDs> or display configuration diagnostic-information recovery verify-appdata process <all process IDs> command in the diagnostic view to check whether the service process database is damaged. If the Err relationid is <ID of the damaged table> message is displayed, the service process database is damaged. In this case, collect log information. 3. Run the display configuration records appdata-diff command in the diagnostic view to check the ID of the slot where inconsistencies exist. 4. Run the reset slot <slot-id> command based on the slot ID information obtained in step 3 to reset the card in the slot corresponding to the process, synchronizing data in the service process database again. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If the reset succeeds, no further action is required. If the reset fails, go to step 5.

description: The interface line protocol is down after received too many PAUSE frames in a short time. (interface-name=[interface-name]) After a large number of PAUSE frames are received within a short period of time, the interface link goes Down.
impact_on_system: The link of the trunk member interface that receives a large number of PAUSE frames goes Down, affecting the trunk interface bandwidth.
possible_causes: A single trunk member interface receives more than 750 PAUSE frames within 15 seconds, and the interface bandwidth usage is lower than 10% within every 5 seconds.
procedure: 1. Rectify the fault on the device that sends PAUSE frames. After confirming that the peer device does not frequently send PAUSE frames, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Perform either of the following operations based on service requirements: If the impact is acceptable and you do not want the alarm to be reported, run the qos received-multi-pause-frame-alarm disable command in the system view to disable the alarm, and then go to Step 4. If you cannot perform accurate analysis, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: interface-name::Interface name.

description: The number of DHCPv6 Snooping binding entries fell below the upper limit. (Max number=[MaxNumber])
impact_on_system: The alarm is cleared, and services are not affected.
possible_causes: The number of DHCPv6 Snooping entries on the device falls below 90% of the upper limit.
parameters: MaxNumber::Maximum number of DHCPv6 snooping binding entries.

description: IS-IS routes advertised by another device were deleted. Log in to the possibly faulty device. If the device is deleting routes, reset or isolate it from the network. Otherwise, check other devices. (SysInstance=[isisSysInstance], HostName=[hwIsisHostName], HostIpAddress=[hwIsisHostIpAddress], SystemID=[isisPduLspId], SysLevel=[isisSysLevelIndex], TotalNodeNum=[hwIsisTotalNodeNum], Log in to the following devices to locate the faulty device: (1) HostName=[hwIsisHostName1], HostIpAddress=[hwIsisHostIpAddress1], SystemID=[hwIsisSystemID1] (2) HostName=[hwIsisHostName2], HostIpAddress=[hwIsisHostIpAddress2], SystemID=[hwIsisSystemID2] (3) HostName=[hwIsisHostName3], HostIpAddress=[hwIsisHostIpAddress3], SystemID=[hwIsisSystemID3]) The local device received a purge LSP from a neighbor indicating that the neighbor had purged the IS-IS LSPs advertised by a third device. The local device does not support IS-IS purge LSP source tracing. In this case, log in to the possibly faulty node and check whether it is purging LSPs. If it is purging LSPs, reset or isolate it. If the possibly faulty node is not purging LSPs, check other possibly faulty nodes.
impact_on_system: Network flapping may occur, affecting traffic forwarding.
possible_causes: IS-IS routes advertised by another device were not deleted.
procedure: 1. Run the display isis route command to check whether any route is deleted. If yes, isolate the device from the network by resetting or isolating the device. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End.

description: An alarm of enabling the PW loop check function. (IFINDEX=[hwPortIndex], IFNAME=[hwPortName], LOOPDETECTTIME=[pwLoopCheckTime], ALARMREASON=[AlarmReason]) The PW interface loopback function was enabled on the interface. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.

description: OAM reported an Unknown alarm. (ServiceType=[ServiceType], ProtocolType=[ProtocolType], VcID=[VcID], VcType=[VcType], PeerAddr=[PeerAddr], IfIndex=[IfIndex], PwMaster=[PwMaster], RmtSiteID=[RmtSiteID], InLabel=[InLabel], OutLabel=[OutLabel], IfName=[IfName], VsiName=[VsiName]) The packet transmission interval or detection type carried in the received packets was inconsistent with that on the local end.
impact_on_system: After OAM is deployed and an APS instance is bound to the PW protection group: The service traffic will be switched from the primary PW to the secondary PW if OAM reports an alarm about the primary PW. The service traffic will not be switched or affected if OAM reports an alarm about the secondary PW.
possible_causes: Cause 1: MPLS OAM configurations were incorrect. Cause 2: The PW detected by OAM became faulty.
procedure: The troubleshooting procedure is as follows: 1. Run the display mpls l2vc or display mpls static-l2vc command to check whether the status and type of the PW fault are consistent with that reported by the alarm. If they are consistent, go to Step 2. If they are inconsistent, go to Step 5. 2. Run the display mpls oam l2vc all verbose command to check whether the status and type of the MPLS OAM fault are consistent with that reported by the alarm. If they are consistent, go to Step 3. If they are inconsistent, go to Step 5.
parameters: ServiceType::Type of the service: 0: VLL. 1: VPLS. | ProtocolType::Type of the protocol: 0: SVC. 1: LDP. 2: BGP (not supported for the time being). | VcID::VC ID. | VcType::VC type. | PeerAddr::IP address of the peer. | IfIndex::Interface index. | PwMaster::PW identifier: 1: primary PW. 2: secondary PW. | RmtSiteID::Remote site ID. | InLabel::VC in-label. | OutLabel::VC out-label. | IfName::Interface name. | VsiName::VSI name.

description: The board temperature exceeded the fatal limit. (EntityPhysicalIndex=[EntityPhysicalIndex],EntPhysicalIndex=[EntPhysicalIndex],EntPhysicalName=[EntityPhysicalName],EntityThresholdType=[EntThresholdType],EntityThresholdCritical=[EntThresholdCritical],EntityThresholdCurrent=[EntThresholdCurrent],EntityTrapFaultID=143872) The board temperature was fatally abnormal. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Services will not be affected temporarily, but a speedy solution is required.
possible_causes: The board temperature was extremely high.
procedure: 1. Check if there are idle slots without filler panels on the device. If there are idle slots without filler panels, install filler panels to cover these slots. 2. Check if the filter screen of the fan module is clogged. If the filter screen is clogged, clean the filter screen. 3. Check the ambient temperature. If the ambient temperature is too high, reduce the temperature to a normal level. 4. Check if the fan module is faulty. If there is a fault on the fan module, rectify the fault first. 5. If the ambient temperature is normal but the alarm is still reported, the possible cause is that the module temperature is too high. In this case, collect the information about alarms, logs, and configurations, and then contact technical support personnel.
parameters: EntityPhysicalIndex::Indicates the index of the physical entity. | EntPhysicalIndex::Indicates the index of the physical entity. | EntityPhysicalName::Indicates the name of the physical entity. | EntThresholdType::Indicates the alarm type. The following values: 1: High temperature. 2: Low temperature. | EntThresholdCritical::Indicates the alarm threshold. | EntThresholdCurrent::The current value that been measured. | EntityTrapFaultID::To describe the fault id of trap.

description: Data failed to be synchronized from the master OMU to the slave OMU. (Reason=The OMU data of [BoardName] synchronization timed out. [Action]) The active OMU fails to synchronize data to the standby OMU. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: System reliability is hindered.
possible_causes: The OMU data synchronization timed out.
procedure: 1. Run the display current-configuration include-default command to check the timeout period configured using the slave batch-backup self-healing-timeout command. If the configured timeout period is not 0, go to Step 2. If the configured timeout period is 0, go to Step 3. 2. Wait until the configured timeout period expires. The system resets the standby board. If the alarm persists, go to Step 5. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 6. 3. description: The status of the virtual neighbor changes. (VirtNbrArea=[VirtNbrArea], VirtNbrRtrId=[VirtNbrRtrId], ProcessId=[ProcessId], RouterId=[RouterId], VirtNbrState=[VirtNbrState], InstanceName=[InstanceName]) The status of the neighbor on the virtual link changed.
impact_on_system: This trap is sent when the status of the neighbor on the virtual link changes. If the neighbor status changes from a lower state to a higher state, no action is required. If the neighbor status changes from a higher state to a lower state, services may be interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Adjacency holdTimer expired Cause 2: Physical interface change Cause 3: Protocol reason Cause 4: BFD session state change Cause 5: Configuration change Cause 6: Peer router reason
procedure: Cause 1: Adjacency holdTimer expired 1. Run the ping command to check whether the link that connects the local and remote devices functions properly. If the ping fails, check the transport devices, link status, and interface status and rectify faults (if any) on the physical devices to restore OSPF services. If the ping succeeds, go to . 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 2: Physical interface change 1. Run the display ospf interface command to check the status of the physical interface used to set up the OSPF neighbor relationship. If the physical interface is in the Down state, check whether the optical power of the physical interface is within the permitted range and whether the transport device works properly. Restore the physical interface status to clear the alarm. If the physical interface is in the *down state, the interface has been shut down. Then run the undo shutdown command on the interface to clear the alarm. If the physical interface is in the Up state, go to 2. 2. Run the display ospf interface command to check the protocol status of the interface used to set up the OSPF neighbor relationship. If the protocol state is Down, check whether the interface IP addresses are configured correctly. If no, configure the IP addresses correctly to clear the alarm. If the protocol state is Up, go to 3. 3. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 3: Protocol reason 1. Run the display this command in both the interface view and OSPF view of the local and remote devices to check whether the two devices use the same protocol. If the two devices use the same protocol, go to 2. If the two devices use different protocols, configure the same protocol for the interfaces. 2. Run the display ospf peer command to view OSPF neighbor information. If no OSPF neighbor information is displayed, the local device cannot receive any Hello messages from the remote device or the received Hello messages have been discarded. Then go to 3. If Init is displayed, the local device can receive Hello messages from the remote device, whereas the remote device cannot receive any Hello messages from the local device. Run the ping command to check whether the link that connects the local and remote devices functions properly. A common cause for the OSPF neighbor to stay in the Init state is that a fault occurs in packet forwarding and hence packets are discarded. If the alarm persists after the fault in packet forwarding is rectified, go to 4. If 2-way is displayed, the value of ospf dr-priority is 0. Run the ospf dr-priority command to set the DR priority of the interface to a value larger than 0 to clear the alarm. If Exstart is displayed, the device generating this alarm keeps performing DD negotiation but fails to complete DD synchronization. Then go to 3. 3. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 4: BFD session state change 1. Run the ping command to check whether the link that connects the local and remote devices functions properly. If the ping fails, check the transport devices, link status, and interface status and rectify faults (if any) on the physical devices to restore OSPF services. If the ping succeeds, go to 4. 2. Run the ping command in the interface view to check whether the link is configured correctly. If the link is correctly configured, go to 3. If the link is incorrectly configured, correct link configurations. 3. Run the display ospf peer command to check whether the OSPF neighbor is in the Up state. If the OSPF neighbor is in the Up state, go to 4. If the OSPF neighbor is in the Down state, go to 4. 4. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 5: Configuration change 1. Run the display this command in the OSPF process view to check whether the area configurations of the two ends are the same. If they are different, change them to be the same. If they are the same, go to step 2. 2. Run the display this command in the OSPF process view to check whether the opaque capability is enabled in the OSPF processes on both ends. If they are different, change them to be the same. If they are the same, go to step 3. 3. Run the display ospf interface command to check whether the OSPF network types (values of the Type fields) of the interfaces at both ends of the link are the same. If they are different, change them to be the same. If yes, go to step 4. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 6: Peer router reason 1. Check whether the peer router is a non-Huawei device. If it is a non-Huawei device, go to 2. If it is a Huawei device, go to 3. 2. Contact the non-Huawei device manufacturer to check its operating status and rectify the fault. 3. Check whether the peer router or the OSPF process has been restarted. If the peer router or the OSPF process has been restarted, refer to alarm and log information to identify the cause. If the peer router or the OSPF process has not been restarted, go to 4. 4. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel.
parameters: VirtNbrArea::Indicates the area ID. | VirtNbrRtrId::Indicates the router ID of the neighbor on the virtual link. | ProcessId::Indicates the process ID. | RouterId::Indicates the ID of the local router. | VirtNbrState::Indicates the status of a virtual neighbor. The trap is a service restoration trap only when the value of Full. Otherwise, it is a fault trap. 1: Down 2: Attempt 3: Init 4: 2-Way 5: ExStart 6: Exchange 7: Loading 8: Full | InstanceName::Indicates the instance name.

Then, go to Step 2. 256: indicates that the local interface is shut down. Then, go to Step 3. 257: indicates a dying gasp event. Then, go to Step 4. 258: indicates a critical event. Then, go to Step 5. 2. Run the display this command in the interface view to check whether EFM is enabled on the remote device. If so, go to Step 6. If not, go to Step 8. 3. Run the display this command in the interface view to check whether the local interface is shut down. If so, go to Step 9. If not, go to Step 6. 4. Check whether the remote device is being restarted. If so, go to Step 10. If not, go to Step 12. 5. Check whether a fault occurs on the module associated with EFM. If so, go to Step 7. If not, go to Step 12. 6. Check whether the physical link is faulty. If so, go to Step 11. If not, go to Step 12. 7. Restore the module associated with EFM and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 13. If not, go to Step 12. 8. Run the efm enable command in the interface view of the remote device to enable EFM. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 13. If not, go to Step 12. 9. Run the undo shutdown command in the interface view and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 13. If not, go to Step 6. 10. After the remote device works normally, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 13. If not, go to Step 12. 11. Replace the physical link and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 13. If not, go to Step 12. 12. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support. 13. End. Cause 2: Receive link fault packet the remote carried. Same as Cause 1. Cause 3: Receive Dying Gasp packet the remote carried. Same as Cause 1. Cause 4: Receive critical event packet the remote carried. Same as Cause 1.

If hwMflpPwResume is not reported, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 2: The PW has been blocked for VSI loop, and the loop has already been punished times times. 1. Run the display current-configuration command to check whether the loopback local command is configured on PW-side interfaces corresponding to the VSI. If the loopback local command is configured on PW-side interfaces corresponding to the VSI, delete the command configuration and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. If the loopback local command is not configured on PW-side interfaces corresponding to the VSI, go to Step 2. 2. description: The state of interface changed from unsuppress to suppress. impact_on_system: After the interface is suppressed, the interface management module no longer reports interface Up or Down events to the routing protocol module before the interface recovers from suppression.
possible_causes: The interface had the flapping control function configured. When the interface alternated between Up and Down frequently, the interface became suppressed. The number of the interface flapping times that triggers the suppression alarm depends on the control-flap command configuration.
procedure: 1. Check the physical link. Interface flapping usually results from a physical link fault or link instability during a short time.If the physical link works improperly, you need to check whether the hardware such as the network cable or optical module is disconnected or loosely connected and correctly connect the physical link and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step 2. If the alarm is generated on a physical interface, check whether the physical link of the interface works properly. If the alarm is generated on a sub-interface, check whether the physical link of the main interface works properly. If the alarm is generated on a trunk interface, check whether the physical links of the trunk member interfaces work properly. 2. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel.
parameters: InterfaceIndex::Interface index | InterfaceExtIndex::Extended interface index | InterfaceName::Interface name | SuppressState::Interface suppression status: 0: The interface is not suppressed. 1: The interface is suppressed.

procedure: 1. Run the distribute-weight command in the view of the involved member interface to set the load balancing weight of the member interface to 1. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Run the undo eth-trunk command in the interface view to remove the interface from the Eth-Trunk interface. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect trap, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support.

If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. If the alarm interval is too small, run the alarm access-rate port-car interval interval-value command to increase the interval. description: Tunnel status changes to Down. (TunnelId=[TunnelId], LocalLspId=[LocalLspId], IngressLsrId=[IngressLsrId], EgressLsrId=[EgressLsrId], OutIfIndex=[OutIfIndex], TunnelAdminStatus=[TunnelAdminStatus], TunnelOperStatus=[TunnelOperStatus], TunnelName=[TunnelName], OutIfName=[OutIfName], SubReason=[SubReason], Reason=[DownReason], SignalledTunnelName=[SignalledTunnelName]) A trap was generated when the current tunnel became faulty and went Down.
impact_on_system: The service traffic to be forwarded through the tunnel will be interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Others Cause 2: A static LSP went Down. Cause 3: A static CR-LSP went Down. Cause 4: The outbound interface of an RSVP-TE LSP's ingress went Down. Cause 5: RSVP-TE LSP resources were preempted. Cause 6: Transmission of an RSVP message timed out. Cause 7: RSVP Hello mechanism detected a downstream node failure. Cause 8: The bypass tunnel in use was Down or unbound from the primary tunnel. Cause 9: CSPF failed to calculate a path. Cause 10: The tunnel was manually shut down.
procedure: Cause 1: Others 1. Check the configurations of the tunnel interface, RSVP, and IGP and bandwidth usage of the tunnel. If any configuration is incorrect, modify the configuration and commit it. If the fault is rectified, go to Step 5. If the problem persists, go to Step 2. If the configurations are correct, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display mpls te tunnel-interface last-error command to check the displayed error messages. If the following error message is displayed: "Cspf failed to calculate a path for Tunnel." indicates that CSPF is enabled on the ingress but CSPF path calculation fails. In this situation, check whether the explicit path and routes are configured correctly and whether the IGP has the MPLS TE capability enabled. If any configuration is incorrect, modify it. If the alarm is cleared, no other action is required. Otherwise, go to Step 3. "Routing Problem:Bad EXPLICIT_ROUTE object." or "Routing Problem:Bad initial subobject."indicates that the ingress does not have CSPF enabled but has an incorrect explicit path configured. In this situation, configure a correct explicit path. No further action is required. Otherwise, go to Step 3. "Routing Problem:No route available toward destination." indicates that both the ingress and transit node do not have CSPF enabled, or have an incorrect explicit path configured, or no route to the destination address is available. In this situation, check IGP and explicit path configurations. No further action is required. Otherwise, go to Step 3. "Service preempted" indicates that the bandwidth of this tunnel is preempted by another tunnel. In this situation, modify the preemption priority configured on the tunnel interface. No further action is required. Otherwise, go to Step 3. "Admission Control failure"indicates that the ingress has CSPF enabled but the downstream node is not. Along the explicit path, CSPF counts the bandwidth: the bandwidth of the ingress is sufficient; but the link bandwidth of the downstream node is insufficient. In this situation, check the explicit path and bandwidth configuration. No further action is required. Otherwise, go to Step 3. For other types of errors, go to Step 4. If no error message is displayed, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display mpls lsp statistics command to check whether the number of LSPs exceeds the specification. If so, delete unnecessary LSPs and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 2: A static LSP went Down. The same as Cause 1. Cause 3: A static CR-LSP went Down. The same as Cause 1. Cause 4: The outbound interface of an RSVP-TE LSP's ingress went Down. The same as Cause 1. Cause 5: RSVP-TE LSP resources were preempted. The same as Cause 1. Cause 6: Transmission of an RSVP message timed out. The same as Cause 1. Cause 7: RSVP Hello mechanism detected a downstream node failure. The same as Cause 1. Cause 8: The bypass tunnel in use was Down or unbound from the primary tunnel. The same as Cause 1. Cause 9: CSPF failed to calculate a path. The same as Cause 1. Cause 10: The tunnel was manually shut down. The same as Cause 1.
parameters: TunnelId::Indicates the ID of the tunnel. | LocalLspId::Indicates the LSP ID of a session. | IngressLsrId::Indicates the LSR ID of the ingress on the tunnel. | EgressLsrId::Indicates the LSR ID of the egress on the tunnel. | OutIfIndex::Indicates the outgoing interface index of the ingress of the LSP that goes Down. | TunnelAdminStatus::Indicates the management status of the tunnel. | TunnelOperStatus::Indicates the operating status of the tunnel. | TunnelName::Indicates the name of the tunnel. | OutIfName::Indicates the name of the outgoing interface on the ingress of the LSP that goes Down. | SubReason::Indicates the sub-cause for identifying the alarm clearance type. The default value is 0 when an alarm is generated. The meaning of a different sub-cause value is as follows: 1: The alarm is cleared because related faults are rectified. 2: The alarm is cleared due to timeout. 3: The alarm is deleted. | DownReason::Indicates the reason of Tunnel down. | SignalledTunnelName::Tunnel alias.

description: The number of LSAs learned by OSPF exceeded the threshold. (Ospfv2ProcessIdIndex=[hwOspfv2ProcessIdIndex], Ospfv2RecvLsaUpper=[hwOspfv2RecvLsaUpper]) This alarm is reported when the number of LSAs learned by an OSPF process exceeds the threshold.

(Normal indicates that the number of LSAs is less than 90% of the alarm threshold. Exceed indicates that the number of LSAs reaches or exceeds the alarm threshold.) If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 4. 2. In the OSPF process that reports the alarm, run the display this command to check whether no import policy is configured for the source device that advertises LSAs or whether the import policy is improper. If so, a large number of LSAs may be imported, causing the local device to learn a large number of LSAs. If no import policy is configured, run the import-route command to configure a policy to limit the routes to be imported. After the configuration is complete, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, no further action is required. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. If an import policy is configured but its configuration is improper, run the import-route command to modify the policy. After the configuration is complete, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, no further action is required. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. If the import policy is correctly configured, go to Step 3. 3. Run the maximum received-lsa threshold <value> command to adjust the threshold of learned LSAs and then check whether the alarm is cleared.

description:
The time lock status is failed. (hwPtpTimeLockStatus=[hwPtpTimeLockStatus], hwPtpTimeLockFailReason=[hwPtpTimeLockFailReason]) The time is out of lock.
This alarm is reported in the following scenarios:
1. The device time changes from the locked state to the out-of-lock state.
2. After the PTP service is configured, the source selection and tracing is normal but the time is not locked. The alarm is reported after a period of time. If the current tracing source is an ATR source, the alarm is reported if the time is out of lock for four consecutive hours. If the current tracing source is not an ATR source, the alarm is reported if the time is out of lock for two consecutive hours. If the tracing source is switched during the timing, the timing starts again. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The system cannot perform time synchronization.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The time is not in the tracking state, no available source. Cause 2: The offset sum exceed the threshold. Cause 3: The timestamps of ptp message remains unchanged. Cause 4: The frequency lock fail. Cause 5: The Inter-chassis time lock fail.
procedure: Cause 1: The time is not in the tracking state, no available source. 1. Run the display ptp all command to check the interface whose clock status is slave, that is, the interface whose state field in Port info is slave. Then run the display this interface command in the interface view to check whether the link status of the interface is Up. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 4. 2. Run the display current-configuration command to check whether PTP-related configurations are changed. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 5. 3. Reconfigure PTP attributes. For details, see "1588v2 Configuration" in "Clock and Time Synchronization" in the Configuration Guide. Then, go to Step 6. 4. Rectify the link fault. For details, refer to "Interface Physical Connection" in the "Universal Service Router Troubleshooting." Check whether the fault is rectified. If so, go to Step 6. If not, go to Step 5. 5. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 6. End. Cause 2: The offset sum exceed the threshold. 1. Run the reset ptp statistics all command to clear timestamp statistics. Then run the display ptp all command multiple times to check whether the difference between Max (T2-T1) and Min (T2-T1) and Realtime (T2-T1) is within 500 ns. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 4. 2. Run the display current-configuration command to check whether PTP-related configurations are changed. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 4. 3. Reconfigure PTP attributes. For details, see "1588v2 Configuration" in "Clock and Time Synchronization" in the Configuration Guide. Then, go to Step 5. 4. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 5. End. Cause 3: The timestamps of ptp message remains unchanged. 1. Run the reset ptp statistics all command to clear timestamp statistics. Then run the display ptp all command multiple times to check whether the value of Max (T2-T1) and Min (T2-T1) is the same as Realtime (T2-T1) and remains unchanged. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 4. 2. Run the display ptp all config command to check whether the rate of sending PTP packets is correct. If so, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Reconfigure PTP attributes. For details, see "1588v2 Configuration" in "Clock and Time Synchronization" in the Configuration Guide. Then, go to Step 5. 4. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 5. End. Cause 4: The frequency lock fail. 1. Run the display clock source command to check whether the clock synchronization source is changed. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 3. 2. Run the display clock config command to check whether the clock source configuration is changed. If yes, configure the attributes of the local clock. For details, see "Physical Layer Clock Synchronization Configuration" in the Configuration Guide. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 5: The Inter-chassis time lock fail. 1. Run the display current-configuration command to check whether the configuration of the clock interconnection interface is correct. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 3. 2. Check whether the inter-chassis cable connection is correct. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 4. 3. Reconfigure the attributes of the clock interconnection port. For details, see "Physical Layer Clock Synchronization Configuration" in the Configuration Guide. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 6. If the alarm persists, go to step 5. 4. Rectify the line fault and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 6. If the alarm persists, go to step 5. 5. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 6. End.
