description: The interface bound to the VPN instance went Down. (VpnInstanceName=[VpnInstanceName], IfName=[IfName], IfCurRowStatus=[IfCurRowStatus], VRFOperationStatus=[VRFOperationStatus]) Of the interfaces that are bound to VPN instance, the last interface in the Up state goes Down.
impact_on_system: No available interface is bound with the VPN instance.
possible_causes: Cause 1: One interface was bound with the VPN instance, and the interface status changed from Up to Down. Cause 2: Multiple interfaces were bound with the VPN instance; the status of all the interfaces changed from Up to Down; the last interface in the Up state went Down. Cause 3: The last interface with Up state is disassociated from the VPN instance.
procedure: 1. Run the display ip vpn-instance verbose <vpn-instance-name> command to view the Interfaces field and check the interfaces bound to the specified VPN instance. If no interface is bound, check whether a log that contains the keyword undo ip binding vpn-instance is generated together with the alarm. If yes and the VPN instance needs to be unbound, run the transit-vpn command to set the VPN status to Up to clear the alarm. If the VPN instance is not used, delete the VPN instance to clear the alarm. Otherwise, run the ip binding vpn-instance <vpn-instance-name> command in the interface view to bind the VPN instance to the interface, and run the ip address command to configure an IP address for the interface. If the L3VPN_1.3.6.1.2.1.10.166.11.0.1 L3VPN_MIB_TRAP_VRF_UP alarm of the VPN instance is displayed, the fault is rectified. Otherwise, go to Step 5. If no, go to Step 5. If there are interfaces bound to the VPN instance, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display ip interface brief command to check whether the interfaces bound to the VPN instance are up. If yes, go to Step 5. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Check whether the interfaces bound to the VPN instance have IP addresses configured. If yes, go to Step 4. Configure IP addresses for the interfaces bound to the VPN instance using the ip address command. If the L3VPN_1.3.6.1.2.1.10.166.11.0.1 L3VPN_MIB_TRAP_VRF_UP alarm of the VPN instance is displayed, the fault is rectified. If no, go to Step 4. 4. Run the display this command in the view of the interface bound to the VPN instance to check whether the shutdown command was run. If yes, run the undo shutdown command to enable the interface as required. If the L3VPN_1.3.6.1.2.1.10.166.11.0.1 L3VPN_MIB_TRAP_VRF_UP alarm of the VPN instance is displayed, the fault is rectified. If no, go to Step 5. If no, go to Step 5. 5. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support. 6. End.
parameters: VpnInstanceName::Indicates the name of the VPN. | IfName::The name of interface. | IfCurRowStatus::Indicates the row status of the interface. Including: 1: Active 2: Not in Service 3: Not Ready 4: Create and Go 5: Create and Wait 6: Destroy | VRFOperationStatus::Indicates the status of the VRF. Including: 1: Up 2: Down

description: PTP attribute mismatching at both ends. (ClockChassisId=[ClockChassisId], PtpPortIfIndex=[PtpPortIfIndex], PtpPortName=[PtpPortName], AlarmReason=[AlarmReason]) The configuration attributes at both ends did not match. If the configurations at both ends do not match, PTP packets cannot be correctly processed. As a result, time synchronization fails. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: When the configurations at both ends do not match, the time cannot be traced normally.
possible_causes: Cause1: The P/E modes mismatch. (If the P/E mode on the master side is the P2P mode and the P/E mode on the slave side is the E2E mode, an alarm is generated on the slave side and the slave side triggers clock source switching. if the P/E mode on the master side is the E2E mode and the P/E mode on the slave side is the P2P mode, an alarm is generated only on the master side and the slave side does not trigger clock source switching.) Cause2: The encapsulation types of the PTP interfaces on both sides are inconsistent. Cause3: The domain configurations of the PTP interfaces on both sides are inconsistent. Cause4: The source port IDs of the PTP interfaces on both sides are inconsistent.
procedure: 1. Check whether the P/E modes at both ends match. If not, modify the P/E modes at both ends to match. 2. Check whether the encapsulation types at both ends match. If not, modify the encapsulation types at both ends to match. 3. Check whether the domains at both ends match. If not, modify the configurations at both ends to match. 4. Check whether an incorrect SourcePortId to be received is configured.
parameters: ClockChassisId::Number of the chassis where the clock source is located. | PtpPortIfIndex::Index of the interface where the clock source is located. | PtpPortName::Name of the interface where the clock source is located. | AlarmReason::Cause of the mismatch between the two ends.

If the board can be registered after being reset and the link fault is rectified, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display ptp all command to check whether the device is in the local state. If so, go to Step 3.
parameters: hwPtpTimeSynchronizationStatus::Whether the device is in the synchronization or out-of-synchronization state. The values are as follows: unsynchronization(1). synchronization(2).

If yes, go to Step 17. If no, see the procedure for handling the alarm ISIS_1.3.6.1.3.37.2.0.17 isisAdjacencyChange. 13. Check whether a source address is specified for the BGP connection. If no, run the peer valid-ttl-hops command to ensure that the TTL value of the message received from the peer device is in the range of [255 – hops + 1, 255]. 16. Contact maintenance engineers of the peer device and check whether BGP has been reset on the peer device, the peer device has been enabled using the peer enable command in other address families on the local device, or BGP connection parameters have been set. If any of these operations has been performed, wait for a while and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 17. 17. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support. Cause 3: BGP receive error packet 1. Contact maintenance engineers of the peer device and check whether BGP has been reset on the peer device, the peer device has been enabled using the peer enable command in other address families on the local device, or BGP connection parameters have been set. If any of these operations has been performed, wait for a while and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 15. 15. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support. Cause 5: BGP remote peer not reachable 1. Run the ping command to check whether the IP address of the BGP peer can be pinged. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Check whether the CPU usage is too high. If yes, go to Step 15. If no, go to Step 4. 3. Run the display ip routing-table command to check whether the BGP peer address exists in the routing table. If yes, go to Step 5. If no, go to Step 6. 4. If the EBGP peer relationship is established and multiple hops exist between EBGP peers, check whether the peer ebgp-max-hop command is configured. If yes, go to Step 13. procedure: 1. Locate the interfaces that do not have the SRv6 license based on information such as the conflicting processes and interface names in the alarm. 2. If the alarm is not cleared but the number of interfaces in the alarm description decreases, the license has taken effect but some interfaces still do not have a valid license. In this case, repeat Step 1. If the alarm is not cleared and the alarm description remains unchanged, go to Step 4. 4. Cause 3: The cross-connect board of the remote device failed, was not installed, or was not installed properly. Cause 4: The clock board of the remote device failed.
procedure: 1. Check whether any optical fiber is connected to the optical interface. If no optical fiber is used, shut down the laser of the optical interface and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 2. Check whether the optical fiber is broken. If the optical fiber is broken, replace the optical fiber and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 3. Check whether the receive optical power of the local device is less than the minimum value. If the receive optical power is less than the minimum value, clean the optical fiber connector and the optical interface on the interface board. Check that the flange and the optical attenuator are properly connected and the optical attenuator value is in the normal range. Then check whether the alarm is cleared.
parameters: hwPhysicalPortIfIndex::Index of physical port. | hwPhysicalPortInSlot::Slot ID. | hwPhysicalPortInCard::Card ID. | hwPhysicalPortInPort::Port ID. | hwPhyPortName::Port name | hwPhysicalPortName::Name of physical port.

description: The number of ARP entries exceeded the threshold. (entPhysicalIndex=[entPhysicalIndex], Slot name=[slotname], Threshold=[Threshold], Number of dynamic ARP entries=[DynEntries], Number of static ARP entries=[StatEntries]) The number of ARP entries exceeded 80% of the threshold.
impact_on_system: If this alarm is displayed, the number of ARP entries on the device is great. If the number continuously increases, system resources become insufficient and no new ARP entries can be learned. As a result, service interruption may occur. After the alarm is generated, do not power off or reset the device; otherwise, resources will be reassigned, and services will be affected.
possible_causes: The number of ARP entries on the device exceeded the upper threshold.
procedure: 1. Run the display arp statistics command to view statistics about ARP entries on the device. Check whether the number of static ARP entries is greater than the number of dynamic ARP entries or vice versa based on the network planning and service deployment. If the number of dynamic ARP entries is greater than the number of static ARP entries, go to Step 2. If the number of static ARP entries is greater than the number of dynamic ARP entries, go to Step 3. 2. Run the display arp command to determine the interfaces that have a large number of ARP entries. For such interfaces, run the display arp interface command to check whether the ARP entries are needed. If the ARP entries are needed, go to Step 5. If some ARP entries are not needed and clearing them does not affect services, run the reset arp all or reset arp interface command to manually clear the ARP entries. Then, go to Step 4. 3. Run the display current-configuration command to check whether the static ARP entries are needed.
parameters: entPhysicalIndex::Indicates the index of the physical entity. | slotname::Indicates the board name. | Threshold::Indicates the alarm threshold. | DynEntries::Indicates the number of dynamic ARP entries. | StatEntries::Indicates the number of static ARP entries.

description: The prefix-sid conflict is detected. (Protocol=[hwProtocol], ProcessId=[hwProcessId], PrefixSid=[hwPrefixSid], PrefixAddress=[hwPrefixAddress], PrefixAddressMask=[hwPrefixAddressMask], Algorithm=[hwAlgorithm], ConflictType=[hwConflictType]) A prefix SID conflict was detected. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The conflicting route is not used by the SR. If a prefix conflict occurs, the system selects only one prefix and ignores the same prefix advertised by other devices. If a SID conflict occurs, the system selects only one SID and ignores the same SIDs advertised by other devices.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The configuration is incorrect. Cause 2: The prefix on a loopback interface is the same as the address of a loopback interface on another device. Cause 3: The SID configured on a loopback interface is the same as the SID on another router.
procedure: 1. If an OSPF prefix SID conflict occurs, run the ospf prefix-sid command on the source device to modify the SID configuration. 2. If an IS-IS prefix SID conflict occurs, run the isis prefix-sid command on the source device to modify the SID configuration. 3. If an OSPF-SR/ISIS-SR prefix-sid conflict occurs, an OSPF-SR / ISIS-SR prefix-sid conflict occurs between protocols or processes. In this case, run the ospf prefix-sid or isis prefix-sid command on the source device to modify the SID configuration. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: hwProtocol::Five SR protocols for initiating alarms: 1. OSPF 2. IS-IS 3. OSPF-SR 4. IS-IS-SR 5. IGP-SR | hwProcessId::Process ID | hwPrefixSid::Prefix SID | hwPrefixAddress::Prefix address | hwPrefixAddressMask::Prefix mask | hwAlgorithm::Flexible algorithm. The value ranges from 128 to 255. | hwConflictType::1. SID conflict. 2. Prefix conflict

impact_on_system: A route loop occurs, and services carried on the route are interrupted.
possible_causes: Improper configurations exist on some devices on the network. For example, the number of times for allowable local AS number repetition is set (using the peer allow-as-loop command) and the route preference is changed in a routing policy; alternatively, the AS number and route preference are changed in a routing policy. As a result, a device receives the routes that it has advertised from its BGP peers again, and the preference of the received routes is higher than that of the routes advertised by the device.
procedure: After detecting a BGP route loop, the device automatically adjusts the route selection rule to eliminate the impact of route flapping caused by the loop on services. Loops still exist between devices. In addition, the route selection rules adjusted by the system during automatic loop breaking may cause the traffic path to be different from the expected one. After the system reports an alarm, you can check the routing information about the loop based on the diagnosis log and rectify the improper configuration that causes the loop. In this way, the risk source of the loop is eliminated. After the risk source is eliminated, run the clear route loop-detect bgp alarm command in the system view of the device generating the alarm to manually clear the alarm.

description: The local device has detected an OSPF routing loop. (LoopType=[LoopType], DetectProtocolAttr=[DetectProtocolAttr], RedistributeID1=[RedistributeID1], RedistributeID2=[RedistributeID2]) The device detects an OSPF routing loop.
impact_on_system: A routing loop occurs, and services carried on the route are interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause 1: If the loop detection type is OSPF, the possible causes of the alarm are as follows: RedistributeID1 and RedistributeID2 correspond to the router ID and process ID of the OSPF processes on the two devices where a routing loop occurs. When the OSPF processes on the two devices import routes from other OSPF processes, no import policy is configured or the import policy is incorrectly configured. As a result, a routing loop occurs. Cause 2: If the loop detection type is OSPF-ISIS, the possible causes of the alarm are as follows: RedistributeID1  correspond to the System ID of the ISIS processes on the devices where a routing loop occurs, RedistributeID2 correspond to the router ID and process ID of the OSPF processes on the devices where a routing loop occurs. When the ISIS/OSPF processes on the two devices import routes from other OSPF/ISIS processes, no import policy is configured or the import policy is incorrectly configured. As a result, a routing loop occurs. Cause 3: If the loop detection type is OSPF-BGP, the possible causes of the alarm are as follows: When the BGP/OSPF processes on the two devices import routes from other OSPF/BGP processes, no import policy is configured or the import policy is incorrectly configured. As a result, a routing loop occurs. RedistributeID2 correspond to the router ID and process ID of the OSPF processes on the devices where a routing loop occurs.
procedure: Cause 1: If the loop detection type is OSPF, the possible causes of the alarm are as follows: RedistributeID1 and RedistributeID2 correspond to the router ID and process ID of the OSPF processes on the two devices where a routing loop occurs. When the OSPF processes on the two devices import routes from other OSPF processes, no import policy is configured or the import policy is incorrectly configured. As a result, a routing loop occurs. Upon detecting a routing loop on imported routes, OSPF automatically increases their costs to break the loop. This prevents the routing loop from affecting services. The original configurations that may cause risks of routing loops still exist on the two redistribution devices. In addition, the route cost adjusted by each system during automatic loop breaking may cause the traffic to be transmitted on an unexpected path. Therefore, after an alarm is reported, modify the policies for importing routes in the OSPF processes on the two devices to eliminate the risks. After the risky configurations are modified, run the clear route loop-detect ospf alarm-state command in the system view of the device that generates the alarm to manually clear the alarm and restore the costs of imported routes. Cause 2: If the loop detection type is OSPF-ISIS, the possible causes of the alarm are as follows: RedistributeID1  correspond to the System ID of the ISIS processes on the devices where a routing loop occurs, RedistributeID2 correspond to the router ID and process ID of the OSPF processes on the devices where a routing loop occurs. When the ISIS/OSPF processes on the two devices import routes from other OSPF/ISIS processes, no import policy is configured or the import policy is incorrectly configured. As a result, a routing loop occurs. Upon detecting a routing loop on imported routes, OSPF automatically increases their costs to break the loop. This prevents the routing loop from affecting services. The original configurations that may cause risks of routing loops still exist on the two redistribution devices. In addition, the route cost adjusted by each system during automatic loop breaking may cause the traffic to be transmitted on an unexpected path. Therefore, after an alarm is reported, modify the policies for importing routes in the IS-IS and OSPF processes on the two devices to eliminate the risks. After the risky configurations are modified, run the clear route loop-detect ospf alarm-state command in the system view of the device that generates the alarm to manually clear the alarm and restore the costs of imported routes. Cause 3: If the loop detection type is OSPF-BGP, the possible causes of the alarm are as follows: When the BGP/OSPF processes on the two devices import routes from other OSPF/BGP processes, no import policy is configured or the import policy is incorrectly configured. As a result, a routing loop occurs. RedistributeID2 correspond to the router ID and process ID of the OSPF processes on the devices where a routing loop occurs. Upon detecting a routing loop on imported routes, OSPF automatically increases their costs to break the loop. This prevents the routing loop from affecting services. The original configurations that may cause risks of routing loops still exist on the two redistribution devices. In addition, the route cost adjusted by each system during automatic loop breaking may cause the traffic to be transmitted on an unexpected path. Therefore, after an alarm is reported, modify the policies for importing routes in the BGP and OSPF processes on the two devices to eliminate the risks. After the risky configurations are modified, run the clear route loop-detect ospf alarm-state command in the system view of the device that generates the alarm to manually clear the alarm and restore the costs of imported routes.
parameters: LoopType::Loop detection type. | DetectProtocolAttr::Information about the loop detection protocol. | RedistributeID1::Re-advertisement device ID 1. | RedistributeID2::Re-advertisement device ID 2.

(ProcessID=[ProcessID],InstanceID=[InstanceID],PortID1=[PortID1],PortID2=[PortID2],PortID3=[PortID3],PortID4=[PortID4],PortIDFlag=[PortIDFlag],PortState=[PortState],IfIndex=[IfIndex],PortName=[PortName],PwName=[PwName]) A protocol packet loopback is detected on an STP-enabled interface.

procedure: Cause 1: Local loopback is configured on the port. 1. Check whether local loopback is configured on the port where the log is generated. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 3. 2. Delete the local loopback configuration, and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 2: A self-loop occurs on the network connected to the port. 1. Check the networking of the network connected to the port and check whether a self-loop occurs on the hub or hub. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 3. 2. Remove the self-looped network cable and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: ProcessID::ID of an MSTP process. | InstanceID::Instance ID | PortID1::Port ID 1 in an MSTP process. | PortID2::Port ID 2 in an MSTP process. | PortID3::Port ID 3 in an MSTP process. | PortID4::Port ID 4 in an MSTP process. | PortIDFlag::Port flag. | PortState::Port status. | IfIndex::Port index. | PortName::Port name. | PwName::PW name.

description: MSDP peer exit the established state. (RemoteAddr=[RemoteAddr], PeerState=[PeerState], InstanceName=[InstanceName], ExitReason=[ExitReason]) The status of the MSDP peer changes from Established to another state.
impact_on_system: The MSDP peer relationship is interrupted or fails to be established, the route is unreachable, and MSDP forwarding services are interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause 1: HoldTime expired Cause 3: Socket error Cause 4: Receive invalid TLV Cause 5: Receive notification TLV Cause 6: User operation
procedure: Cause 1: HoldTime expired 1. Run the ping command to check whether the link between the and the peer is normal. If yes, go to Step 3. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display ip routing-table command to check whether the unicast route to the peer is normal. If the route is normal, go to Step 3. If the route is abnormal, rectify the unicast route fault to clear the alarm. 3. Run the display msdp peer-status command in the MSDP view of the peer to check the status of the peer, that is, the State field. If the status is Up, go to Step 4. If the MSDP peer relationship is in the Shutdown state, run the undo shutdown command in the MSDP view of the MSDP peer to clear the alarm. If the status is Down, check the Connect interface field to see whether the IP address of the interface used to establish the TCP connection is correct. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, run the peer <peer-address> connect-interface <interface-type> <interface-number> command in the MSDP view to configure a correct IP address for the interface. In the case of other states, run the display msdp peer-status command to check whether the MSDP authentication configurations on both ends are the same. If they are the same, go to Step 4. If they are different, configure the same MSDP authentication on both ends of the peer peer-address password { cipher cipher-password | simple simple-password } or peer peer-address keychain keychain-name to clear the alarm. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 3: Socket error 1. Run the ping command to check whether the link between the MSDP peers is Up. If the link is Up, go to Step 3. If the link is Down, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display ip routing-table command to check whether the unicast route from the local device to the peer device works properly. If the route works properly, go to Step 3. If the route works improperly, you can clear the alarm by rectifying the routing fault. 3. Run the display current-configuration command to check whether multicast is enabled on both MSDP peers. If multicast is enabled on both MSDP peers, go to Step 4. If multicast is not enabled on both MSDP peers, run the multicast routing-enable command to enable multicast to clear the alarm. 4. Run the display this command in the MSDP view of both MSDP peers to check whether the MSDP peer relationship is configured. If the MSDP peer relationship is configured, go to Step 5. If no MSDP peer relationship is configured, run the peer<peer-address>connect-interface<interface-type><interface-number> command in the MSDP view to configure the MSDP peer relationship to clear the alarm. 5. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 4: Receive invalid TLV 1. The MSDP implementations on both peers may be different. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 5: Receive notification TLV 1. Check whether the reset msdp peer command is run in the user view on the peer device. If the command is run, wait till the peer relationship is re-established. If the command is not run, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display this command in the MSDP view of the peer device to check whether the MSDP peer relationship is configured. If the MSDP peer relationship is configured, go to Step 3. If no MSDP peer relationship is configured, run the peer<peer-address>connect-interface<interface-type><interface-number> command in the MSDP view to configure the MSDP peer relationship to clear the alarm. 3. Run the display interface brief command to check whether the shutdown command is run on interfaces connecting the MSDP peers. If the shutdown command is run, run the undo shutdown command in the interface view to clear the alarm. If no shutdown command is run, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 6: User operation 1. Check whether the reset msdp peer command is run in the user view. If the command is run, wait till the peer relationship is re-established. If the command is not run, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display this command in the MSDP view to check whether the MSDP peer relationship is configured. If the MSDP peer relationship is configured, go to Step 3. If no MSDP peer relationship is configured, run the peer<peer-address>connect-interface<interface-type><interface-number> command in the MSDP view to configure the MSDP peer relationship to clear the alarm. 3. Run the display interface brief command to check whether the shutdown command is configured on interfaces connecting the MSDP peers. If the shutdown command is run, run the undo shutdown command in the interface view to clear the alarm. If no shutdown command is run, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel.
parameters: RemoteAddr::MSDP peer address | PeerState::Status of the MSDP peer relationship | InstanceName::Instance name | ExitReason::Causes triggering the alarm

description: The host access interface frequently changed. (LocalIPAddress=[LocalIP], LocalBDID=[LocalBDId], LocalMAC=[LocalMAC], RemoteIPAddress=[ConflictIP], RemoteBDID=[RemoteBDId], RemoteMAC=[RemoteMAC], LocalInterface=[LocalInterface], RemoteInterface=[RemoteInterface], TunnelPeer=[TunnelPeer]) The host access interface frequently changed.
impact_on_system: This alarm may lead to interruption of user services.
possible_causes: In a BD gateway scenario, a user frequently migrates between local and remote devices or between different local EVC sub-interfaces. (The alarm reporting condition is controlled by the arp host ip-conflict-check command. By default, an alarm is reported when the number of migrations within 180s reaches 5.)
procedure: 1. Based on the alarm information, determine the IP address, BD, and access interface of the alarm user. If the alarm user's information can be determined, go to Step 2. If the alarm user's information cannot be determined, go to Step 5. 2. Based on the network plan, service deployment, and alarm user information, check the user access information on the BD gateway and the user configuration on the device connected to the user access interface. If multiple devices connected to the BD gateway are configured with the same alarm user IP address, go to Step 3. Run the debugging arp packet command in the user view to obtain ARP packets of the alarm user, and run the display arp history command in the diagnostic view to check the user change information. If the user frequently goes online between distributed gateways or between different EVC sub-interfaces on the same device, go to Step 4. If the same alarm user IP address is not configured on the devices connected to the distributed gateway and packets of the alarm user for frequent access cannot be obtained, go to Step 5. 3. Change the conflicting IP address and check whether the alarm persists.
parameters: LocalIP::Local IP address | LocalBDId::Local BD ID | LocalMAC::Local MAC address | ConflictIP::Remote IP address | RemoteBDId::Remote BD ID | RemoteMAC::Remote MAC address | LocalInterface::Local interface | RemoteInterface::Remote interface | TunnelPeer::Peer IP address of the tunnel

description: The interface turned to block state. (VLAN ID=[vlanid], Interface Name=[acifname], Block Time=[blocktime], Block Reason=[blockreason], DetectMAC=[mac]) An interface is blocked.
impact_on_system: Traffic on interface in the VLAN cannot be forwarded.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The interface has been blocked for VLAN loop, and the port has already been permanently blocked. Cause 2: The interface has been blocked for VLAN loop, and the loop has already been punished times times.
procedure: Cause 1: The interface has been blocked for VLAN loop, and the port has already been permanently blocked. 1. Run the display current-configuration command to check whether the loopback local command is configured on interfaces corresponding to the VLAN. If the loopback local command is configured on interfaces corresponding to the VLAN, delete the command configuration and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. If the loopback local command is not configured on interfaces corresponding to the VLAN, go to Step 2. 2. Log in to the device and run the reset loop-detect eth-loop vlan <vlan-id> { all | interface <interfacetype> <interfacenumber> } command to unblock the interfaces and check whether hwMflpIfBlock_clear is reported. If hwMflpVlanAcResume is not reported, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 2: The interface has been blocked for VLAN loop, and the loop has already been punished times times. 1. Run the display current-configuration command to check whether the loopback local command is configured on interfaces corresponding to the VLAN. If the loopback local command is configured on interfaces corresponding to the VLAN, delete the command configuration and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. If the loopback local command is not configured on interfaces corresponding to the VLAN, go to Step 2. 2. Check whether the interface recovers after the block-time specified in the loop-detect eth-loop command expires. If the interface does not recover, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel.
parameters: vlanid::VLAN ID | acifname::Interface name | blocktime::Blocking time | blockreason::Reason for the blocking | mac::Detected MAC address

description: The bandwidth sum of sliced sub-interfaces plus the actual effective SQ bandwidth of non-sliced sub-interfaces in an ETH-BN group is greater than the ETH-BN bandwidth. (group-name=[group-name], eth-bn-sub-interface=[eth-bn-sub-interface]) The sum of the total bandwidth of channelized sub-interfaces in the microwave bandwidth sharing group and the actual bandwidth of non-channelized sub-interface SQs was greater than the microwave bandwidth.
impact_on_system: The channelized sub-interface bandwidth cannot be guaranteed, and packet loss may occur on microwave links.
possible_causes: The bandwidth sum of sliced sub-interfaces plus the actual effective SQ bandwidth of non-sliced sub-interfaces in an ETH-BN group is greater than the ETH-BN bandwidth. Actual effective SQ bandwidth = MIN (qos-profile user-queue PIR bandwidth, MAX (10M, microwave bandwidth - bandwidth sum of sliced sub-interfaces in the ETH-BN group)).
procedure: 1. Reduce the total bandwidth of channelized sub-interfaces in the group or the configured SQ PIR of non-channelized sub-interfaces to meet the following requirement: Total bandwidth of channelized sub-interfaces + Min (10 Mbit/s, configured SQ PIR) ≤ microwave bandwidth. To reduce the total bandwidth of channelized sub-interfaces in the group, run the mode channel bandwidth <bwvalue> command in the interface view. To reduce the configured SQ PIR of non-channelized sub-interfaces, run the user-queue { cir <cir-value> pir <pir-value> | cir-percentage <percentage-value> pir-percentage <percentage-value> } command to enter the view of the QoS profile applied to the non-channelized sub-interfaces. If the alarm is cleared 1 minute later, go to Step 3. If the alarm persists after 1 minute, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: group-name::Name of a microwave bandwidth sharing group. | eth-bn-sub-interface::Non-channelized sub-interface in the bandwidth group.

description: The number of broadcast domain MAC addresses learned reached the upper threshold. (EntPhysicalIndex=[EntPhysicalIndex], PhyscialName=[PhyscialName], MacLimitVlanId=[Vlan_ID], MacLimitVsiName=[MacLimitVsiName], MacLimitBDId=[BD_ID], MacLimitEvpnName=[evpn_name], TrapSeverity=[TrapSeverity], TrapProbableCause=[TrapProbableCause], TrapEventType=[TrapEventType], MacDynAddressLearnNum=[MacDynAddressLearnNum], MacLimitMaxMac=[MacLimitMaxMac], MacLimitUpthreshold=[MacLimitUpthreshold], MacLimitDownthreshold=[MacLimitDownthreshold]). MAC address limit was configured in a broadcast domain and the alarm function for MAC address limit was enabled. When the number of learned dynamic MAC addresses reached the upper threshold, an alarm was generated.
impact_on_system: 1. If the action to be taken after the MAC address limit is reached is discard and the number of learned dynamic MAC addresses reaches the upper limit, packets with excess source MAC addresses are discarded. 2. If the action to be taken after the MAC address limit is reached is forward and the number of learned dynamic MAC addresses reaches the upper limit, packets with excess source MAC addresses are forwarded.
possible_causes: After MAC address limit was configured and the trap function for MAC address limit was enabled, the number of learned dynamic MAC addresses reached the configured upper threshold.
procedure: 1. Run the reset mac-address command in the user view to delete unnecessary MAC address entries. 2. Run the mac-limit maximum command in the VSI view to reconfigure the maximum number of MAC addresses that can be learned. After the configuration is complete, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to 4. If the alarm persists, go to 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End.
parameters: EntPhysicalIndex::Indicates the index of a physical entity. | PhyscialName::Name of a physical entity. | Vlan_ID::VLAN ID. | MacLimitVsiName::Name of a VSI. | BD_ID::BD ID. | evpn_name::EVPN name. | TrapSeverity::NMS alarm severity. | TrapProbableCause::Alarm cause value. | TrapEventType::Alarm event type. | MacDynAddressLearnNum::Number of learned MAC addresses. | MacLimitMaxMac::Maximum number of MAC addresses. | MacLimitUpthreshold::Indicates the upper MAC address learning limit. | MacLimitDownthreshold::Indicates the lower MAC address learning limit.

When a board that supports only two port queue cir configurations is inserted into the same slot as the board, the port-queue cir configurations do not take effect and a trap is generated. Cause 2: The scheduling tree of the sliced sub-interface can't be able to be created due to insufficient resources. Cause 3: During configuration restoration or board replacement, the number of queues in 4-CoS mode configured based on the board exceeds the upper limit. Cause 4: During configuration restoration or board replacement, the number of uplink queues in enhanced 8-CoS mode configured based on the board exceeds the upper limit. procedure: Cause 1: When more than two port queue cir configurations are configured on a board, the function is normal. When a board that supports only two port queue cir configurations is inserted into the same slot as the board, the port-queue cir configurations do not take effect and a trap is generated. 1. Switch the PQ CIR configurations to another board that supports more than two PQs, or change the number of PQ CIR configurations of all interfaces on the board to a value less than or equal to 2. 2. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 2: The scheduling tree of the sliced sub-interface can't be able to be created due to insufficient resources. 1. Check whether the number of configured channelized sub-interfaces exceeds the board specifications. If yes, switch some channelized sub-interface configurations to another board and go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 3: During configuration restoration or board replacement, the number of queues in 4-CoS mode configured based on the board exceeds the upper limit. 1. Check whether the number of 4-CoS queue resources configured on the board exceeds the board's specification. If yes, decrease the value of <4cos-size> in the qos user-queue resource 4cos <4cos-size> command based on the specification. Then, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support engineers. 4. End. Cause 4: During configuration restoration or board replacement, the number of uplink queues in enhanced 8-CoS mode configured based on the board exceeds the upper limit. 1. Check whether the number of enhanced 8-CoS upstream queue resources configured on the board exceeds the board's specification. If yes, decrease the value of <8cos-enhance-size> in the qos user-queue resource 8cos-enhance <8cos-enhance-size> inbound command based on the specification. Then, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support engineers. 4. End. Cause 5: During configuration restoration or board replacement, the number of downlink queues in enhanced 8-CoS mode exceeds the upper limit. 1. Check whether the number of enhanced 8-CoS downstream queue resources configured on the board exceeds the board's specification. If yes, decrease the value of <8cos-enhance-size> in the qos user-queue resource 8cos-enhance <8cos-enhance-size> outbound command based on the specification. Then, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support engineers. 4. End. Cause 7: During configuration restoration or board replacement, the microburst monitoring function of queues does not take effect. 1. Check whether the qos micro-burst queue-monitor command is configured on the interface. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 4. 2. Check whether the board supports microburst monitoring for queues on the interface. If so, go to Step 4. If not, delete the corresponding microburst monitoring configuration and go to Step 3. 3. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 8: During configuration restoration or board replacement, the buffer mode adjustment function does not take effect. 1. Check whether the qos buffer mode inbound command is run in the slot view to configure buffer mode adjustment. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 4. 2. Check whether the board supports buffer mode adjustment. If so, go to Step 4. If not, delete the buffer mode adjustment configuration and go to Step 3. 3. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 5. End. Cause 9: Chip failure, basic forwarding function abnormal. 1. Restart the board. After the board is registered, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 3. End. Cause 10: During configuration restoration or board replacement, the PFC function does not take effect. 1. Check whether the qos pfc enable <pfc-name> command is run on the interface. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 4. 2. Check the lossless capability of PFC and determine whether the board supports the PFC function. If so, go to Step 4. If not, delete the PFC configuration and go to Step 3. 3. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 5. End.

Cause 2: An interface connected to the MPLS tunnel is shut down so that no CC message can be transmitted. Cause 3: The MPLS tunnel is congested so that no CC message can be transmitted. Cause 4: The MPLS tunnel is deteriorated so that no CC message can be transmitted.

Reconfigure the CC function on the ingress and egress MEGs. Then check whether MPLS_LSPM_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.121.2.1.19 hwMplsOamLossRecovery is reported. If so, go to Step 7. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display interface command to check whether any physical interface connected to the MPLS tunnel is shut down.

description: The number of LSAs learned by OSPFv3 exceeded the threshold. (Ospfv3ProcessId=[hwOspfv3ProcessId], Ospfv3RecvLsaUpper=[hwOspfv3RecvLsaUpper]) This alarm is reported when the number of LSAs learned by an OSPFv3 process exceeds the threshold.

procedure: 1. Run the display ospfv3 command and check the Alarm Status field in the command output to determine whether the number of LSAs exceeds the alarm threshold. (Normal indicates that the number of LSAs is less than 90% of the alarm threshold. Exceed indicates that the number of LSAs reaches or exceeds the alarm threshold.) If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 4. 2. In the OSPFv3 process that reports the alarm, run the display this command to check whether no import policy is configured for the source device that advertises LSAs or whether the import policy is improper. If so, a large number of LSAs may be imported, causing the local device to learn a large number of LSAs. If no import policy is configured, run the import-route command to configure a policy to limit the routes to be imported. After the configuration is complete, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, no further action is required. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. If an import policy is configured but its configuration is improper, run the import-route command to modify the policy. After the configuration is complete, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, no further action is required. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. If the import policy is correctly configured, go to Step 3. 3. Run the maximum received-lsa threshold <value> command to adjust the threshold of learned LSAs and then check whether the alarm is cleared.
parameters: hwOspfv3ProcessId::ID of an OSPFv3 process. | hwOspfv3RecvLsaUpper::Upper threshold for LSAs learned by OSPFv3.

(hwOspfv2ProcessIdIndex=[hwOspfv2ProcessIdIndex], hwOspfv2AreaId=[hwOspfv2AreaId], hwOspfv2Threshold=[hwOspfv2Threshold]) The number of NSSA LSAs generated when an OSPF process imported external routes exceeded the upper alarm threshold (in percentage) multiplied by the maximum number allowed.
impact_on_system: The network stability may be adversely affected.
possible_causes: The number of NSSA LSAs generated when an OSPF process imported external routes exceeded the upper alarm threshold (in percentage) multiplied by the maximum number allowed.
procedure: 1. Run the display ospf brief command to check whether the number of NSSA LSAs generated when OSPF imports routes exceeds the upper alarm threshold. The Current status field in the display ospf brief command output shows the overload status. Normal indicates that the number is less than the lower alarm threshold. Approach limit indicates that the number reaches 90% of the upper alarm threshold. Exceed limit indicates that the number reaches or exceeds the maximum number. If the threshold is exceeded, this message is informational only, and no action is required. If the threshold is not exceeded yet, go to Step 2. 2. Perform the following operations as required: If a change in the maximum number of NSSA LSAs generated when OSPF imports routes is allowed, run the import-route limit <limit-number> [ threshold-alarm upper-limit <upper-limit-value> lower-limit <lower-limit-value> ] command to change the maximum number. If a change in the maximum number of NSSA LSAs generated when OSPF imports routes is not allowed, go to Step 3. 3. Contact technical support personnel.
parameters: hwOspfv2ProcessIdIndex::Indicates the OSPF process ID. | hwOspfv2AreaId::Indicates the ID of an OSPF area. | hwOspfv2Threshold::Indicates the upper alarm threshold for the number of NSSA LSAs generated when an OSPF process imports external routes.

The resource ID in the segment list of the SR Policy is the same as the Binding SID of the SR Policy. 4. The resource ID in the segment list of the SR Policy is used by non-SR Policy services.

If the alarm persists, collect alarm and configuration information and contact technical support.

Cause 3: The link group fault causes IS-IS to adjust the link cost. 1. Run the display isis link-group command to check the status of the IS-IS link group and information about the member interfaces in the link group. description: Package verification failed.(PhysicalName=[PhysicalName], PackageName=[PackageName], FailReason=[FailReason]) Failed to verify the package. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Cause 1: The digital signature of the system software package failed to be verified. Services are not affected. Cause 2: The digital signature of the patch package failed to be verified. Services are not affected. Cause 3: The digital signature of the feature package failed to be verified. Services are not affected. Cause 4: The digital signature of the system software package failed to be verified at the startup stage. The upgrade fails. Roll back to the source version. Cause 5: The digital signature of the patch package failed to be verified at the startup stage. The patch package is not loaded.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The digital signature of the system software package failed to be verified. Cause 2: The digital signature of the patch package failed to be verified. Cause 3: The digital signature of the feature package failed to be verified. Cause 4: The digital signature of the system software package failed to be verified at the startup stage. Cause 5: The digital signature of the patch package failed to be verified at the startup stage.
procedure: Cause 1: The digital signature of the system software package failed to be verified. 1. The digital signature verification of the running software package has expired. The software package is uninstalled. 2. The digital signature verification of the system software package for next startup expires. Reconfigure the system software package for next startup. Cause 2: The digital signature of the patch package failed to be verified. 1. Run the clear alarm active command in the alarm management view to manually clear the alarm. 2. If the digital signature of the current patch package expires, run the patch delete all command in the user view to uninstall the patch package. 3. If the digital signature of the patch package for next startup expires, run the startup patch all command in the user view to reset the patch package for next startup. 4. Run the display alarm active verbose command in the user view to check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 6. If not, go to Step 5. 5. Collect log files and contact technical engineers. 6. End. Cause 3: The digital signature of the feature package failed to be verified. If the digital signature verification of the running (next startup) feature package has expired: 1. Uninstall the feature package. 2. Clear the feature package for the next startup. 3. Specify another feature package for next startup. 4. Upgrade the feature package. Cause 4: The digital signature of the system software package failed to be verified at the startup stage. 1. After the device is started, reset the software package for next startup. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information and contact technical engineers. 3. End. Cause 5: The digital signature of the patch package failed to be verified at the startup stage. 1. After the device is started, run the patch delete all command to delete the current and next-startup patch packages. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information and contact technical engineers. 3. End.
parameters: PhysicalName::Indicates an entity name. | PackageName::Software package name | FailReason::Indicates the error cause.

description: MEP received a CCM with unexpected MAC address. (MdIndex=[MdIndex], MaIndex=[MaIndex], MdName=[MdName], MaName=[MaName], MepId=[MepId], RmepId=[RmepId]) The source MAC address carried in a CCM sent by the RMEP was different from the RMEP's MAC address specified on the MEP.

possible_causes: The source MAC address carried in a CCM sent by the RMEP was different from the RMEP's MAC address specified on the MEP under the following conditions: The MEP and RMEP had the same MD level. The MEP and RMEP had the same MA ID. The MEP ID carried in the received CCMs was listed in the RMEP list on the MEP. The MEP was enabled to receive CCMs. The MEP and RMEP had the same interval at which CCMs were sent.
procedure: 1. Run the cfm md <md-name> command on the MEP to enter the MD view. Run the display this command on the MEP to view the RMEP's MAC address. Run the display cfm mep [ md <md-name> [ ma <ma-name> [ mep-id <mep-id> ] ] ] command on the RMEP to check the value of the MAC field. Check whether the value of the MAC field on the RMEP is the same as the RMEP's MAC address on the MEP. a. Run the cfm md <md-name> command on the MEP to enter the MD view. b. Run the display this command on the MEP to view the RMEP's MAC address. c. Run the display cfm mep [ md <md-name> [ ma <ma-name> [ mep-id <mep-id> ] ] ] command on the RMEP to check the value of the MAC field. d. Check whether the value of the MAC field on the RMEP is the same as the RMEP's MAC address on the MEP. If yes, go to Step 3. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Perform the following operations: a. Run the undo remote-mep mep-id <mep-id> command to delete the existing RMEP configuration. b. Run the remote-mep mep-id <rmep-id> command to rebind the RMEP to the MAC address. c. Run the display alarm active command to check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.

impact_on_system: The network stability may be adversely affected.
possible_causes: The number of ASE LSAs generated when an OSPF process imported external routes reached or exceeded the maximum number allowed.
procedure: 1. Run the display ospf brief command to check whether the number of ASE LSAs generated when OSPF imports routes reaches or exceeds the maximum number allowed. The Current status field in the display ospf brief command output shows the overload status. Normal indicates that the number is less than the lower alarm threshold. Approach limit indicates that the number reaches 90% of the upper alarm threshold. Exceed limit indicates that the number reaches or exceeds the maximum number. If the maximum number is exceeded, this message is informational only, and no action is required. If the maximum number is not exceeded yet, go to Step 2. 2. Perform the following operations as required: If a change in the maximum number of ASE LSAs generated when OSPF imports routes is allowed, run the import-route limit <limit-number> [ threshold-alarm upper-limit <upper-limit-value> lower-limit <lower-limit-value> ] command to change the maximum number. If a change in the maximum number of ASE LSAs generated when OSPF imports routes is not allowed, go to Step 3. 3. Contact technical support personnel.
parameters: hwOspfv2ProcessIdIndex::Indicates the OSPF process ID. | hwOspfv2MaxLimit::Indicates the maximum value for the number of ASE LSAs generated when an OSPF process imports external routes.

description: The IPv4 status changes. (ifName=[ifName], OperStatus=[ifOperStatus], Reason=[Reason]) The IPv4 status of the interface changed.
impact_on_system: The interface cannot forward packets normally.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The interface link status is down. Cause 2: The interface is a layer 2 interface. Cause 3: The interface protocol status is down. Cause 4: The IPv4 address of the interface conflicts with that of another interface.
procedure: Cause 1: The interface link status is down. 1. Check whether the hardware such as the network cable or optical module is loose or disconnected. If the physical link is not working properly, reconnect the physical link and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. If the physical link is working properly, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 2: The interface is a layer 2 interface. 1. Run the display this command in the interface view to check whether the interface is a Layer 2 interface. If the interface is a Layer 2 interface, run the undo portswitch command to switch the interface to a Layer 3 interface. If the interface is not a Layer 2 interface, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 3: The interface protocol status is down. 1. Run the display this interface command in the interface view to check the protocol status of the interface. If the protocol status of the interface is Down, go to step 2. If the protocol status of the interface is Up, go to step 3. 2. Run the display this command in the interface view to check whether ARP probe (arp status-detect) is configured on the interface. If ARP probe is configured, go to step 3. If ARP probe is not configured, go to step 4. 3. Run the display this command in the interface view to check the IP address for ARP probe. If a nonexistent peer IP address is detected, run the undo arp status-detect command to clear the configuration. If the detected IP address is correct, go to step 4. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 4: The IPv4 address of the interface conflicts with that of another interface. 1. Run the undo ip address command in the interface view to delete the conflicting IP address. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, no further action is required. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: ifName::Interface name | ifOperStatus::Current status of an interface. | Reason::Alarm cause.

procedure: 1.Check whether any optical fiber is connected to the optical interface. If no optical fiber is used, shut down the laser of the optical interface and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 2.Check whether the optical fiber is broken. If the optical fiber is broken, replace the optical fiber and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm persists, go to Step 9. 3.Check whether the receive optical power of the local device is less than the minimum value. If the receive optical power is less than the minimum value, clean the optical fiber connector and the optical interface on the interface board. Check that the flange and the optical attenuator are properly connected and the optical attenuator value is in the normal range. Then check whether the alarm is cleared.

description: PIM neighbor loss. (NbrIntIndex=[NbrIntIndex], NbrAddrType=[NbrAddrType], NbrAddr=[NbrAddr], NbrUpTime=[NbrUpTime], NbrIntName=[NbrIntName], InstanceID=[InstanceID], InstanceName=[InstanceName], NeighborLossReason=[NeighborLossReason]) After receiving a Hello message from a neighbor, a device recorded information about this neighbor and started a timer for this neighbor. If the device received no Hello packet before the timer expired, the device considered the neighbor lost, and thereby reported a trap message.
impact_on_system: The PIM neighbor relationship is interrupted or fails to be established, the route is unreachable, and data forwarding services are interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Neighbor timer expired. Cause 3: Interface is down. Cause 5: Neighbor is deleted. Cause 7: Receive hello cancel message. Cause 8: BFD session is down.
procedure: Cause 1: Neighbor timer expired. 1. Run the ping or ping ipv6 command to check whether the link between PIM neighbors is Up. If the link is Up, go to Step 3. If the link is Down, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display ip routing-table or display ipv6 routing-table command to check whether the unicast route from the local device to the neighbor works properly. If the route works properly, go to Step 3. If the route works improperly, you can clear the alarm by rectifying the routing fault. 3. Run the display this command in the view of the corresponding PIM neighboring interface to check whether the interface is enabled with PIM-SM. If PIM-SM is enabled on the neighboring interface, the IP address of the neighboring interface changes. If the PIM neighbor relationship is not re-established after a certain period, go to Step 4. If PIM-SM is not enabled on the neighboring interface, configure the interface enable with PIM-SM. 4. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. Cause 3: Interface is down. 1. Run the display interface brief or display ipv6 interface brief command on the device to check whether the protocol layer status of the interface is Up. If the protocol status is Up, go to Step 2. If the protocol layer status is Down, run the ip address or ipv6 address command to configure an IP address for the interface. If the interface is Down, run the undo shutdown command. 2. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 5: Neighbor is deleted. 1. Run the ping or ping ipv6 command to check whether the link between the device and its neighbor is normal. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, check the interface status. 2. Run the display ip routing-table or display ipv6 routing-table command to check whether the unicast route to the neighbor is normal. If yes, go to Step 3. If no, rectify the unicast route fault to clear the alarm. 3. Run the display this command in the corresponding interface view to check whether pim neighbor-policy or pim ipv6 neighbor-policy is configured on the interface. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 5. 4. Run the display acl or display acl ipv6 command to check whether the ACL configuration meets requirements. If yes, go to Step 5. If no, reconfigure the ACL rules. 5. Run the display this command in the corresponding interface view to check whether pim silent or pim ipv6 silent is configured on the interface. If yes, delete the pim silent or pim ipv6 silent configuration. If no, go to Step 6. 6. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 7: Receive hello cancel message. 1. Run the display this command in the interface view of the neighbor to check whether PIM SM or PIM IPv6 SM is enabled on the interface. If PIM SM or PIM IPv6 SM is enabled, go to step 2. If PIM-SM or IPv6 PIM-SM is not enabled on the interface, run the pim sm or pim ipv6 sm command on the interface. 2. Run the display ip interface brief or display ipv6 interface brief command to check whether the interface status is Up and whether the interface is configured with an IP address. If the protocol status is Up, go to Step 3. If the protocol status is Down, run the ip address or ipv6 address command to configure an IP address for the interface. If the interface is Down, run the undo shutdown command. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 8: BFD session is down. 1. Run the display this command in the interface view of the neighbor to check whether PIM SM or PIM IPv6 SM is enabled on the interface. If PIM SM or PIM IPv6 SM is enabled, go to step 2. If PIM-SM or IPv6 PIM-SM is not enabled on the interface, run the pim sm or pim ipv6 sm command on the interface. 2. Run the display ip interface brief or display ipv6 interface brief command to check whether the interface status is Up. If the protocol status is Up, go to Step 3. If the protocol status is Down, run the ip address or ipv6 address command to configure an IP address for the interface. If the interface is Down, run the undo shutdown command. 3. Check whether the route to the peer device is normal using the display ip routing-table or display ipv6 routing-table command. If the route is normal, go to Step 4. If the route is abnormal, configure a route to the peer device. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: NbrIntIndex::Index of the interface where the neighbor relationship is established. | NbrAddrType::Address type of the neighbor: 0: MIB_ADDRESSTYPE_UNKNOWN 1: MIB_ADDRESSTYPE_IPV4 2: MIB_ADDRESSTYPE_IPV6 3: MIB_ADDRESSTYPE_IPV4Z 4: MIB_ADDRESSTYPE_IPV6Z 16: MIB_ADDRESSTYPE_DNS 17: MIB_ADDRESSTYPE_MAX | NbrAddr::Neighbor address. | NbrUpTime::Time when the neighbor relationship has been established (in centiseconds) | NbrIntName::Name of the interface where the neighbor relationship is established. | InstanceID::Instance index. | InstanceName::Instance name. | NeighborLossReason::Reason why the neighbor relationship is unavailable.

description: L3 loop detect alarmed. (ChassisID=[hwL3LoopDetectChassisID], Slot=[hwL3LoopDetectSlotID], IP=[hwL3LoopDetectIPAddr]) Layer 3 loop detection detected route loops. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Routing loops affect packet forwarding paths.
possible_causes: When a routing loop occurs, a large number of TTL timeout packets are generated on the network. If the number of TTL timeout packets sent to the CPU is greater than or equal to 6000 within 1 minute, a 1-minute timer is started for sampling and analysis. If the number of packets reaches 1024 or the number of packets exceeds 100 when the timer expires, the destination IP addresses of top 5 packets are tracerted one by one. If a routing loop exists, an alarm is generated.
procedure: 1. Tracert the destination address of the route displayed in the alarm to check whether a loop occurs on the link. If a loop exists, remove the loop. If the alarm is cleared after the loop is removed, go to Step 3. If the alarm persists after the loop is removed, go to Step 2. If no loop exists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End.
parameters: hwL3LoopDetectChassisID::Chassis ID. | hwL3LoopDetectSlotID::Board ID. | hwL3LoopDetectIPAddr::IP address.

description: The number of public IPv6 prefixes exceeded the threshold. (PrefixCount=[PrefixCount], Threshold=[Threshold]) The number of IPv6 public route prefixes exceeded the value calculated using the formula (Maximum number x Threshold/100).
impact_on_system: The number of IPv6 public route prefixes exceeded the value calculated using the formula (Maximum number x Threshold/100), and services may be affected if the number of IPv6 public route prefixes keeps increasing.
possible_causes: Cause 1: A large number of IPv6 routes were added to the routing table. Cause 2: The threshold of the number of IPv6 public route prefixes was decreased.
procedure: 1. Run the display ipv6 routing-table statistics command to check the total number of public network route prefixes and the number of routes that each protocol has added to the IPv6 routing table. Run the display ipv6 routing-table limit command to check the total number of existing public network route prefixes and the configured limit on the number of route prefixes. Cause 2: A service status availability ACK message is not received 30 minutes after service status becomes available. Perform an active/standby switchover or restart the device to check whether data synchronization is restored. Cause 3: Data synchronization between the active and standby components is incomplete. description: The local device has detected an OSPFv3 routing loop. (LoopType=[LoopType], DetectProtocolAttr=[DetectProtocolAttr], RedistributeID1=[RedistributeID1], RedistributeID2=[RedistributeID2]) The device detects an OSPFv3 routing loop.
impact_on_system: A routing loop occurs, and services carried on the route are interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause 1: If the loop detection type is OSPFv3, the possible causes of the alarm are as follows: RedistributeID1 and RedistributeID2 correspond to the router ID and process ID of the OSPFv3 processes on the two devices where a routing loop occurs. When the OSPFv3 processes on the two devices import routes from other OSPFv3 processes, no import policy is configured or the import policy is incorrectly configured. As a result, a routing loop occurs. Cause 2: If the loop detection type is OSPFv3-ISIS, the possible causes of the alarm are as follows: RedistributeID1  correspond to the System ID of the ISIS processes on the devices where a routing loop occurs, RedistributeID2 correspond to the router ID and process ID of the OSPFv3 processes on the devices where a routing loop occurs. When the ISIS/OSPFv3 processes on the two devices import routes from other OSPFv3/ISIS processes, no import policy is configured or the import policy is incorrectly configured. As a result, a routing loop occurs. Cause 3: If the loop detection type is OSPFv3-BGP, the possible causes of the alarm are as follows: When the BGP/OSPFv3 processes on the two devices import routes from other OSPFv3/BGP processes, no import policy is configured or the import policy is incorrectly configured. As a result, a routing loop occurs. RedistributeID2 correspond to the router ID and process ID of the OSPFv3 processes on the devices where a routing loop occurs.
procedure: Cause 1: If the loop detection type is OSPFv3, the possible causes of the alarm are as follows: RedistributeID1 and RedistributeID2 correspond to the router ID and process ID of the OSPFv3 processes on the two devices where a routing loop occurs. When the OSPFv3 processes on the two devices import routes from other OSPFv3 processes, no import policy is configured or the import policy is incorrectly configured. As a result, a routing loop occurs. After detecting a loop on an imported route, OSPFv3 automatically increases the cost of the imported route to attempt to eliminate the loop. In this manner, the impact of the loop on services is automatically eliminated. The original risk source of the routing loop caused by the two re-advertisement devices still exists. In addition, the route cost adjusted by the system during automatic loop prevention may cause the traffic path to be different from the planned path. Therefore, after the system reports the alarm, modify the policy for importing routes in the OSPFv3 processes on the two re-advertisement devices as soon as possible to eliminate the risk source that causes routing loops. You can run the display ospfv3 process-id import-route loop-detect state command to view information about the routes that have encountered loops and are automatically removed. process-id specifies the process ID in the alarm parameter loop detection protocol information. Cause 2: If the loop detection type is OSPFv3-ISIS, the possible causes of the alarm are as follows: RedistributeID1  correspond to the System ID of the ISIS processes on the devices where a routing loop occurs, RedistributeID2 correspond to the router ID and process ID of the OSPFv3 processes on the devices where a routing loop occurs. When the ISIS/OSPFv3 processes on the two devices import routes from other OSPFv3/ISIS processes, no import policy is configured or the import policy is incorrectly configured. As a result, a routing loop occurs. After detecting a loop on an imported route, OSPFv3 automatically increases the cost of the imported route to attempt to eliminate the loop. In this manner, the impact of the loop on services is automatically eliminated. The original risk source of the routing loop caused by the two re-advertisement devices still exists. In addition, the route cost adjusted by the system during automatic loop prevention may cause the traffic path to be different from the planned path. Therefore, after the system reports the alarm, modify the route import policy configuration in the IS-IS and OSPFv3 processes on the two re-advertisement devices as soon as possible to eliminate the risk source that causes routing loops. You can run the display ospfv3 process-id import-route loop-detect state command to view information about the routes that have encountered loops and are automatically removed. process-id specifies the process ID in the alarm parameter loop detection protocol information. After eliminating the risk source that causes the loop, run the clear route loop-detect ospfv3 alarm-state command in the system view of the device that generates the alarm to clear the alarm and restore the cost of the imported route to the normal value. Cause 3: If the loop detection type is OSPFv3-BGP, the possible causes of the alarm are as follows: When the BGP/OSPFv3 processes on the two devices import routes from other OSPFv3/BGP processes, no import policy is configured or the import policy is incorrectly configured. As a result, a routing loop occurs. RedistributeID2 correspond to the router ID and process ID of the OSPFv3 processes on the devices where a routing loop occurs. After detecting a loop on an imported route, OSPFv3 automatically increases the cost of the imported route to attempt to eliminate the loop. In this manner, the impact of the loop on services is automatically eliminated. The original risk source of the routing loop caused by the two re-advertisement devices still exists. In addition, the route cost adjusted by the system during automatic loop prevention may cause the traffic path to be different from the planned path. Therefore, after the system reports the alarm, modify the policy for importing routes in the BGP and OSPFv3 processes on the two re-advertisement devices as soon as possible to eliminate the risk source that causes routing loops. You can run the display ospfv3 process-id import-route loop-detect state command to view information about the routes that have encountered loops and are automatically removed. process-id specifies the process ID in the alarm parameter loop detection protocol information. After eliminating the risk source that causes the loop, run the clear route loop-detect ospfv3 alarm-state command in the system view of the device that generates the alarm to clear the alarm and restore the cost of the imported route to the normal value.
parameters: LoopType::Routing loop detection type. | DetectProtocolAttr::Information about the loop detection protocol. | RedistributeID1::Re-advertise device ID 1. | RedistributeID2::Re-advertise device ID 2.

description: The Y.1731 statistic value exceeded the upper limit value. (MdIndex=[MdIndex], MaIndex=[MaIndex], MepID=[MepID], Type=[Type], MAC=[MAC], Priority=[Priority], MdName=[MdName], MaName=[MaName], Value=[Value], UpperLimitThreshold=[UpperLimitThreshold], LowerLimitThreshold=[LowerLimitThreshold], ValueHigh=[ValueHigh], ValueLow=[ValueLow]) The Y.1731 performance statistic value exceeded the upper alarm threshold.
impact_on_system: Services are not affected.
possible_causes: The Y.1731 statistic value exceeded the upper limit value.
procedure: 1. Check the Type field in the alarm information, and perform the following operations based on the value of the Type field: If the value of Type is 0, a one-way frame delay alarm is detected. Go to Step 2. If the value of Type is 1, a two-way frame delay alarm is detected. Go to Step 3. If the value of Type is 2, a one-way delay jitter alarm is detected. Go to Step 4. If the value of Type is 3, a two-way frame delay jitter alarm is detected. Go to Step 5. If the value of Type is 4, a near-end frame loss rate alarm in single-ended frame loss measurement is detected. Go to Step 6. If the value of Type is 5, a far-end frame loss rate alarm in single-ended frame loss measurement is detected. Go to Step 7. If the value of Type is 6, a near-end frame loss rate alarm in dual-ended frame loss measurement is detected. Go to Step 8. If the value of Type is 7, a far-end frame loss rate alarm in dual-ended frame loss measurement is detected. Go to Step 9. 2. Run the display y1731 threshold-info onedelay-threshold md <md-name> ma <ma-name> mep-id <mep-id> [ 8021p <8021p-value> ] command to check the values of UpperLimit and LowerLimit. Check whether the upper threshold is too small. If yes, run the delay-measure one-way delay-threshold mep <mep-id> upper-limit <upper-limit> lower-limit <lower-limit> [ 8021p <8021p-value> ] command to reconfigure the upper threshold. Go to Step 10. If no, go to Step 11. 3. Run the display y1731 threshold-info twodelay-threshold md <md-name> ma <ma-name> mep-id <mep-id> [ 8021p <8021p-value> ] command to check the values of UpperLimit and LowerLimit.
