description: The CGN configurations of the master and backup devices are inconsistent. (ConfigurationItem=[ConfigurationItem],ItemName=[ItemName],ItemId=[ItemId],Description=[Description]) CGN configurations on the active and standby chassis for inter-chassis backup were inconsistent. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Cause 1: The PCP server configurations in the instances on the active and standby chassis are inconsistent. PCP traffic is abnormal. Cause 2: The section configurations of the static global address pools in the active and standby chassis are inconsistent. After an active/standby switchover, traffic may be abnormal. Cause 3: The global address pools in the active and standby chassis do not function with one adopting the active role and the other adopting the standby role. The global address pools on the active and standby chassis may assign different address segments to instances. As a result, traffic may be abnormal after an active/standby switchover. Cause 4: The lengths of the initial and extended address segments assigned by the global address pool in the active chassis to the service-location group of the instance are different from those assigned by the global address pool in the standby chassis. The global address pools on the active and standby chassis may assign different address segments to instances. As a result, traffic may be abnormal after an active/standby switchover. Cause 5: The block address segments assigned by the global address pools in the active and standby chassis are inconsistent. The block address segments allocated by the global address pools of the active and standby chassis are different. As a result, traffic may be abnormal after an active/standby switchover.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The PCP server configurations in the instances on the active and standby chassis are inconsistent. Cause 2: The section configurations of the static global address pools in the active and standby chassis are inconsistent. Cause 3: The global address pools in the active and standby chassis do not function with one adopting the active role and the other adopting the standby role. Cause 4: The lengths of the initial and extended address segments assigned by the global address pool in the active chassis to the service-location group of the instance are different from those assigned by the global address pool in the standby chassis. Cause 5: The block address segments assigned by the global address pools in the active and standby chassis are inconsistent.
procedure: Cause 1: The PCP server configurations in the instances on the active and standby chassis are inconsistent. 1. Run the pcp server ipv4 ipv4-address { mask | mask-len } or pcp server ipv6 ipv6-address prefix-length command to configure the same PCP server for the instance on the active and standby chassis. 2. After 15 minutes, check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, the fault is rectified. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 2: The section configurations of the static global address pools in the active and standby chassis are inconsistent. 1. Run section(nat-ip-pool) to configure the same section for the global static address pools on the active and standby chassis. 2. After 30 minutes, check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, the fault is rectified. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 3: The global address pools in the active and standby chassis do not function with one adopting the active role and the other adopting the standby role. 1. Change the active/standby role of the global address pool on the active/standby chassis according to the alarm information so that the global address pools in the active and standby chassis function with one adopting the active role and the other adopting the standby role. 2. After 15 minutes, check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, the fault is rectified. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 4: The lengths of the initial and extended address segments assigned by the global address pool in the active chassis to the service-location group of the instance are different from those assigned by the global address pool in the standby chassis. 1. Run the nat-instance subnet length command to configure the same lengths of the initial and extended address segments assigned by the global address pool in the active chassis to the service-location group of the instance as those assigned by the global address pool in the standby chassis. 2. After 15 minutes, check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, the fault is rectified. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. Cause 5: The block address segments assigned by the global address pools in the active and standby chassis are inconsistent. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: ConfigurationItem::Configuration item | ItemName::Configuration item name | ItemId::Configuration item ID | Description::Description

description: The number of user resources on the board or the device reached the threshold. (Type=[type],Slot=[slotid],MaxUserThreshold=[threshold]) The number of user resources on a board or device reached the threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: When the number of user resources reaches the threshold, subsequent users may fail to go online.
possible_causes: Cause 1:The number of access users exceeded the threshold. Cause 2:The threshold was set too small.
procedure: 1. Run the display current-configuration command in the system view to check whether the user resource threshold (dhcp-user-slot-warning-threshold/ppp-user-slot-warning-threshold/dhcp-user-warning-threshold/ppp-user-warning-threshold) is too small. If the number of users on a board exceeds the threshold, run the display access-user slot slot-id command in the system view to check the number of current users. If the number of users is close to the maximum number of users on the board, replace the board with a board with a larger number of users. 3. If global user resources exceed the threshold, run the display access-user command in the system view to check the number of current users. If the number of user resources is close to the maximum number of user resources supported by the device, add an interface board or go to Step 5. 4. Check whether the alarm is cleared.

description: The control-tunnel connection was Down. (IP Type=[ControlTunnelIpType], Local IP=[ControlTunnelLocalIp], Remote IP=[ControlTunnelRemoteIp], VrfName=[VrfName], DatapathId=[DatapathId], AuxiliaryId=[AuxiliaryId], SubReason=[SubReason], Reason=[Reason]) The control channel was disconnected. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The control channel is disconnected. As a result, services that depend on the control tunnel are abnormal.
possible_causes: Cause 1: TCP DOWN. Cause 2: Heartbeat Timeout. Cause 3: PDU Invalid.
procedure: Cause 1: TCP DOWN. 1. Check whether the controller configuration of the control tunnel is changed and whether the control tunnel configuration is deleted or modified. If yes, correct the configuration of the control tunnel. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Run the ping command on both ends of the control tunnel session to check whether the network is connected. If yes, go to Step 3. If no, rectify the network connection fault. After the connectivity fault is rectified, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display control-tunnel session command to check the status of the control tunnel session. If the control tunnel session is not in the REGISTERED state, go to Step 4. If the control tunnel session is in the REGISTERED state, go to Step 5. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 2: Heartbeat Timeout. 1. Run the ping command on both ends of the control tunnel session to check whether the network is connected. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, rectify the network connection fault. After the connectivity fault is rectified, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display control-tunnel session command to check the status of the control tunnel session. If the status of the control tunnel session is not REGISTERED, go to Step 3. If the status of the control tunnel session is REGISTERED, go to Step 4. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 3: PDU Invalid. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: ControlTunnelIpType::IP address type. | ControlTunnelLocalIp::Local IP address. | ControlTunnelRemoteIp::Remote IP address. | VrfName::Index of the VRF where the control channel resides. | DatapathId::Unique ID of a control channel. | AuxiliaryId::Auxiliary connection ID. | SubReason::Detailed cause of the control channel disconnection. | Reason::Reason why the session goes down.

description: The number of user resources on the board reached the threshold. (Slot=[slotid],SlotMaxUserThreshold=[threshold]) The number of user resources on the board reached the threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: When the number of user resources reaches the threshold, subsequent users may fail to go online.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The number of access users exceeded the threshold. Cause 2: The threshold was set too small.
procedure: 1. Run the display this command in the system view to check whether the user resource threshold (slot-warning-threshold) is too small. If yes, set it to an expected value. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display access-user slot slot-id command in the system view to check the number of current user resources. If the number of current user resources is close to the maximum number of user resources on a board, replace the board with a board with a larger number of user resources or go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End.
parameters: slotid::Slot ID of the board through which users go online | threshold::User resource threshold

description: The resource of users or cpu usage on the device reached the upper threshold. (Slot=[slotId],Cpu usage=[cpuUsage],User resource usage=[usrResUsage]) The user resource or CPU usage reached the upper limit. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.

procedure: 1. Run the display this command in the system view to check whether the value of upper-limit configured for access-user exhaust threshold-alarm { main-resource-usage | slot-resource-usage | main-cpu-usage | slot-cpu-usage } upper-limit < upper-limit> lower-limit < lower-limit> is too small. If yes, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 3. 2. Run the access-user exhaust threshold-alarm command in the system view to reconfigure the alarm threshold (upper-limit). Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 5. If not, go to Step 4. 3. Run the display access-user [ slot < slot-id > ] command in the system view to check the Total user field, which displays the number of current users on the board in the specified slot or on the device.
parameters: slotId::Slot ID | cpuUsage::CPU usage | usrResUsage::User resource usage

description: External interface status is down. (ApAdminIp=[ApAdminIp], IfName=[IfName], IfIndex=[IfIndex], IfAdminStatus=[IfAdminStatus], IfOperStatus=[IfOperStatus], Reason=[Reason]) The external communication interface went Down. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The interface cannot forward packets, and services on the interface will be interrupted.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Interface physical link is down Cause 2: The interface is deleted
procedure: Cause 1: Interface physical link is down 1. Run the display this command on the master's remote interface for external communication interface to check whether the shutdown configuration exists on the interface. If the shutdown configuration exists on the interface, go to Step 2. If the shutdown configuration does not exist on the interface, go to Step 3. 2. Run the undo shutdown command in the master's remote interface view to check whether the trap VIRTUAL-ACCESS_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.343.2.4.2 hwVirtualAccessExterLinkDownClear is generated. If the trap VIRTUAL-ACCESS_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.343.2.4.2 hwVirtualAccessExterLinkDownClear is generated, go to Step 8. If the trap VIRTUAL-ACCESS_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.343.2.4.2 hwVirtualAccessExterLinkDownClear is not generated, go to Step 3. 3. If the master's remote interface has a sub-interface, check whether a VLAN is configured on the sub-interface. If a VLAN is configured on the sub-interface, go to Step 5. If a VLAN is not configured on the sub-interface, go to Step 4. 4. Configure a VLAN on the sub-interface, and check whether the trap VIRTUAL-ACCESS_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.343.2.4.2 hwVirtualAccessExterLinkDownClear is generated. If the trap VIRTUAL-ACCESS_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.343.2.4.2 hwVirtualAccessExterLinkDownClear is generated, go to Step 8. If the trap VIRTUAL-ACCESS_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.343.2.4.2 hwVirtualAccessExterLinkDownClear is not generated, go to Step 5. 5. Check whether the external communication interface's physical link on the AP is properly connected (for example, check whether the network cable and optical module are properly connected). If the external communication interface's physical link on the AP is properly connected, go to Step 7. If the external communication interface's physical link on the AP is not properly connected, go to Step 6. 6. Rectify the fault on the external communication interface's physical link, and check whether the trap VIRTUAL-ACCESS_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.343.2.4.2 hwVirtualAccessExterLinkDownClear is generated. If the trap VIRTUAL-ACCESS_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.343.2.4.2 hwVirtualAccessExterLinkDownClear is generated, go to Step 8. If the trap VIRTUAL-ACCESS_1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.5.25.343.2.4.2 hwVirtualAccessExterLinkDownClear is not generated, go to Step 7. 7. Collect alarm information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 8. End. Cause 2: The interface is deleted 1. This is a user operation, and no action is required.
parameters: ApAdminIp::Management IP address of the AP on which the external communication interface went Down | IfName::Name of the external communication interface | IfIndex::Index of the external communication interface | IfAdminStatus::Management status of the external communication interface: Up Down | IfOperStatus::Operating status of the external communication interface: Up Down | Reason::Reason of the external communication interface failure: 1: The physical link went Down. 2: The interface was deleted.

procedure: Cause 1: Apply for a trusted certificate again. This message is informational only, and no action is required. Cause 2: The trusted certificate has expired. Perform the following steps to apply for a trusted certificate again: 1. Check the trusted certificate type. If the LAK certificate is used, go to step 2. If the certificate is an IAK certificate, go to step 3. 2. Replace the certificate with a valid trusted certificate. You can try to update the certificate using remote-attestation pki update-request {all | {slot <slotID>}}. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect log and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End.

description: The IPv6 DHCPv6-PD prefix usage of the domain [domainName] fell below the lower threshold. (Domain index = [domainIndex],MinThreshold=[threshold]) The IPv6 DHCPv6-PD prefix usage reached the lower threshold in the domain. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: If the fault persists, more users may be logged out unexpectedly.
possible_causes: Cause 1: A large number of users logged out. Cause 2: The configured lower limit was too high.
procedure: 1. Run the display domain domain-name command in the system view to check the value of IPv6-warning-threshold(Low) and determine whether the configured lower threshold for the IPv6 DHCPv6-PD prefix usage is proper. If the configured lower threshold is too large, go to Step 2. If the configured lower threshold is proper, go to Step 3. 2. Run the ipv6-warning-threshold lower-limit command in the AAA domain view to change the lower threshold for the IPv6 DHCPv6-PD prefix usage. 3. Run the display domain domain-name command in the system view to check the current IPv6 address usage. If the IPv6 DHCPv6-PD prefix usage falls below or approaches the lower threshold, run the display aaa offline-record brief command to check whether the user offline reason is User request to offline. a. If yes, it is normal. b. If not, contact technical support engineers. If the IPv6 DHCPv6-PD prefix usage is not close to the configured lower threshold, go to Step 4.
parameters: domainName::Domain name. | domainIndex::Domain index. | threshold::Alarm threshold, in percentage. For example, the value 80 indicates 80%.

description: The configured NetStream sampling ratio was different from the effective one. (Slot=[Slot-Id], Fix-packets-lower-limit=[Fix-packets-lower-limit], Random-packets-lower-limit=[Random-packets-lower-limit], Fix-time-lower-limit=[Fix-time-lower-limit]) The configured sampling ratio was different from the actual sampling ratio. impact_on_system: The configured NetStream sampling ratio is different from the actual sampling ratio.
possible_causes: The configured sampling ratio or mode was not supported by the board.
procedure: 1. Check the sampling ratio configuration of the board generating the alarm. If fixed-packet-number-based sampling or random-packet-number-based sampling is used, go to Step 2. If fixed-interval sampling is used, go to Step 3. 2. Change the fixed-packet-number-based sampling or random-packet-number-based sampling ratio from a value less than 10000 to a value greater than 10000. Then, check whether the alarm persists. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 5. 3. Change fixed-interval sampling to fixed-packet sampling or random-packet sampling, and set the sampling ratio to a value greater than 10000. Then, check whether the alarm persists.
parameters: Slot-Id::Slot ID. | Fix-packets-lower-limit::Lower limit of the fixed-packet-number-based sampling ratio. | Random-packets-lower-limit::Lower limit of the random-packet-number-based sampling ratio. | Fix-time-lower-limit::Lower limit of the fixed-interval sampling ratio.

description: PW APS does not support the current public tunnel. (VcID=[VcID], VcType=[VcType], PeerAddr=[PeerAddr]) PW APS did not support the current public network tunnel.
impact_on_system: PW APS fails.
possible_causes: The PW bound to the APS instance was carried over a non-TE tunnel.
procedure: 1. Check the public network tunnel type of the PW. In a VLL scenario, run the display mpls l2vc command to check the public network tunnel type of the VLL. In a VSI scenario, run the display vsi name command to check the public network tunnel type of the VSI. If the tunnel is a TE tunnel, go to Step 3. If the tunnel is not a TE tunnel, go to Step 2. 2. Configure the TE tunnel as the public network tunnel, and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: VcID::ID of a VC. | VcType::VC type. 1: FR 2: ATM_AAL5 3: ATM_CELL_TRANSPORT 4: VLAN 5: ETHERNET 6: HDLC 7: PPP 8: CEM 9: ATM_CELL_VCC 10: ATM_CELL_VPC 11: IP_LAYER2_TRANSPORT 12: ATM_ONE_TO_ONE_VCC_CELL_MODE 13: ATM_ONE_TO_ONE_VPC_CELL_MODE 14: ATM_AAL5_PDU_VCC_TRANSPORT 15: FR_PORT 16: CEP 17: SAT_E1_OVER_PACKET 18: SAT_T1_OVER_PACKET 19: SAT_E3_OVER_PACKET 20: SAT_T3_OVER_PACKET 21: CESOPSN_BASIC_MODE 22: TDMOIP_AAL1 23: CESOPSN_TDM 24: TDMOIP_AAL2 25: FR_DLCI 26: INTERWORKING 27: VPLS 64: IP_INTERWORKING | PeerAddr::Peer address.

description: Loss of code group synchronization alarm. (hwPhysicalPortIfIndex=[hwPhysicalPortIfIndex],SlotID=[hwPhysicalPortInSlot],CardID=[hwPhysicalPortInCard],PortID=[hwPhysicalPortInPort],InterfaceName=[hwPhysicalPortName]) Loss of code group synchronization alarm. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The interface will fail to receive services.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The SDH path connected to the interface failed to receive packets properly. For example, an hwLosAlarm, hwLofAlarm, hwLaisAlarm, hwAuLopAlarm, hwAuAisAlarm alarm was generated. Cause 2: The SDH path received a large amount of error codes and a hwB1TcaAlarm, hwB2TcaAlarm or hwB3TcaAlarm alarm was generated. Cause 3: The physical-layer processing chip on a subcard failed to function properly
procedure: 1. Check and clear an hwLosAlarm, hwLofAlarm, hwLaisAlarm, hwAuLopAlarm, hwAuAisAlarm alarm generated for the SDH path connecting the upstream device and the interface. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step 2. 2. Check and clear a hwB1TcaAlarm, hwB2TcaAlarm or hwB3TcaAlarm alarm for the local device. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm is not cleared, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm information, log information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel.
parameters: hwPhysicalPortIfIndex::Index of physical port. | hwPhysicalPortInSlot::Slot ID. | hwPhysicalPortInCard::Card ID. | hwPhysicalPortInPort::Port ID. | hwPhysicalPortName::Name of physical port.

description: RBS heartbeat signals were abnormal.(RBS = [hwBrasRbsName]) The RBS heartbeat signal was abnormal. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The dual-device hot backup function is affected.
possible_causes: RBS heartbeat signals were abnormal.
parameters: hwBrasRbsName::Backup service name.

description: The number of IPv6 addresses in the IPv6 pool fell below 90% of the threshold. (IPv6PoolIndex=[IPv6PoolIndex],IPv6PoolName=[IPv6PoolName]) In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: There is no impact.
possible_causes: Users logged off and the IPv6 address pool usage fell below 90% of the threshold.
parameters: IPv6PoolIndex::Index of an address pool. | IPv6PoolName::Name of an address pool.

description: The disaster recovery roles of two CPs conflict. (hwSourceIpAddress=[hwSourceIpAddress],hwPeerIpAddress=[hwPeerIpAddress]) The role configurations of two CPs conflicted, and an alarm was generated on the UP. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The geographic redundancy function was unavailable.
possible_causes: The roles configured for the two CPs conflicted and they had the same priority.
procedure: 1. Check whether the active/standby status configured for the disaster recovery groups on the two CPs conflicts. If yes, run the set preferred-role { master | slave } command in the disaster recovery group view to configure different active/standby roles for the two CPs. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 3. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End.
parameters: hwSourceIpAddress::IP address of the peer controller of the CUSP channel on CP1. | hwPeerIpAddress::IP address of the peer controller of the CUSP channel on CP2.

description: The chassis was inserted. (EntityPhysicalIndex=[EntityPhysicalIndex],EntPhysicalIndex=[EntPhysicalIndex],EntPhysicalName=[EntPhysicalName],EntityTrapFaultID=131073) In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Services are not affected.
possible_causes: The chassis was inserted.
parameters: EntityPhysicalIndex::Indicates the entity index. | EntPhysicalIndex::Indicates the entity index. | EntPhysicalName::Indicates the entity name. | EntityTrapFaultID::Indicates the error code.

description: The rate and PLL of the ports in the group do not match. (IfIndex=[IfIndex],SlotId=[SlotId],CardId=[CardId],PortId=[PortId],ReasonDescription=[ReasonDescription]) The interfaces of the same group worked in the wrong transmission mode. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Traffic forwarding on the physical interfaces will be affected. Thus, a speedy solution is required.
possible_causes: The rate and PLL of the ports in the group do not match.
procedure: 1. Run the set transfer-mode command to configure all the ports in the group to work in LAN transmission mode. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End.
parameters: IfIndex::Index of physical port. | SlotId::Slot ID. | CardId::Card ID. | PortId::Port ID. | ReasonDescription::Reason Description.

description: The log host status is available. (InstanceType=[InstanceType], InstanceName=[InstanceName], Protocol=[Protocol], HostIP=[HostIP], HostPort=[HostPort], HostVpn=[HostVpn]) In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The log server is available and can correctly save NAT flow logs.
possible_causes: The log host status is available.
parameters: InstanceType::Instance type | InstanceName::Instance name | Protocol::Detection protocol type | HostIP::IP address of the log server | HostPort::Port number of the log server | HostVpn::VPN instance name of the log server

description: The board hardware is faulty, and the active/standby role is abnormal. (Physical index=[PhysicalIndex], Entity name=[PhysicalName]) The board hardware is faulty, and the active/standby role is abnormal. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Services are affected.
possible_causes: 1. The board hardware is faulty. 2. The board is not securely inserted or in poor contact.
procedure: 1. Restart the board whose hardware active/standby role is abnormal. You can view the ID of the board to be restarted in the alarm description. After the board is started, wait for 60s and check whether the alarm is generated again. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 6. 2. Restart the device. After the device is started, wait for 60s and check whether the alarm is generated again. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 6. 3. Replace the board whose hardware active/standby role is abnormal and check whether the alarm is generated again.
parameters: PhysicalIndex::Physical index. | PhysicalName::Entity name.

description: The number of ports assigned to CPEs reaches the upper limit. (Protocol=[Protocol], CPEIP=[CPEIP], InstanceType=[InstanceType], InstanceName=[InstanceName], AddrGroupName=[AddrGroupName], Threshold=[Threshold], Ports=[Ports], Slot=[Slot], Cpu=[Cpu], UserID=[UserID]) For an instance configured with a port range, the usage of ports allocated by the CGN device to users in the instance reached the threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: When the alarm is generated, services are not affected. If the number of new sessions reaches the maximum number of ports available for the user, the user fails to create a session. In an instance, only the alarm information about the first user (not all users) whose port usage exceeds the threshold is reported. When multiple CPUs are used for load balancing in an instance, each CPU reports only the alarm for the first user whose traffic exceeds the threshold.
possible_causes: The proportion of CGN interfaces assigned to users to the total supported ones reached a specified threshold.
procedure: 1. Run the display this command in the view of the instance for which the alarm is generated to check whether the alarm threshold is far less than 80%. If the alarm threshold is far less than 80%, go to Step 2. If the alarm threshold is not far less than 80%, go to Step 3. 2. Run the nat alarm user port-number threshold command in the NAT instance view to set a higher alarm threshold for the user port usage. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: Protocol::Protocol type. The value is TOTAL. | CPEIP::IP address of the CPE. | InstanceType::Instance type. | InstanceName::Instance name. | AddrGroupName::Name of an address pool. | Threshold::Threshold for the usage of ports allocated by the CGN device to users. | Ports::Number of used ports. | Slot::Slot ID of a service board. | Cpu::CPU ID of a service board. | UserID::User ID.

description: A VXLAN tunnel between the CP and UP Service went Down. (SrcAddr=[SrcAddr],PeerAddr=[PeerAddr],VniId=[VniId],Vpn=[Vpn], DownReason=[DownReason]) Services carried on a VXLAN tunnel between the UP and CP went down. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The CP cannot communicate with the UP.
possible_causes: A VXLAN tunnel between the CP and UP was down in the CU separation scenario.
procedure: 1. Check the failure cause displayed in the alarm information. If the alarm cause is VXLAN link down, go to Step 4. If the alarm cause is NQA down, check whether the NQA configurations on the vBRAS-UP and vBRAS-CP are consistent. If the configurations are inconsistent, go to Step 2. If the configurations are the same, go to Step 4. 2. Modify the NQA configurations on the vBRAS-CP and vBRAS-UP and ensure that the protocol-tunnel track nqa command is run on both the vBRAS-CP and vBRAS-UP, and the UDP port numbers specified in the command must be the same. 3. Check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 5. If the alarm persists, go to Step 4.
parameters: SrcAddr::UP-side IP address of a VXLAN tunnel in CU separation scenarios. | PeerAddr::CP-side IP address of a VXLAN tunnel in CU separation scenarios. | VniId::Network identifier of a VXLAN. | Vpn::VPN instance on the UP side of a VXLAN tunnel in a CU separation scenario. | DownReason::Reason why a VXLAN tunnel goes down in a CU separation scenario.

description: The data redundancy elimination service took effect because the local fault was rectified. (InstanceName=[InstanceName],MinimumCPU=[MinimumCPU],WorkCPU=[WorkCPU],ConfigCPU=[ConfigCPU]) In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: There is no impact on the system.
possible_causes: The data processing service took effect because the local fault was rectified.

description: The public network tunnel of EVPN cannot forward traffic. (EvpnName=[hwNotSupportTunnelEvpnName], RemoteIp=[hwEVPNPeerRemoteIp], TunnelType=[hwNotSupportTunnelType]) The public network tunnel configured for EVPN does not support traffic forwarding. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: EVPN traffic fails to be forwarded.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The EVPN is carried over a BGP over GRE tunnel, and the signaling protocol status of the EVPN is up. Cause 2: The EVPN is carried over a BGP over LDP over GRE tunnel, and the signaling protocol status of the EVPN is up. Cause 3: The EVPN is carried over a LDP over GRE tunnel, and the signaling protocol status of the EVPN is up.
procedure: 1. Change the EVPN tunnel type. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 3. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End.
parameters: hwNotSupportTunnelEvpnName::EVPN name. | hwEVPNPeerRemoteIp::Remote IP address. | hwNotSupportTunnelType::Tunnel type.

description: The number of users with uplink traffic but no downlink traffic falls below 80 percent of the threshold or the alarm function is disabled. (UnidirectionalUserNumber=[unidirectionalUserNumber], Threshold=[threshold]) In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: There is no impact on the system.
possible_causes: The number of users with uplink traffic but no downlink traffic falls below 80 percent of the threshold or the alarm function is disabled.
parameters: unidirectionalUserNumber::Number of users with uplink traffic but no downlink traffic | threshold::An alarm is generated when the number of users who have uplink traffic but no downlink traffic reached the threshold.

description: The link between pcef and pcrf is abnormal. (DiameterPeerHostName=[hwDiameterPeerHostName],DiameterPeerIP=[hwDiameterPeerIP],DiameterPeerPort=[hwDiameterPeerPort],DiameterLocalIf=[hwDiameterLocalIf],DiameterGrpLinkLocalPort=[hwDiameterGrpLinkLocalPort]) This alarm was generated when the link between the host and the server was faulty because the policy server was down or the peer IP address or port number was changed. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: After the link is disconnected, the user selects another up link in the server group. If no up link is available, the user cannot deliver services through the policy server.
possible_causes: Cause 1: A policy server became faulty. Cause 2: The local IP address or port of the link was changed. Cause 3: The peer IP address or port of the link was changed.
procedure: 1. Run the display diameter configuration command to view the Diameter link status. If the link status is up, the link is normal and no fault alarm should be generated. Go to Step 4. If the link status is down, the link is abnormal. Go to Step 2. If the link status is error, the link configuration is incorrect. Go to Step 4. 2. Run the display diameter configuration command to check the local and peer configurations of the corresponding link, including the local interface IP address (Local interface IP), local port number (Client port), peer IPv4 address (Peer IPv4 addr), and peer port number (Peer port). Log in to the portal page of the policy server to check whether the local and peer configurations of the link are the same. If they are the same, go to Step 4. If they are different, go to Step 3. 3. Run the diameter-local and diameter-peer commands in the system view to change the inconsistency between local and peer IP address and port number. Then run the display diameter configuration command again to check the link status.
parameters: hwDiameterPeerHostName::Name of the peer host. | hwDiameterPeerIP::IP address of the peer host. | hwDiameterPeerPort::Peer host port. | hwDiameterLocalIf::Name of the local port. | hwDiameterGrpLinkLocalPort::Source port ID

description: Voltage exceeded the lower prealarm limit. (BaseTrapSeverity=[BaseTrapSeverity],BaseTrapProbableCause=73217,BaseTrapEventType=[BaseTrapEventType],EntityPhysicalIndex=[EntityPhysicalIndex],EntPhysicalName=[EntPhysicalName],BaseThresholdValue=[BaseThresholdValue],BaseThresholdUnit=[BaseThresholdUnit],LowCritical=[BaseThresholdLowCritical],LowWarning=[BaseThresholdLowWarning]) The voltage of a physical entity exceeded the lower critical threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Temporarily, services will not be interrupted but clearing this trap is urgent.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The PDF power supply was insufficient. Cause 2: The power supply module was faulty.
procedure: 1.Run the display voltage slot <slot-id> command in the user view to view the voltage of each board. 2.Check whether the PDF power supply is sufficient. If so, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 3. 3.Increase the PDF power supply and check whether the trap is cleared. If so, go to Step 6. If not, go to step 4.
parameters: BaseTrapSeverity::Indicates the level of trap. | BaseTrapProbableCause::Indicates the possible cause of trap. | BaseTrapEventType::Indicates the type of trap. | EntityPhysicalIndex::Indicates the physical index. | EntPhysicalName::Indicates the textual name of the physical entity. | BaseThresholdValue::Indicates the actual value. | BaseThresholdUnit::Indicates the unit. The value 5 indicates millivolt (mV). | BaseThresholdLowCritical::Indicates the upper critical limit. | BaseThresholdLowWarning::Indicates the minor upper limit.

description: The alarm is cleared, because the IPv6 GRE configuration has been deleted from the board or the board has been replaced with one that supports IPv6 GRE. (Slot=[slotID]) In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Services are not affected.
possible_causes: The IPv6 GRE configuration has been deleted from the board or the board has been replaced with one that supports IPv6 GRE.
parameters: slotID::Slot ID

description: The IP address usage of the domain [domainName] fell below the lower threshold. (Domain index = [domainIndex],MinThreshold=[threshold]) The IP address usage in the domain fell below the lower threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: If the fault persists, more users may be logged out unexpectedly.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Some users logged out. Cause 2: The configured lower limit was too high.
procedure: 1. Run the display domain domain-name command in the system view to check the value of IP-warning-threshold(Low) and determine whether the configured lower threshold for the IP address usage is proper. If the configured minimum threshold is too large, go to Step 2. If the configured minimum threshold is proper, go to step 3. 2. Run the ip-warning-threshold lower-limit command in the AAA domain view to change the lower threshold for the IP address usage. 3. Run the display domain domain-name command in the system view to check the current IP address usage. If the IP address usage falls below or approaches the lower threshold, run the display aaa offline-record brief command to check whether the offline reason is User request to offline. a. If yes, it is normal. b. If no, contact technical support engineers. If the IP address usage is not close to the lower threshold, go to Step 4.
parameters: domainName::Domain name. | domainIndex::Domain index. | threshold::Alarm threshold, in percentage. For example, the value 80 indicates 80%.

description: Using IPsec hot standby function without enable DPD detection. DPD is not configured for IPsec dual-device hot backup. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Packet loss may occur during the switchover of the VRRP group bound to IPsec dual-device hot backup.
possible_causes: DPD has not been enabled for IPsec dual-system hot backup.
procedure: 1. Run the ike dpd [ interval | on-demand ] <check-interval> [ <retry-interval> ] command to configure DPD. 2. Delete the IPsec dual-device hot backup function.

description: The IPv6 DHCPv6-PD prefix usage of the domain [domainName] reached the upper threshold. (Domain index = [domainIndex],Threshold=[threshold]) The IPv6 DHCPv6-PD prefix usage in the domain reached the upper threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: If the problem persists, DHCPv6-PD prefixes in the address pools bound to the domain may be exhausted. As a result, new users cannot go online because they cannot be assigned DHCPv6-PD prefixes.
possible_causes: A large number of users got online from the domain, causing the number of IPv6 prefixes allocated using DHCPv6-PD to reach the threshold.
procedure: 1. Run the display domain domain-name command to check the IPv6 address usage alarm threshold (IPv6-warning-threshold) configured in the domain. If the value of IPv6-warning-threshold ranges from 1 to 100, go to Step 2. If IPv6-warning-threshold is not configured or is set to 100 in the domain, go to Step 4. 2. Run the display ipv6-pool pool-usage command to check whether the number of online users with IPv6 prefixes assigned in DHCPv6-PD mode in the domain has reached the maximum value. If yes, go to Step 5. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Run the ipv6-pool command in the domain view to reference a delegation address pool or run the access-type command in the BAS interface view to configure new users to go online from another domain. Wait for 30 minutes and check whether the alarm persists.
parameters: domainName::Domain name. | domainIndex::Domain index. | threshold::IPv6 address threshold in a domain, in percentage. For example, the value 80 indicates 80%.

description: The alarm indicating that the fan module was unavailable was cleared. (EntityPhysicalIndex=[EntityPhysicalIndex],EntPhysicalName=[EntPhysicalName],EntityTrapFaultID=[EntityTrapFaultID],Reason=[Reason]) In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Services are not affected.
possible_causes: The fan module recovered.
parameters: EntityPhysicalIndex::The index for this entry. | EntPhysicalName::The textual name of the physical entity. | EntityTrapFaultID::To describe the fault id of trap. | Reason::Reason.

description: The number of IPv6 addresses in the IPv6 pool reached the threshold. (IPv6PoolIndex=[IPv6PoolIndex],IPv6PoolName=[IPv6PoolName]) The IPv6 address usage exceeded the threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Services are not affected. However, if the number of IPv6 addresses continues to increase, IPv6 addresses will be exhausted and IPv6 users cannot be assigned addresses from the address pool.
possible_causes: The user number has passed the threshold.
procedure: 1. Check the address usage of the address pool bound to the domain and evaluate whether there are sufficient addresses. If the addresses are sufficient, you are advised to manually clear the alarm. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Bind a new IPv6 address pool to the domain. 3. Check whether the problem persists. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 5.
parameters: IPv6PoolIndex::Index of an address pool. | IPv6PoolName::Name of an address pool.

description: User services on the RUI backup device failed to be recovered for a long period of time. User services on the backup device in RUI scenarios failed to be restored for a long time. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The dual-device hot backup function is affected.
possible_causes: User services on the RUI backup device failed to be recovered for a long period of time.
procedure: 1. Check whether the board, subcard, interface, or CGN board from which users go online is faulty. Run the display device/display device pic-status/ display interface <interface-name> command to check the status of the board, subcard, or interface. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. After the fault is rectified, wait for 90 minutes and check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Collect trap, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.

description: The IPv6 addresses in the IPv6 pool is exhausted. (IPv6PoolIndex=[IPv6PoolIndex],IPv6PoolName=[IPv6PoolName]) Addresses in the IPv6 address pool were exhausted, and no IPv6 address was available for assignment. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Subsequent users cannot obtain IP addresses from this address pool.
possible_causes: Addresses in the IPv6 address pool were exhausted and became unavailable.
procedure: 1. Check the usage of the address pool bound to the domain and evaluate whether there are sufficient addresses. If addresses are sufficient, you are advised to manually clear the alarm. If addresses are insufficient, go to Step 2. 2. Bind a new IPv6 address pool to the domain. 3. Check whether the problem persists. If yes, go to Step 4. If no, go to Step 5.
parameters: IPv6PoolIndex::Address pool index | IPv6PoolName::Address pool name

(hwIfMonitorIndex=[hwIfMonitorIndex],hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorStatistics=[hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorStatistics],hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorThreshold=[hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorThreshold],hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorInterval=[hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorInterval],hwIfMonitorName=[hwIfMonitorName]) In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Services are restored to normal.
possible_causes: The number of bytes of received error packets was 0 within a specified period.

description: The trustem certificate will expire. (PhysicalIndex=[PhysicalIndex], PhysicalName=[PhysicalName], CertificateName=[hwTrustemCertificateName], CertificateType=[hwTrustemCertificateType], BeginTime=[hwTrustemCertificateBeginTime], EndTime=[hwTrustemCertificateEndTime]) This alarm is generated 30 days before the trusted certificate expires. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: After the trusted digital certificate expires, users cannot pass trusted security authentication.
possible_causes: The trusted certificate is about to expire
procedure: 1. Check the trusted certificate type. If the LAK certificate is used, go to step 2. If the certificate is an IAK certificate, go to step 3. 2. Replace the certificate with a valid trusted certificate. You can try to update the certificate using remote-attestation pki update-request {all | {slot <slotID>}}. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect log and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: PhysicalIndex::Physical index | PhysicalName::Name of an entity | hwTrustemCertificateName::The name of the Certificate File | hwTrustemCertificateType::The type of the Certificate File | hwTrustemCertificateBeginTime::The begin time of the Certificate File | hwTrustemCertificateEndTime::The end time of the Certificate File

description: The total number of global multicast groups exceeded the upper threshold. impact_on_system: The total number of global multicast groups has reached the threshold. If new global multicast groups are added, the number may exceed the upper limit.

description: CUSP connection is down. (IP Type=[CuspIpType], Local IP=[CuspLocalIp], Remote IP=[CuspRemoteIp], VrfName=[VrfName], DatapathId=[DatapathId], AuxiliaryId=[AuxiliaryId], SubReason=[SubReason], Reason=[Reason]) The CUSP connection was interrupted. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The CUSP connection was interrupted. As a result, the session service that depends on the CUSP connection was abnormal.
possible_causes: Cause 1: A TCP connection became abnormal. Cause 2: CUSP heartbeat packets timed out. Cause 3: A forwarder received invalid packets sent by the controller of a CUSP session or incorrectly processed received packets.
procedure: Cause 1: A TCP connection became abnormal. 1. Check whether the CUSP controller configuration is changed and whether the CUSP configuration is deleted or modified. If yes, correct the CUSP configuration. If no, go to Step 2. 2. Run the ping command on both ends of the CUSP session to check whether the network connection is normal. If yes, go to Step 3. If no, rectify the network connection fault. After the connectivity fault is rectified, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display cusp session command to check the CUSP session status. If the CUSP session status is not REGISTERED, go to Step 4. If the CUSP session is in the REGISTERED state, go to Step 5. 4. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 2: CUSP heartbeat packets timed out. 1. Run the ping command on both ends of the CUSP session to check whether the network connection is normal. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, rectify the network connection fault. After the connectivity fault is rectified, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display cusp session command to check the CUSP session status. If the CUSP session status is not REGISTERED, go to Step 3. If the CUSP session status is REGISTERED, go to Step 4. 3. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 3: A forwarder received invalid packets sent by the controller of a CUSP session or incorrectly processed received packets. Collect alarm and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: CuspIpType::IP address type. | CuspLocalIp::IP address of a CUSP forwarder. | CuspRemoteIp::IP address of the CUSP controller. | VrfName::Index of the VRF to which the CUSP belongs. | DatapathId::Unique ID of a CUSP forwarder. | AuxiliaryId::Auxiliary connection ID. | SubReason::Detailed cause of the CUSP connection interruption. | Reason::Reason why the CUSP session went Down.

description: The packets are discarded because they do not match the PW source tunnel. (PwLabel=[hwPwLabel], TeLabel=[hwTeLabel], PortName=[hwPortName]) The packet was discarded because the PW source tunnel did not match. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Packets are discarded and fail to be forwarded.
possible_causes: The tunnel and PW labels carried in received packets did not match those on the local end.
procedure: 1. Check whether the public network label and private network label configured on the local device are correct. If the configuration is correct, go to Step 2. If the configuration is incorrect, reconfigure the public and private network labels on the local end to ensure that the public and private network labels on the local end match correctly. Then, go to Step 2. 2. Check whether the public network label and private network label configured on the peer device are correct. If the configuration is incorrect, go to Step 3. If the configurations are correct, go to Step 4. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: hwPwLabel::PW label. | hwTeLabel::TE label. | hwPortName::Interface name.

description: Security Application-apperceive drop packets alarmed. (ChassisID=[ChassisID], SlotID=[SlotID], Protocol=[Protocol], CurrentRateLow=[CurrentRateLow], CurrentRateHigh=[CurrentRateHigh], NotifyEnabled=[NotifyEnabled], RateThreshold=[RateThreshold], RateInterval=[RateInterval], ProtocolDescription=[ProtocolDescription], Reason=[Reason]) The number of discarded packets on an interface board exceeded the configured alarm threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The bandwidth for sending normal protocol packets to the CPU may be preempted. As a result, protocols are interrupted and data is lost.
possible_causes: Application related traffic's discarded rate exceeded alarm threshold.
procedure: 1. Run the display cpu-defend statistics command to check the CIR and CBS of the interface board and the values of Actual CIR in NP and Actual CBS in NP. The unit of Actual CIR in NP is kbit/s, and the unit of Actual CBS in NP is bytes. If the CAR value is too small to meet service requirements, run the car command to increase the rate and wait for 60 seconds. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. If the set CAR value meets service requirements but the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display cpu-defend policy <policy-number> command to check the alarm configuration of Application apperceive Configuration and determine whether the alarm threshold and alarm interval are set properly. If the alarm threshold is too low, run the alarm drop-rate command to increase the threshold based on service traffic. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. If the alarm interval is too small, run the alarm drop-rate command to increase the interval. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Run the display attack-source-trace slot <slot-id> original-information command and check the Attack Source Data field to check the packet header information cached by the attack source tracing module.
parameters: ChassisID::Chassis ID. | SlotID::Slot ID. | Protocol::Protocol number of discarded packets. The protocol numbers are as follows: ftpServer(1) sshServer(2) snmp(3) telnetServer(4) tftp(5) bgp(6) ldp(7) rsvp(8) ospf(9) rip(10) isis(11) sftpSever(12) icmp(13) msdp(14) pim(15) ipv4Arp(16) bpdu(17) dhcp(18) lacp(19) ntp(20) radius(21) hwTacacs(22) lspPing(23) igmp(24) rrpp(26) vrrp(27) bfd(28) mplsOam(29) eth8021ag(30) ftpClient(31) telnetClient(32) sshClient(33) sftpClient(34) dnsClient(35) telnetv6Server(64) telnetv6Client(65) icmpv6(67) pimv6(69) sshv6Server(70) ospfv3(71) bgpv6(72) ftpv6Client(73) ftpv6Server(74) | CurrentRateLow::Indicates the least significant 32 bits of traffic statistics. | CurrentRateHigh::Indicates the most significant 32 bits of traffic statistics. | NotifyEnabled::Whether the trap function is enabled: 1: enabled 2: disabled | RateThreshold::Current alarm threshold. | RateInterval::Current alarm interval. | ProtocolDescription::Protocol description. | Reason::Alarm cause.

description: The bandwidth usage of the slot exceeds the threshold. Run the display nat bandwidth and display nat statistics payload commands in any view to check whether the current traffic volume and historical maximum traffic volume on the CGN board exceed the maximum forwarding bandwidth. If the current or historical maximum bandwidth is close to the maximum bandwidth configured in the CGN board bandwidth license, go to Step 2. If the current or historical maximum bandwidth is not close to the maximum bandwidth configured in the CGN board bandwidth license, go to Step 3. 2. Upgrade the bandwidth license or expand the board capacity. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.

description: The number of cached packets reached the upper limit. (MaxCachePackets=[hwRadiusMaxCachePackets],Threshold=[hwRadiusThreshold]) The number of cached packets reached the upper threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: There is no impact on the system. If the number of cached packets reaches the maximum number of packets that can be cached, all packets of the earliest user in the cache queue are released, and subsequent accounting packets are cached.
possible_causes: The ratio of the number of cached packets to the maximum number of packets that can be cached reached the configured upper limit.
procedure: 1. Check whether the alarm threshold (value of Threshold in the alarm information) is proper. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, run the radius-server accounting cache-warning-threshold upper-limit < upper-limit > lower-limit < lower-limit > command to increase the upper threshold for the number of cached packets. 2. Run the test-aaa command to check whether the link to the RADIUS server is normal. If the interval between packet sending and response packet sending is longer than 30s, the link to the RADIUS server is busy. If no response is received, the link to the RADIUS server is unreachable. If yes, go to Step 3. If no, rectify the link fault. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: hwRadiusMaxCachePackets::Maximum number of accounting packets that can be cached | hwRadiusThreshold::Upper threshold for the number of cached packets

description:

description: Security URPF drop packets alarmed. (ChassisID=[ChassisID], SlotID=[SlotID], CurrentRateLow=[CurrentRateLow], CurrentRateHigh=[CurrentRateHigh], NotifyEnabled=[NotifyEnabled], RateThreshold=[RateThreshold], RateInterval=[RateInterval]) This alarm was generated when URPF packets were discarded. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The bandwidth for sending normal protocol packets to the CPU is preempted, which may cause protocol interruption.
possible_causes: The number of discarded URPF protocol packets exceeded the alarm threshold.
procedure: 1. Run the display cpu-defend tcpip-defend statistics slot <slot-id> command to check the committed access rate (CIR) and committed burst rate (CBS) of the interface board. Check the values of Actual CIR in NP and Actual CBS in NP. If the protocol rate is too small to meet service requirements, run the car command to increase the rate and wait for 60 seconds. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. If the configured protocol rate meets service running requirements but the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Run the display cpu-defend policy <policy-number> command to check whether the alarm threshold and alarm interval of the protocol are set properly based on Application apperceive Configuration. If the alarm threshold is too low, run the alarm drop-rate command to increase the threshold based on service traffic. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. If the alarm interval is too small, run the alarm drop-rate command to increase the alarm interval. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. description: Failed to enable the Diameter service. (ReasonCode=[hwDiameterReasonCode],Reason=[hwDiameterReason]) The Diameter service failed to be enabled. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: After this alarm is generated, the Diameter server cannot be used to manage users on the device.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The diamgxdict directory failed to be created when the Diameter service was enabled. Cause 2: The total size of files in the dictionary package was greater than 256 KB when the Diameter service was enabled. Cause 3: The dictionary package failed to be decompressed when the Diameter service was enabled. Cause 4: Files in the dictionary package were incomplete when the Diameter service was enabled. Cause 5: The dictionary package signature failed to be verified when the Diameter service was enabled. Cause 6: The dictionary file failed to be read when the Diameter service was enabled. Cause 7: The protocol stack failed to be initialized when the Diameter service was enabled.
procedure: Cause 1: The diamgxdict directory failed to be created when the Diameter service was enabled. 1. Manually create the diamgxdict directory in the home directory. If the creation fails, go to Step 2. If the creation succeeds, go to step 3. 2. Run the dir command to check whether the CF card has free space. If there is no free space, clear the space and go to Step 3. If there is still free space, go to Step 4. 3. Run the undo diameter enable command and then the diameter enable command. If the alarm persists, go to Step 4. 4. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 5. End. Cause 2: The total size of files in the dictionary package was greater than 256 KB when the Diameter service was enabled. 1. Reduce the total size of files in the dictionary package to less than 256 KB. After the reduction is successful, go to Step 2. 2. Run the undo diameter enable command and then the diameter enable command. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 3: The dictionary package failed to be decompressed when the Diameter service was enabled. 1. Use the decompression software to check whether the dictionary package can be decompressed properly. If the dictionary package cannot be decompressed, restore the dictionary package and go to Step 2. If the dictionary package can be decompressed, go to Step 3. 2. Run the undo diameter enable command and then the diameter enable command. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 4: Files in the dictionary package were incomplete when the Diameter service was enabled. 1. Check whether the dictionary package contains diamgxdict.xml, diamgxdict.xml.cms, and diamgxdict.xml.crl. If the file does not contain the three files, supplement the files and go to Step 2. If all the three files are contained, go to Step 3. 2. Run the undo diameter enable command and then the diameter enable command. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 5: The dictionary package signature failed to be verified when the Diameter service was enabled. 1. Check whether the dictionary package is consistent with the content provided by technical engineers and whether the dictionary package is tampered with. If the content has been tampered with, upload the correct dictionary package to CF card 1 and go to step 2. If the content is not tampered with, go to step 3. 2. Run the undo diameter enable command and then the diameter enable command. If the alarm persists, go to step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 6: The dictionary file failed to be read when the Diameter service was enabled. 1. Run the dir command to check whether the diamgxdict.xml file exists in the diamgxdict directory. If the diamgxdict.xml file does not exist, upload the correct dictionary package and go to Step 2. If the diamgxdict.xml file exists, go to Step 3. 2. Run the undo diameter enable command and then the diameter enable command. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End. Cause 7: The protocol stack failed to be initialized when the Diameter service was enabled. 1. Run the display health command to check whether the system memory usage and CPU usage are too high. If the CPU usage is too high, restore the system and go toStep 2. If the CPU usage is not too high, go to Step 3. 2. Run the undo diameter enable command and then the diameter enable command. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 4. End.
parameters: hwDiameterReasonCode::Cause code for the failure to enable the Diameter service. | hwDiameterReason::Reason why the Diameter service fails to be enabled.

description: The IPv6 address usage of the domain [domainName] fell below the lower threshold. (Domain index = [domainIndex],MinThreshold=[threshold]) The IPv6 address usage was above the lower threshold in the domain. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: If the fault persists, more users may be logged out unexpectedly.
possible_causes: Cause 1: A large number of users logged out. Cause 2: The configured lower limit was too high.
procedure: 1. Run the display domain domain-name command in the system view to check the value of IPv6-warning-threshold(Low) and determine whether the configured lower threshold for IPv6 addresses in the domain is proper. If the configured minimum threshold is too large, go to Step 2. If the configured minimum threshold is proper, go to Step 3. 2. Run the ipv6-warning-threshold lower-limit command in the AAA domain view to change the lower threshold for the IPv6 address usage. 3. Run the display domain domain-name command in the system view to check IPv6 addresses of the current domain. If the number of IPv6 addresses in the domain falls below or approaches the lower threshold, run the display aaa offline-record brief command to check whether the user offline reason is User request to offline. a. If yes, users go offline normally. b. If no, contact technical support engineers. If the number of IPv6 addresses in the domain is not close to the configured lower threshold, go to Step 4.
parameters: domainName::Domain name. | domainIndex::Domain index. | threshold::Alarm threshold, in percentage. For example, the value 80 indicates 80%.

description: The link between pcef and pcrf is abnormal. (DiameterPeerHostName=[hwDiameterPeerHostName],DiameterPeerIP=[hwDiameterPeerIpStr],DiameterPeerPort=[hwDiameterPeerPort],DiameterLocalIf=[hwDiameterLocalIf],DiameterGrpLinkLocalPort=[hwDiameterGrpLinkLocalPort]) This alarm was generated when the link between the host and the server was faulty because the policy server was down or the peer IP address or port number was changed. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: After the link is disconnected, the user selects another up link in the server group. If no up link is available, the user cannot deliver services through the policy server.
possible_causes: Cause 1: A policy server became faulty. Cause 2: The local IP address or port of the link was changed. Cause 3: The peer IP address or port of the link was changed.
procedure: 1. Run the display diameter configuration command to view the Diameter link status. If the link status is Up, the link is normal and no fault alarm should be generated. Go to Step 4. If the link status is Down, the link is abnormal. Go to Step 2. If the link status is Error, the link configuration is incorrect. Go to Step 4. 2. Run the display diameter configuration command to check the local and peer configurations of the corresponding link, including the local interface IP address (Local interface IP), local port number (Client port), peer IP address (Peer IP addr), and peer port number (Peer port). Log in to the portal page of the policy server to check whether the local and peer configurations of the link are the same. If they are the same, go to Step 4. If they are different, go to Step 3. 3. Run the diameter-local and diameter-peer commands in the system view to change the inconsistency between local and peer IP address and port number. Then run the display diameter configuration command again to check the link status.
parameters: hwDiameterPeerHostName::Name of the peer host. | hwDiameterPeerIpStr::IPv6 address of the peer host. | hwDiameterPeerPort::Peer host port. | hwDiameterLocalIf::Name of the local port. | hwDiameterGrpLinkLocalPort::Source port ID

description: The bytes of error packets reach the upper threshold. (hwIfMonitorIndex=[hwIfMonitorIndex],hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorStatistics=[hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorStatistics],hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorThreshold=[hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorThreshold],hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorInterval=[hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorInterval],hwIfMonitorName=[hwIfMonitorName]) The number of bytes of received error packets exceeded the alarm threshold within a specified period. If the alarm is not cleared, go to step 2. 2.Check the transmit optical power of the remote end in the NMS. If the transmit optical power of the remote end is abnormal, replace the LPU at the remote end, and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to End. If the alarm is not cleared, go to step 3. 3.Replace the LPU at the local end for which the alarm is generated, and check whether the alarm is cleared.
parameters: hwIfMonitorIndex::Index of physical port. | hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorStatistics::Statistics about bytes of error packets. | hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorThreshold::Maximum number of bytes of error packets. | hwIfMonitorBadBytesErrorInterval::Period within which the number of bytes of received error packets is counted. | hwIfMonitorName::Name of physical port.

description: The instance failed to apply for a subnet from the global address pool. (PoolName=[PoolName], Instance Type=[InstType], Instance Name=[InstName], Service-location=[SvclocId]) The instance failed to apply for a network segment from the global address pool. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: An instance cannot apply for new IP addresses from the global address pool. After the existing IP addresses in the instance are exhausted, user traffic fails to be forwarded or users cannot go online.
possible_causes: The number of available addresses in the global address pool was insufficient.
procedure: 1. Run the display nat ip-pool command to check the usage of the global address pool. If the usage reaches 100%, go to Step 2. If the usage does not reach 100%, go to Step 4. 2. If the global address pool is a static global address pool, run the section section-id start-ip mask mask-length command in the global address pool view to add a section. 3. If the global address pool is a dynamic global address pool, check whether the channel between the vBRAS-UP and vBRAS-CP is normal. If the channel is abnormal, restore the channel. If the channel is normal, check whether the number of networks of the DAP server on the CP is insufficient. If yes, add networks. 4. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: PoolName::Global address pool name | InstType::Instance type | InstName::Instance name | SvclocId::Backup group

possible_causes: The remaining validity period of the imported HTTPS redirection certificate is less than 90 days.
procedure: 1. Import a new HTTPS redirection import certificate. 2. Check whether the problem persists. If yes, go to Step 1. If no, go to Step 3. 3. End.
parameters: CertStartTime::Start time of the validity period of the imported certificate for HTTPS redirection. | CertFinishTime::End time of the validity period of the imported certificate for HTTPS redirection.

possible_causes: When users went offline, IPv6 DHCPv6-PD prefixes were reclaimed. The number of allocated IPv6 DHCPv6-PD prefixes in the domain fell below the configured threshold.
parameters: domainName::Domain name. | domainIndex::Domain index. | threshold::IPv6 address threshold in a domain, in percentage. For example, the value 80 indicates 80%.

description: The pre-allocation rate of the reserved PCP ports reached 100 percent for a RADIUS authentication user with Huawei proprietary attributes 162 and 163. (AddrGroupName=[AddrGroupName], InstanceType=[InstanceType], InstanceName=[InstanceName], Pre-PortNum=[Pre-PortNum], Slot=[Slot], CPU=[CPU]) PCP reserved ports were exhausted after were pre-allocated to RADIUS authentication users carrying Huawei proprietary attributes 162 and 163. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: When RADIUS authentication users carrying Huawei proprietary attributes 162 and 163 go online, the PCP reserved port pre-allocation usage reaches 100%. As a result, new users fail to go online.
possible_causes: The pre-allocation rate of the reserved PCP ports reached 100% in scenarios where a RADIUS authentication user with Huawei proprietary attributes 162 and 163 attempted to go online.
procedure: 1. Run the display nat address-usage by-session command to check whether the usage of PCP reserved ports reaches 100%. If the usage reaches 100%, go to Step 2. If the usage does not reach 100%, go to Step 3. 2. Determine whether to expand the capacity of PCP reserved ports based on the site requirements. If capacity expansion is required, run the port-reservation command in the instance view to expand the capacity. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If yes, no further action is required. If no, go to Step 3. If capacity expansion is not required, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: AddrGroupName::Name of an address pool. | InstanceType::Instance type. | InstanceName::Instance name. | Pre-PortNum::Number of pre-allocated ports. | Slot::Slot ID of a service board. | CPU::CPU ID of a service board.

impact_on_system: A large number of packets were retransmitted in the CUSP channel, which may affect the delivery of service messages in the CUSP channel.
possible_causes: A large number of retransmissions occurred in the CUSP channel message.

impact_on_system: There is no impact on the system.

description: The interfaces in this group worked in different transmission modes. (IfIndex=[IfIndex],SlotId=[SlotId],CardId=[CardId],PortId=[PortId],ReasonDescription=[ReasonDescription]) The interfaces of the same group did not work in the same transmission mode. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Traffic forwarding on the physical interfaces will be affected. Thus, a speedy solution is required.
possible_causes: Cause 1: Some interfaces in this group worked in LAN mode while some worked in WAN mode. Cause 2: Some interfaces in this group worked in GE mode while some worked in WAN mode.
procedure: Cause 1: Some interfaces in this group worked in LAN mode while some worked in WAN mode. 1.Run the set transfer-mode command to configure all the interfaces in this group to work in the same transmission mode. 2.Collect alarm information, log information and configuration information, and then contact technical support personnel. 3.End. Cause 2: Some interfaces in this group worked in GE mode while some worked in WAN mode. 1. Run the set transfer-mode command to configure the non-target interfaces in the group to work in LAN mode, and then switch to the GE or WAN mode related to the target port. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 3. End.
parameters: IfIndex::Index of physical port. | SlotId::Slot ID. | CardId::Card ID. | PortId::Port ID. | ReasonDescription::Reason Description.

description: IP addresses in a global public address pool were exhausted in N+1 warm backup+CGN warm backup scenarios. (PoolName=[PoolName], UsedIPNum=[UsedIPNum], ProfileName=[ProfileName], VirMac-vrid=[VirMac-vrid]) IP addresses in a global public address pool were exhausted in N+1 warm backup+CGN warm backup scenarios. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: No more public IP addresses can be assigned from the globally shared public address pool.
possible_causes: IP addresses in a global address pool were exhausted.
procedure: 1. Run the display nat ip-pool command to check whether the addresses in the global address pool are used up. If the global address pool is exhausted, go to Step 2. If the addresses in the global address pool are not exhausted, go to Step 3. 2. Check whether the channel between the vBRAS-UP and vBRAS-CP is normal. If no, restore the channel. If yes, check whether the number of networks of the DAP server on the CP is sufficient. Try to add networks. 3. Collect trap, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: PoolName::Name of a global address pool for N+1 warm backup. | UsedIPNum::Number of used IP addresses in the global public address pool for N+1 warm backup. | ProfileName::Name of an N+1 warm backup group. | VirMac-vrid::VRID of the virtual MAC address.

description: The IPv6 NDRA prefix usage of the domain [domainName] fell below the lower threshold. (Domain index = [domainIndex],MinThreshold=[threshold]) The IP address usage was above the lower threshold of the domain. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: If the fault persists, more users may be logged out unexpectedly.
possible_causes: Cause 1: A large number of users logged out. Cause 2: The configured lower limit was too high.
procedure: 1. Run the display domain < domain-name > command in the system view to check the value of IPv6-warning-threshold (Low) and determine whether the configured lower threshold for the IPv6 NDRA prefix usage is proper. If the configured lower threshold is too large, go to Step 2. If the configured lower threshold is proper, go to step 3. 2. Run the ipv6-warning-threshold lower-limit command in the AAA domain view to change the lower threshold for the IPv6 NDRA prefix usage. 3. Run the display domain < domain-name > command in the system view to check the IPv6 NDRA prefix usage. If the IPv6 NDRA prefix usage falls below or approaches the lower threshold, run the display aaa offline-record brief command to check whether the user offline reason is User request to offline. a. If yes, it is normal. b. If no, contact Huawei technical support. If the IPv6 NDRA prefix usage is not close to the configured lower threshold, go to Step 4.
parameters: domainName::Domain name. | domainIndex::Domain index. | threshold::Alarm threshold, in percentage. For example, the value 80 indicates 80%.

description: The number of pre-allocated NAT64 IP that are obtained from the public network address pool reaches the upper limit. (AddrGroupName=[AddrGroupName], InstanceType=[InstanceType], InstanceName=[InstanceName], Threshold=[Threshold], Pre-IPNum=[Pre-IPNum], Slot=[Slot], Cpu=[Cpu]) This alarm was generated when the usage of IP addresses in a no-PAT public address pool of a NAT64 instance in virtual cluster mode reached the threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: When the alarm is generated, services are not affected. When the number of users increases and the number of used IP addresses reaches the upper limit of the public address pool, the system cannot assign IP addresses in the address pool to new users.
possible_causes: In no-PAT scenarios, each user is assigned a single IP address from a public address pool. The user and IP address are in 1:1 mapping. When users increase, IP address usage of the public address pool in multic-chassis mode reached a specified threshold.
procedure: 1. Run the display this command in the NAT64 instance view to check whether the alarm threshold is too small. If the alarm threshold is too small, go to Step 2. If the alarm threshold is not too small, go to Step 3. 2. Run the nat64 alarm address-group port-number threshold threshold-value command to increase the alarm threshold, and then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 5. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Expand the address pool based on the live network configuration and check whether the alarm is cleared.
parameters: AddrGroupName::Name of an address pool. | InstanceType::Instance type. | InstanceName::Instance name. | Threshold::Threshold for the usage of IP addresses in a no-PAT public address pool. | Pre-IPNum::Number of used IP addresses. | Slot::Name of a service board in virtual cluster mode. | Cpu::CPU ID of a service board.

description: The pack ratio of the dictionary file used in the application exceeded the threshold. (Application=[ApplicationId], Dictionary=[DictionaryFileName], Threshold=[Threshold], PackRatio=[PackRatioValue], BenchmarkRatio=[BenchmarkRatioValue]) In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
