description: The usage of IPv4 sessions reached the threshold. (Usage = [Usage],Threshold = [Threshold],BoardName = [BoardName],Cpu = [Cpu]) In virtual cluster mode, the IPv4/IPv6 session usage configured on the processing engine of a service board exceeded the threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: When the alarm is just generated, services are not affected. If the number of entries in the sessions reaches the upper limit, user sessions fail to be created.
possible_causes: The proportion of configured IPv4/IPv6 sessions to the total supported ones on a service board's forwarding engine in virtual cluster mode reached a specified threshold.
procedure: 1. Run the display nat session table command to check whether the number of sessions reaches the maximum number of IPv4/IPv6 sessions. If the maximum number of IPv4/IPv6 sessions is reached, go to Step 2. If the number of IPv4/IPv6 sessions does not reach the maximum, go to Step 3. 2. Run the nat alarm session-number threshold command in the system view to set a larger alarm threshold. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: Usage::Usage of sessions. | Threshold::Threshold of the session usage. | BoardName::Name of a service board in virtual cluster mode. | Cpu::CPU ID of a service board.

description: The number of ipv6 address in the slot reached the lower limit of the device. (Slot=[slotId],hwAAASlotIpv6AddrThreshold=[threshold]) In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: There is no impact on the system.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The number of IPv6 addresses used for online users on the device fell below the lower threshold. Cause 2: The configured lower threshold increases, and the number of IPv6 addresses used for online users on the device fell below the lower threshold.

description: The license item of chassis [hwGtlChassisID] mismatched with the one of the main chassis. The license control item or serial number of the specified chassis is inconsistent with that of the active MPU of the master chassis.
impact_on_system: Services will not be affected.
possible_causes: The license item or serial number of the chassis mismatched with that of the main chassis.
procedure: 1. Apply for a license file that matches the active MPU of the master chassis. For details, see the License Usage Guide of the corresponding product. 2. Upload the license file to the device. 3. Run the license active <filename> command in the user view to activate the license file.
parameters: hwGtlChassisID::Description of the current chassis or board ID.

description: Symbol error alarm. (hwIfMonitorIndex=[hwIfMonitorIndex],hwIfMonitorSymbolErrorStatistics=[hwIfMonitorSymbolErrorStatistics],hwIfMonitorSymbolErrorThreshold=[hwIfMonitorSymbolErrorThreshold],hwIfMonitorSymbolErrorInterval=[hwIfMonitorSymbolErrorInterval],hwIfMonitorName=[hwIfMonitorName]) Symbol error alarm. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Packet loss occurs on an interface when the alarm is generated. As a result, services are affected.
possible_causes: For three consecutive detection time intervals, the number of symbol error messages has reached the specified high threshold value. You can configure the high threshold value, low threshold value, and detection time interval for symbol error alarms through the trap-threshold symbol-error high-threshold <high_threshold_val> low-threshold <low_threshold_val> interval-second <interval_val> command.
procedure: 1. Check the links (including optical fibers, optical modules, transmission devices, and jumper racks). Check whether there is a fault. If so, go to Step 2. If not, go to Step 3. 2. Replace the faulty component and ensure that the link is properly connected. Then check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If not, go to step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: hwIfMonitorIndex::Index of physical port. | hwIfMonitorSymbolErrorStatistics::Symbol error statistics value. | hwIfMonitorSymbolErrorThreshold::Symbol error alarm threshold. | hwIfMonitorSymbolErrorInterval::Specifies the interval for reporting the symbol error alarm, in seconds. | hwIfMonitorName::Name of physical port.

description: The number of BGP FlowSpec rules matching the start AS (Origin-AS) of the destination IPv6 address reaches the upper limit. The number of BGP FlowSpec rules matching the origin AS of the destination IPv6 address reached the upper limit.
impact_on_system: There is no impact on the system.
possible_causes: The number of BGP FlowSpec rules matching the start AS (Origin-AS) of the destination IPv6 address is 255.
procedure: 1. Delete the redundant BGP FlowSpec rule that matches the origin AS of the destination IPv6 address and check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 3. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect trap, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End.

description: The optical module configurations of the ports in this group are inconsistent. Currently, the optical module configuration takes effect based on port 0. (PortGroup=[PortGroup],ActivePortName=[ActivePortName],ActivePortIndex=[ActivePortIndex],ReasonDescription=[ReasonDescription]) The optical module configurations of the ports in the same group were inconsistent. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The optical module configurations take effect based on the configuration on port 0. If an optical module cannot be detected, the port configuration delivered through the corresponding command does not take effect.
possible_causes: One or more of the following configurations for the ports in this group are inconsistent: automatic laser shutdown, optical module's wavelength, frequency, channel number corresponding to the center wavelength, and optical module's optical power.
procedure: 1. Check whether the values configured using the laser autoshutdown enable, laser auto-shutdown-interval, wavelength-channel, and optical-tx-power target commands are the same. If so, go to Step 3. If not, go to Step 2. 2. Run the preceding commands again to ensure that the values are the same. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If so, go to Step 4. If not, go to Step 3. 3. Collect log and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: PortGroup::Port group | ActivePortName::Name of the active port | ActivePortIndex::Index of the active port | ReasonDescription::Possible cause

description: The imported HTTPS redirection certificate has been updated or deleted. (CertStartTime=[CertStartTime], CertFinishTime=[CertFinishTime]) In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: There is no impact on the system.
possible_causes: An imported HTTPS redirection certificate which is within the validity period has been imported, or the imported HTTPS redirection certificate has been deleted.
parameters: CertStartTime::Start time of the validity period of the imported certificate for HTTPS redirection. | CertFinishTime::End time of the validity period of the imported certificate for HTTPS redirection.

description: The ipv4 framed route usage exceeds the upper threshold. (ipv4FramedRouteUsage=[ipv4FramedRouteUsage]) The IPv4 framed route usage on the device exceeded the upper threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Services will not be affected.
possible_causes: The number of IPv4 routes generated based on the RADIUS-delivered Framed-Route attribute exceeded 90% of the specification.
procedure: 1. Re-plan the networking so that the number of IPv4 framed routes on the device falls below 80% of the upper limit. Then, check whether the alarm is cleared. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 3. If the alarm persists, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel. 3. End.
parameters: ipv4FramedRouteUsage::IPv4 framed route usage

description: User tables ran out. (UserTableNum=[UserTableNum],BoardName=[BoardName], Cpu=[Cpu]) CGN user tables were exhausted in virtual cluster mode. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The number of user tables was exhausted, and new users cannot be added.
possible_causes: The number of used user tables in virtual cluster mode reached the upper limit.
procedure: 1. Run the display nat user-information command to check whether the number of CGN connections reaches the maximum number of user tables supported by the system. If the maximum number of licenses is reached, purchase more licenses to support more user tables. If the maximum number of licenses is not reached, go to Step 2. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: UserTableNum::Number of user tables. | BoardName::Name of a service board in virtual cluster mode. | Cpu::CPU ID of a service board.

description: The interfaces in this group worked in different split types. (IfIndex=[IfIndex],ChassisId=[ChassisId],SlotId=[SlotId],CardId=[CardId],PortId=[PortId]) The interfaces in a group worked in different split types. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Traffic on the physical interface is affected. The problem must be resolved immediately.
possible_causes: The interfaces in this group worked in different split types.
procedure: 1. Configure all interfaces in the group that report the alarm to work in the same hash mode. 2. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support. 3. End.
parameters: IfIndex::Index of a physical interface. | ChassisId::Chassis ID. | SlotId::Slot ID. | CardId::Card number. | PortId::Interface number.

description: The public network tunnel used to carry the VPLS PW or EVPN is not a LDP over GRE tunnel. (VsiName=[hwVplsOverLdpOverGreVsiName], RemoteIp=[hwPeerRemoteIp], PwId=[hwVplsOverLdpOverGrePwId], EvpnName=[hwEvpnOverLdpOverGreEvpnName]) In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: There is no impact on the system.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The VPLS PW or EVPN whose signaling protocol status is Up is no longer carried over an LDP over GRE tunnel. Cause 2: The signaling protocol status of the VPLS PW or EVPN carried over an LDP over GRE tunnel changes to Down. Cause 3: The VPLS PW or EVPN whose signaling protocol status is Up and which is carried over an LDP over GRE tunnel is deleted.
parameters: hwVplsOverLdpOverGreVsiName::VSI name. | hwPeerRemoteIp::Remote IP address. | hwVplsOverLdpOverGrePwId::PW ID. | hwEvpnOverLdpOverGreEvpnName::EVPN name.

description: The IP address usage of the domain [domainName] reached the upper threshold. (Domain index = [domainIndex],Threshold=[threshold]) The number of IP addresses used by users in the domain reached the upper threshold for the total number of IP addresses in the local address pool. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: If the problem persists, addresses in the address pool bound to the domain may be exhausted. As a result, new users cannot go online because they cannot be assigned IP addresses.
possible_causes: The number of IP addresses used by the users in the domain reached the upper threshold.
procedure: 1. Run the display domain domain-name command in any view to check the ip-warning-threshold value configured in the domain. If the value of ip-warning-threshold configured in the domain ranges from 1 to 100, go to Step 2. If ip-warning-threshold is not configured or set to 100 in the domain view, go to Step 4. 2. Check whether the number of online users using IP addresses in the local address pool in the domain reaches the maximum value. If yes, go to Step 5. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Apply the local address pool to the domain or plan new users to go online from another domain. Wait for 30 minutes and check whether the alarm is cleared.
parameters: domainName::Domain name. | domainIndex::Domain index. | threshold::Threshold for the total number of IP addresses in the local address pool of a domain.

description: The corresponding license resources became sufficient and the CGN function license on the board has been activated, or the configuration for activating the CGN function license on the board was deleted. (ItemName=[LicenseItemName], ItemDescription=[LicenseDescription], Slot=[Slot])
impact_on_system: Services are not affected.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The corresponding license resources became sufficient and the CGN function license on the board had been activated. Cause 2: The configuration for activating the CGN function license on the board was deleted.
parameters: LicenseItemName::License control item name. | LicenseDescription::License control item description. | Slot::Slot ID of a service board.

description: The IP address usage of the vpn reached the threshold. (VPNInstance=[VPNName],Threshold=[threshold]) The address usage of the address pools bound to the VPN instance exceeded the threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: Services are not affected. However, if the number of IP addresses continues to increase, IP addresses in the VPN instance will be exhausted, and users cannot go online.

description: Configurations on the active and standby devices were inconsistent in a dual-device hot backup scenario. The configurations on the active and standby devices were inconsistent in a dual-device hot backup scenario. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The dual-device hot backup function is affected.
possible_causes: Configurations on the active and standby devices were inconsistent in a dual-device hot backup scenario.
procedure: 1. Run the display rui config-check-info command in the diagnostic view to check the configuration check result on the active and standby devices in the dual-device hot backup mode. 2. Based on the display rui config-check-info command output, change the configurations on the active and standby devices to be the same. The modification methods are as follows: RBP: Find the corresponding remote backup profile on the active and standby devices based on the displayed remote backup profile name and backup ID, and modify the configurations to be the same. RBS: Change the remote backup service configurations on the active and standby devices to be the same based on the displayed remote backup service name. RBP_VLAN: Based on the sub-interface name, find the remote backup profile bound to the sub-interface. On the peer device, find the sub-interface that is bound to the same remote backup profile and corresponds to this sub-interface, change the user VLANs of the sub-interfaces on the active and standby devices to be the same. RBP_V4_POOL: Find the remote backup profile bound to the address pool based on the IPv4 address pool name displayed in the command output and modify the IPv4 address pool configurations in the remote backup profile on the active and standby devices to be the same. RBS_V4_POOL: Find the remote backup service bound to the address pool based on the IPv4 address pool name displayed in the command output and modify the IPv4 address pool configurations in the remote backup service on the active and standby devices to be the same. RBP_V6_POOL: Find the remote backup profile bound to the address pool based on the IPv6 address pool name displayed in the command output and modify the IPv6 address pool configurations in the remote backup profile and the prefix pool configurations bound to the address pool on the active and standby devices to be the same. RBS_V6_POOL: Find the remote backup service bound to the IPv6 address pool based on the IPv6 address pool name displayed in the command output and modify the IPv6 address pool configurations in the remote backup service and the prefix pool configurations bound to the address pool on the active and standby devices to be the same. 3. After the active/standby configuration is modified to be consistent, run the set rui config-check start command in the diagnostic view of the peer device and wait for 10 minutes. Then run the set rui config-check start command in the diagnostic view of the local device and wait for 10 minutes, check whether the alarm is cleared at the local device. If yes, go to Step 5. If no, go to Step 4.

If the alarm threshold is far less than 80%, go to Step 2. If the alarm threshold is not far less than 80%, go to Step 3. 2. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 5. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Expand the address pool based on the live network configuration and check whether the alarm is cleared.

If the tunnel is not an LDP over GRE tunnel, go to Step 2. 2. Run the tunnel-policy command to access the PW tunnel policy view and run the tunnel select-seq or tunnel binding command to change the public network tunnel to a non-LDP over GRE tunnel. If the alarm is cleared, go to Step 4. If the alarm persists, go to Step 3. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.

description: The usage of MF classification rules exceeded the pre-warning threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.

After upstream MF classification is configured and IPv4 rules are applied, the number of TCAM resources has exceeded the upper limit, which does not affect service use. However, if MF classification services continue to be configured and the number of services reaches the upper limit, the newly configured rules do not take effect. Cause 2: The number of IPv4 TCAM indexes for downstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification(The uplink and downlink share resources, and pre-alarms may be generated in both directions). After downstream MF classification is configured and IPv4 rules are applied, the number of TCAM resources has exceeded the upper limit, which does not affect service use. However, if downstream MF classification services continue to be configured and the number of services reaches the upper limit, the newly configured rules do not take effect. Cause 3: The number of IPv6 TCAM indexes for upstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification(The uplink and downlink share resources, and pre-alarms may be generated in both directions). After upstream MF classification is configured and IPv6 rules are applied, the number of TCAM resources has exceeded the upper limit, which does not affect service use. However, if MF classification services continue to be configured and the number of services reaches the upper limit, the newly configured rules do not take effect. Cause 4: The number of IPv6 TCAM indexes for downstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification(The uplink and downlink share resources, and pre-alarms may be generated in both directions). After downstream MF classification is configured and IPv6 rules are applied, the number of TCAM resources has exceeded the upper limit, which does not affect service use. However, if downstream MF classification services continue to be configured and the number of services reaches the upper limit, the newly configured rules do not take effect. Cause 5: The number of IPv4 UCL TCAM indexes for upstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification. After upstream MF classification is configured and IPv4 UCL rules are applied, the number of UCL TCAM resources has exceeded the upper limit, which does not affect service use. However, if MF classification services continue to be configured and the number of services reaches the upper limit, the newly configured rules do not take effect. Cause 6: The number of IPv4 UCL TCAM indexes for downstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification. After downstream MF classification is configured and IPv4 UCL rules are applied, the number of UCL TCAM resources has exceeded the upper limit, which does not affect service use. However, if MF classification services continue to be configured and the number of services reaches the upper limit, the newly configured rules do not take effect. Cause 7: The number of IPv6 UCL TCAM indexes for upstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification. After upstream MF classification is configured and IPv6 UCL rules are applied, the number of UCL TCAM resources has exceeded the upper limit, which does not affect service use. However, if MF classification services continue to be configured and the number of services reaches the upper limit, the newly configured rules do not take effect. Cause 8: The number of IPv6 UCL TCAM indexes for downstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification. After downstream MF classification is configured and IPv6 UCL rules are applied, the number of UCL TCAM resources has exceeded the upper limit, which does not affect service use. However, if MF classification services continue to be configured and the number of services reaches the upper limit, the newly configured rules do not take effect.
possible_causes: Cause 1: The number of IPv4 TCAM indexes for upstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification(The uplink and downlink share resources, and pre-alarms may be generated in both directions). Cause 2: The number of IPv4 TCAM indexes for downstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification(The uplink and downlink share resources, and pre-alarms may be generated in both directions). Cause 3: The number of IPv6 TCAM indexes for upstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification(The uplink and downlink share resources, and pre-alarms may be generated in both directions). Cause 4: The number of IPv6 TCAM indexes for downstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification(The uplink and downlink share resources, and pre-alarms may be generated in both directions). Cause 5: The number of IPv4 UCL TCAM indexes for upstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification. Cause 6: The number of IPv4 UCL TCAM indexes for downstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification. Cause 7: The number of IPv6 UCL TCAM indexes for upstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification. Cause 8: The number of IPv6 UCL TCAM indexes for downstream traffic exceeded the threshold of forwarding engine resource specification.
procedure: 1. Check whether the pre-alarm threshold is proper based on the service volume on the live network. If yes, go to Step 2. If no, go to Step 3. 2. Check the device configuration, delete unnecessary traffic policy rule configurations, and go to Step 4. 3. Run the traffic-policy rule-resource pre-alarm-threshold <alarm-threshold-value> command in the system view to adjust the pre-alarm threshold for the traffic policy rule usage. 4. Check whether the alarm is cleared.

description: If the engine does not exist or the engine does not support the data processing service, the data processing services associated with the engine do not take effect. (SlotID=[SlotId], EngineID=[EngineId]) The CPU cannot be detected after the service board for scale-in is replaced. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: The CPU configured with data redundancy elimination does not exist on the board after scale-in. As a result, the data redundancy elimination service becomes invalid.
possible_causes: The service board is replaced with the board to be scaled in. The CPU for which the data processing service has been configured is not on the board to be scaled in.
procedure: 1. Delete the data redundancy service configuration from the CPU for which the alarm is generated. If the fault persists, go to Step 2. If the fault is rectified, go to Step 4. 2. Remove the board where the CPU reporting the alarm is located. If the fault persists, go to Step 3. If the fault is rectified, go to Step 4. 3. Collect alarm, log, and configuration information, and contact technical support personnel.
parameters: SlotId::Indicates the board ID. | EngineId::Indicates the CPU ID.

description: The IPv6 NDRA prefix usage of the domain [domainName] reached the upper threshold. (Domain index = [domainIndex],Threshold=[threshold]) The usage of IPv6 NDRA prefixes in the domain reached the upper threshold. In VS mode, this trap is supported only by the admin VS.
impact_on_system: If the problem persists, NDRA prefixes in the address pools bound to the domain may be exhausted. As a result, new users cannot go online because they cannot be assigned NDRA prefixes.
possible_causes: A large number of users got online from the domain, causing the number of IPv6 prefixes allocated using NDRA to reach the threshold.
procedure: 1. Run the display domain domain-name command to check the IPv6 address usage alarm threshold (IPv6-warning-threshold) configured in the domain. If the value of IPv6-warning-threshold ranges from 1 to 100, go to Step 2. If IPv6-warning-threshold is not configured or is set to 100 in the domain, go to Step 4. 2. Run the display ipv6-pool pool-usage command to check whether the number of online users with IPv6 prefixes assigned in NDRA mode in the domain has reached the maximum value. If yes, go to Step 5. If no, go to Step 3. 3. Run the ipv6-pool command in the domain view to reference a delegation address pool or run the access-type command in the BAS interface view to configure new users to go online from another domain. Wait for 30 minutes and check whether the alarm persists.
parameters: domainName::Domain name. | domainIndex::Domain index. | threshold::IPv6 address threshold in a domain, in percentage. For example, the value 80 indicates 80%.
